sentences.zh: 五禮之別，二曰凶。

translations.literal: Among the divisions of the Five Rites, the second is called "inauspicious" (rites of misfortune and mourning).
translations.idiomatic: The Five Rites fall into categories; the second covers mourning and calamity.

sentences.zh: 自天子至於庶人，身體髮膚，受之父母，其理既均，其情亦等，生則養，死則哀，故曰三年之喪，天下之達禮者也。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, body, hair, and skin are received from father and mother; the principle is equally binding and the affection equally owed—in life one nurtures them, in death one grieves them—therefore it is said that three years' mourning is the universally acknowledged rite under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and commoner alike owe their bodies—and every hair on them—to their parents; the duty is universal and the feeling the same: we support them while they live and mourn them when they die. That is why three years of mourning has always been treated as the normative observance for the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 漢禮，天子崩，自不豫至於登遐及葬，喪紀之制，與夫三代變易。

translations.literal: In Han ritual, when the Son of Heaven died, from indisposition through passing away ("ascending to the remote") down to burial, the system of mourning observances differed from that of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Han regulations for an emperor's death—from his last illness through his demise and interment—set mourning procedures that had moved away from Xia, Shang, and Zhou precedent.

sentences.zh: 魏晉以來，大體同漢。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, in the main it was the same as Han.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei and Jin, the overall framework largely continued Han practice.

sentences.zh: 然自漢文革喪禮之制，後代遵之，無復三年之禮。

translations.literal: Yet from Emperor Wen of Han's reform of the mourning-rite system, later generations observed it and there was no longer the rite of three years.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Han pared back full mourning, succeeding ages kept to his model, and the classical three-year observance effectively vanished from practice.

sentences.zh: 及魏武臨終，遺令「天下尚未安定，未得遵古。

translations.literal: When Wei Wu was near death, he left instructions: "The realm is not yet pacified; one cannot follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: As he faced death, Cao Cao—later canonized as Emperor Wu of Wei—instructed his heirs that while the empire remained unsettled, they must not revert to ancient mourning usages.

sentences.zh: 百官當臨中者，十五舉音，葬畢便除。

translations.literal: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central [mourning site], fifteen utterances of sound; when burial is finished then remove [mourning dress].
translations.idiomatic: Officials obliged to join the central lament were to voice grief fifteen times; formal mourning ended as soon as the burial was over.

sentences.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，不得離部。

translations.literal: Those who command troops or garrison and defend may not leave their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Generals in the field and troops on garrison duty were forbidden to abandon their posts.

sentences.zh: 」魏武以正月庚子崩，辛丑即殯，是月丁卯葬，是為不逾月也。

translations.literal: " Wei Wu died on gengzi of the first month; on xinchou the laying-in-repose was carried out; on dingmao of that month he was buried—this is called not exceeding the month.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu of Wei died on the gengzi day of the first month; his coffining followed on xinchou, and he was buried on dingmao that same month—his funeral was thus completed within one lunar month.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝、景帝之崩，並從權制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan and Emperor Jing died, both likewise followed expedient regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The deaths of Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi) and Emperor Jing (Sima Shi) were handled under the same shortened, expedient mourning rules.

sentences.zh: 文帝之崩，國內服三日。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, within the state mourning dress was worn three days.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Wen's passing the realm wore mourning garb for only three days.

sentences.zh: 武帝亦遵漢魏之典，既葬除喪，然猶深衣素冠，降席撤膳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also followed the statutes of Han and Wei; once buried mourning was removed, yet still he wore deep garments and plain cap, lowered the mat and withdrew fine foods.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu adhered to the Han–Wei rule ending formal mourning at burial, yet he continued to dress plainly in deep robes and an unbleached cap, lowered his seat, and ate simple fare.

sentences.zh: 太宰司馬孚、太傅鄭沖、太保王祥、太尉何曾、司徒領中領軍司馬望、司空荀顗、車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔、都護大將軍郭建、侍中郭綏、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜等奏曰：「臣聞禮典軌度，豐殺隨時，虞夏商周，咸不相襲，蓋有由也。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Fu, Grand Mentor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Minister of War He Zeng, Minister of Education concurrently Commander of the Palace Guards Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu, Deputy Director Wu Yan, Defender-in-Chief Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Supervisor of the Secretariat Xun Xu, General of the Central Army Yang Hu, and others memorialized: "We have heard that in ritual canons and norms, fullness or reduction follows the times; Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou did not blindly imitate one another—there were reasons for this.
translations.idiomatic: Leading ministers—including Sima Fu, Zheng Chong, Wang Xiang, He Zeng, Sima Wang, Xun Yi, Jia Chong, Pei Xiu, and others—submitted a joint memorial: "Rites expand or contract with circumstance; the legendary sage-kings of antiquity never copied one another blindly, and they had good cause.

sentences.zh: 大晉紹承漢魏，有革有因，期於足以興化而已，故未得皆返太素，同規上古也。

translations.literal: Great Jin inherits Han and Wei; there is reform and continuation; the expectation is only that it suffice to promote transformation—therefore it could not all return to utmost simplicity and match high antiquity in one norm.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty builds on Han and Wei; some usages change and some carry forward, aiming only at what will civilize the age—it cannot simply unwind everything to primal austerity or mirror remote antiquity in every detail.

sentences.zh: 陛下既以俯遵漢魏降喪之典，以濟時務，而躬蹈大孝，情過乎哀，素冠深衣，降席撤膳，雖武丁行之于殷世，曾閔履之於布衣，未足以逾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already condescended to follow Han–Wei statutes that shorten mourning in order to meet pressing affairs of the time, yet personally practices great filial piety; the feeling exceeds grief—plain cap and deep garments, lowered mat and withdrawn fine foods—even were it Wu Ding acting thus in the Yin age, or Zengzi and Min Sun practicing it as commoners, it would not suffice to surpass.
translations.idiomatic: You have accepted the shortened mourning appropriate to Han and Wei exigencies, yet you still embody the utmost filial devotion—plain cap, simple robes, lowered seating, frugal meals—with a grief deeper than ritual prescribes. Not even King Wu Ding of Shang or paragons like Zengzi and Min Sun among commoners could have surpassed this.

sentences.zh: 方今荊蠻未夷，庶政未乂，萬機事殷，動勞神慮，豈遑全遂聖旨，以從至情。

translations.literal: Now the Jing-Man are not yet pacified, the myriad policies are not yet ordered, the myriad affairs are pressing and constantly weary Your Majesty's mind—how could there be leisure fully to realize sagely intentions so as to follow utmost feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Southern rebels remain unrestored, government is not yet fully ordered, and the burden of state exhausts you daily; you cannot possibly indulge every dictate of private grief at the cost of public duty.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為陛下宜割情以康時濟俗，輒敕御府易服，內省改坐，太官復膳，諸所施行，皆如舊制。

translations.literal: We consider that Your Majesty ought to cut feeling so as to bring peace to the age and aid custom; we venture to order the imperial wardrobe to change garments, the inner quarters to alter seating, the grand provisioner to restore meals—all measures implemented according to old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: We urge you to rein in personal sorrow for the sake of stabilizing the times and the people: change out of mourning dress, resume normal seating in the palace, and restore regular meals—everything should return to established court practice.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「每感念幽冥，而不得終苴絰於草土，以存此痛，況當食稻衣錦，誠詭然激切其心，非所以相解也。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Whenever I think on the dark realm below and cannot finish twisted hemp on straw and earth to preserve this pain, how much more if I should eat polished rice and wear brocade—it truly twists and cuts the heart; it is not the means by which to relieve one another.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "Whenever I think of my father in the grave and cannot wear full mourning straw and hemp to the end, the wound stays raw. To sit down to fine rice and silk would tear at me inside; that would not ease my grief at all.

sentences.zh: 吾本諸生家，傳禮來久，何心一旦便易此情於所天！

translations.literal: I am originally from a scholar family; transmission of ritual has been long—what heart could in one morning change this feeling toward him who is my Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: I was raised in a literati household steeped in the classics; how could I overnight blunt the love I owe the father who gave me life?

sentences.zh: 相從已多，可試省孔子答宰我之言，無事紛紜也。

translations.literal: You have followed long enough; you may try reviewing Confucius's reply to Zai Wo—there is no need for confused clamor.
translations.idiomatic: You have pressed your case at length. Reread what Confucius said to Zai Wo about mourning; there is no call for further wrangling.

sentences.zh: 言及悲剝，柰何！

translations.literal: Speaking reaches grief cutting—what to do!
translations.idiomatic: Even to speak of it tears me apart—what can I do?

sentences.zh: 柰何！

translations.literal: What to do!
translations.idiomatic: What am I to do?

sentences.zh: 」孚等重奏：「伏讀聖詔，感以悲懷，輒思仲尼所以抑宰我之問，聖思所以不能已已，甚深甚篤。

translations.literal: " Fu and others submitted again: "We bow and read the sagely edict; moved with sorrowful feeling, we recall why Confucius restrained Zai Wo's question; the sagely thoughts therefore cannot cease—very deep, very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Fu's party answered again: "Your words move us to tears. We recall how Confucius checked Zai Wo's impatience with mourning; your own sorrow runs just as deep and will not be argued away.

sentences.zh: 然今者干戈未戢，武事未偃，萬機至重，天下至眾。

translations.literal: Yet now shields and spears are not yet stored away, military affairs are not yet laid down; the myriad threads are supremely weighty, all under Heaven is supremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet arms have not been laid away, military burdens persist, and the affairs of state—together with the countless people who depend on you—remain overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 陛下以萬乘之尊，履布衣之禮，服粗席稿，水飲疏食，殷憂內盈，毀悴外表。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with the honor of ten thousand chariots, treads the rites of common cloth; wearing coarse [garments], mat of straw, drinking water, eating coarse food, deep grief fills within, emaciation and haggardness show without.
translations.idiomatic: You rule a great empire yet live like a common mourner—coarse cloth, straw bedding, water and plain grain—while grief consumes you within and gaunt sorrow shows on your face.

sentences.zh: 而躬勤萬機，坐而待旦，降心接下，仄不遑食，所以勞力者如斯之甚。

translations.literal: Yet personally toiling at myriad threads, sitting awaiting dawn, lowering mind to receive inferiors, leaning [over tablets] without leisure to eat—the labor expended is thus so extreme.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time you grind through every memorial before dawn, humble yourself before officials, and skip meals bent over documents—the strain could hardly be greater.

sentences.zh: 是以臣等悚息不寧，誠懼神氣用損，以疚大事。

translations.literal: Therefore we tremble and breathe uneasy; we truly fear spirit and breath will suffer harm and thereby injure great matters.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot rest for fear this regimen will sap your strength and endanger the dynasty itself.

sentences.zh: 輒敕有司，改坐復常，率由舊典。

translations.literal: We venture to order the relevant offices to change seating and restore normality, uniformly following old canons.
translations.idiomatic: We have instructed the proper bureaus to restore normal seating and routine, all according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察納愚款，以慰皇太后之心。

translations.literal: We only hope Your Majesty will examine and accept our foolish sincerity, so as to console the heart of the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to heed this blunt plea and give your mother the Empress Dowager some peace of mind.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「重覽奏議，益以悲剝，不能自勝，柰何！

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "Again reviewing the memorials and discussions, I increase in grief cutting; I cannot overcome myself—what to do!
translations.idiomatic: " Another rescript ran: "Reading your petitions again only sharpens my grief; I cannot master myself—what can I do?

sentences.zh: 柰何！

translations.literal: What to do!
translations.idiomatic: What can I do?

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，自古達禮，誠聖人稱情立衷，明恕而行也。

translations.literal: Three years' mourning, from antiquity the universally acknowledged rite—it is truly that sages matched feeling and established inner substance, practicing with enlightened forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Three years' mourning is the universal standard the sages framed to align outward rites with inward feeling and humane restraint.

sentences.zh: 神靈日遠，無所訴告，雖薄於情，食旨服美，所不堪也。

translations.literal: Spirits daily grow more distant; there is nowhere to declare and tell; although slight toward feeling, to eat delicacies and wear fine garments is what one cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: My father's spirit withdraws farther each day, and I have nowhere to pour out my heart; even if ritual seems to demand less, fine food and rich clothes are unbearable to me.

sentences.zh: 不宜反覆，重傷其心，言用斷絕，柰何！

translations.literal: It is not fitting to go back and forth, doubly injuring his heart; words use cutting off—what to do!
translations.idiomatic: Do not press me again and wound his shade anew—I am speechless with grief—what can I do?

sentences.zh: 柰何！

translations.literal: What to do!
translations.idiomatic: What can I do?

sentences.zh: 」帝遂以此禮終三年。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon with this rite completed three years.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he observed full three-year mourning on these terms.

sentences.zh: 後居太后之喪亦如之。

translations.literal: Later in observing the Empress Dowager's mourning it was also thus.
translations.idiomatic: When he later mourned the Empress Dowager, he followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔曰：「此上旬，先帝棄天下日也，便以周年。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict said: "This early decade is the day the late emperor abandoned all under Heaven; thereby it completes one cycle year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict declared: "These opening days mark the anniversary of my father's death—the first full year has turned.

sentences.zh: 吾煢煢，當復何時一得敘人子之情邪！

translations.literal: I am solitary and alone—when again shall I once obtain to express the feelings of a person's son!
translations.idiomatic: I stand utterly alone; when will I ever satisfy the heart of a son toward his father?

sentences.zh: 思慕煩毒，欲詔陵瞻侍，以盡哀憤。

translations.literal: Longing and admiring are vexing poison; I desire to order the mausoleum for viewing attendance, so as to exhaust sorrowful grief.
translations.idiomatic: My longing burns like poison; I wish to visit his tomb with attendants and pour out every ounce of grief.

sentences.zh: 主者具行備。

translations.literal: Let those in charge fully prepare the traveling equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices make ready for the journey.

sentences.zh: 」太宰安平王孚、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔等奏：「陛下至孝蒸蒸，哀思罔極。

translations.literal: " Grand Tutor the Prince of Anping, Wang Fu, Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu, Deputy Director Wu Yan, and others memorialized: "Your Majesty's utmost filial piety steams upward; sorrowful thoughts know no limit.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Fu, Pei Xiu, Wu Yan, and others replied: "Your filial devotion knows no bounds and your grief is bottomless.

sentences.zh: 衰麻雖除，哀毀疏食，有損神和。

translations.literal: Although hemp mourning is removed, grief-wreck and coarse eating harm spirit harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Though formal sackcloth is laid aside, fasting and sorrow still sap your health.

sentences.zh: 今雖秋節，尚有餘暑，謁見山陵，悲感摧傷，群下竊用竦息，以為宜降抑聖情，以慰萬國。

translations.literal: Now although it is autumn season, there is still leftover heat; paying respects at the hills-and-mounds tomb, grief and feeling crush and wound—your servants secretly draw breath in awe and consider it fitting to lower and restrain sagely feeling so as to console the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn has begun but heat lingers; a pilgrimage to the imperial tombs would wring you with grief. Your ministers tremble for your welfare and urge you to curb this sorrow for the sake of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「孤煢忽爾，日月已周，痛慕摧感，永無逮及。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "I, orphan, solitary, suddenly thus—the sun and moon have completed a cycle; pain and longing crush feeling—forever there is no catching up.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered: "I am left alone; a year has flown by while longing tears at me—nothing can bring him back.

sentences.zh: 欲瞻奉山陵，以敘哀憤，體氣自佳耳。

translations.literal: I desire to gaze upon and attend the hills-and-mounds tomb so as to narrate sorrowful grief; body and breath are themselves fine.
translations.idiomatic: I only want to stand before his mound and voice my grief; my body is strong enough.

sentences.zh: 又已涼，便當行，不得如所奏也。

translations.literal: Moreover it is already cool; then ought to go—I cannot be as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The weather has cooled; I am going, and I cannot accept your advice.

sentences.zh: 主者便具行備。

translations.literal: Let those in charge then fully prepare the traveling equipage.
translations.idiomatic: See that everything needed for the journey is prepared at once.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「漢文不使天下盡哀，亦帝王至謙之志。

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "Emperor Wen of Han did not cause all under Heaven fully to grieve—this too was the utmost modest intent of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: " A further rescript noted: "Emperor Wen of Han refused to impose universal mourning—that too reflected an emperor's humility.

sentences.zh: 當見山陵，何心而無服，其以衰絰行。

translations.literal: When about to see the hills-and-mounds tomb, what heart to be without garments—thereby wear frayed hemp strips in proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: Facing my father's tomb, how could I go without mourning dress? I shall wear sackcloth and hemp cord.

sentences.zh: 」孚等重奏曰：「臣聞上古喪期無數，後世乃有年月之漸。

translations.literal: " Fu and others submitted again: "We have heard that in high antiquity mourning periods had no fixed number; later ages then had the gradual appearance of years and months.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Fu's group pressed again: "Antiquity fixed no uniform mourning span; only later did successive reigns reckon it in years and months.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝隨時之義，制為短喪，傳之於後。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han, with the meaning of following the times, regulated it as short mourning and transmitted it to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han shortened mourning to suit his age, and posterity has kept that precedent.

sentences.zh: 陛下以社稷宗廟之重，萬方億兆之故，既從權制，釋除衰麻，群臣百姓吉服，今者謁陵，以敘哀慕，若加衰絰，進退無當。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because of the weight of altars of soil and grain and ancestral temples, and the reasons of the myriad regions and hundred millions, having already followed expedient regulation and released and removed hemp mourning, the hundred officials and hundred surnames are in auspicious dress; now in paying respects at the tomb so as to narrate sorrowful longing, if adding frayed hemp strips, advance and retreat lack propriety.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of state and ancestral cult you already ended formal mourning; officials and commoners alike wear bright clothes. To resume sackcloth for this tomb visit would leave neither court protocol nor popular expectation with a clear rule.

sentences.zh: 不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: We dare not receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot obey this order.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「亦知不在此麻布耳。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Also know it is not in this hemp cloth alone.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "I know the issue is not really the hemp.

sentences.zh: 然人子情思，為欲令哀喪之物在身，蓋近情也。

translations.literal: Yet a person's child's feelings and thoughts—desiring to cause mourning objects on the person—generally nears feeling.
translations.idiomatic: As a son I simply want the outward tokens of grief on my body; that is the natural impulse.

sentences.zh: 群臣自當案舊制。

translations.literal: The hundred officials naturally ought to examine old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministers adhere to the standing rules for themselves.

sentences.zh: 」孚等又奏曰：「臣聞聖人制作，必從時宜。

translations.literal: " Fu and others again memorialized: "We have heard that when sages establish institutions, they necessarily follow what fits the times.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered again: "The sages framed ritual to fit their times.

sentences.zh: 故五帝殊樂，三王異禮，此古今所以不同，質文所以迭用也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Five Thearchs had different music, the Three Kings had different rites—this is why ancient and modern are not the same, why substance and pattern alternate in use.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Five Thearchs did not share one music, nor did the Three Kings share one court ritual—substance and refinement succeed one another because circumstances change.

sentences.zh: 陛下隨時之宜，既降心克己，俯就權制，既除衰麻，而行心喪之禮，今復制服，義無所依。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, following what fits the times, having already lowered mind and restrained self, condescended to expedient regulation; having already removed hemp mourning and practicing the rite of mourning in the heart—now again putting on garments, in principle there is nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: You already humbled yourself to accept shortened mourning in form while keeping grief in your heart; to don sackcloth again would have no grounding in principle.

sentences.zh: 若君服而臣不服，亦未之敢安也。

translations.literal: If the lord wears [mourning] but ministers do not wear, likewise we dare not be at ease in this.
translations.idiomatic: If you mourn visibly while we do not, we could hardly feel right about it.

sentences.zh: 參議宜如前奏。

translations.literal: After consulting, it is fitting as in the prior memorial.
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation we reaffirm our earlier recommendation.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「患情不能跂及耳，衣服何在。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "The trouble is feeling cannot stand on tiptoe and reach—where are garments?
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "My grief cannot reach him whether I dress up or down—what do clothes matter?

sentences.zh: 諸君勤勤之至，豈苟相違。」

translations.literal: Lords, your diligent earnestness reaches utmost—how could I lightly oppose one another."
translations.idiomatic: You press me from earnest care, not from sheer stubbornness."

sentences.zh: ，皇太后崩。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「前代故事，倚廬中施白縑帳、蓐、素床，以布巾裹塊草，軺輦、版輿、細犢車皆施縑裏。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "According to precedents of former dynasties, in the lean-to mourning hut hang white thin-silk curtains, rush mat, plain bed; with cloth towel wrap clod grass; light carriage, plank litter, and fine calf cart all have thin silk lining.
translations.idiomatic: Officials cited precedent: the mourning shelter should use white silk curtains, a rush mat, and an undecorated bed; the burial clod was wrapped in cloth; escort wagons and sedan chairs were lined with silk.

sentences.zh: 」詔不聽，但令以布衣車而已，其餘居喪之制，不改禮文。

translations.literal: " The edict did not heed; only ordered plain cloth carts—that was all; the rest of regulations for dwelling in mourning did not alter ritual text.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused, permitting only plain hemp-draped carts while leaving every other mourning regulation as written.

sentences.zh: 有司又奏：「大行皇太后當以四月二十五日安厝。

translations.literal: The relevant offices again memorialized: "The late Empress Dowager ought on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month to be settled in burial.
translations.idiomatic: They further reported that the late Empress Dowager was to be interred on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 故事，虞著衰服，既虞而除。

translations.literal: According to precedent, at the Yu rite one wears frayed garments; once Yu is finished then remove.
translations.idiomatic: By custom mourners wore sackcloth for the Yu offering at the tomb site and laid it aside once that service ended.

sentences.zh: 其內外官僚皆就朝晡臨位，御除服訖，各還所次除衰服。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials all proceed to morning and late-afternoon wailing stations; when the sovereign finishes removing garments, each returns to his station and removes frayed garments.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside officials were to take their turns at dawn and dusk lamentation; after you ended mourning at court they would return to their posts and strip off sackcloth.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「夫三年之喪，天下之達禮也。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Now three years' mourning is the universally acknowledged rite under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "Three years' mourning is the acknowledged standard for the realm.

sentences.zh: 受終身之愛，而無數年之報，柰何葬而便即吉，情所不忍也。

translations.literal: Receiving lifelong love, yet without several years' repayment—how can burial then immediately reach auspicious—feeling cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: She cherished me all my life; am I to repay her with no real mourning? To shift to auspicious dress the moment she is buried is more than I can endure.

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏：「世有險易，道有洿隆，所遇之時異，誠有由然，非忽禮也。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices again memorialized: "Ages have peril and ease; the Way has low and high; the times encountered differ—indeed there is reason thus; it is not treating ritual lightly.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered: "Times differ—some turbulent, some calm—and the Way rises or falls with them; adapting ritual is not contempt for ritual.

sentences.zh: 方今戎馬未散，王事至殷，更須聽斷，以熙庶績。

translations.literal: Just now war horses are not yet dispersed; kingly affairs are extremely numerous—moreover must hear and decide so as to brighten the myriad accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: War bands still roam and state business presses; you must hold court and decide cases so government can function.

sentences.zh: 昔周康王始登翌室，猶戴冕臨朝。

translations.literal: Formerly King Kang of Zhou when first ascending the next chamber still wore the crown and cap and attended court.
translations.idiomatic: Even King Kang of Zhou, fresh from the mourning chamber, already assumed his coronet and held audience.

sentences.zh: 降于漢魏，既葬除釋，諒闇之禮，自遠代而廢矣。

translations.literal: Descending to Han and Wei, once buried remove and release; the rite of "sincere darkness" [mourning seclusion], from remote generations has been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: By Han and Wei times mourning ended at burial; the old "silent vigil" of early kings had long since lapsed.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下割高宗之制，從當時之宜。

translations.literal: Only hope Your Majesty cuts Gaozong's regulations and follows what fits the present time.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to set aside the prolonged mourning of kings like Gaozong of Shang and follow what today's crisis demands.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「夫三年之喪，所以盡情致禮，葬已便除，所不堪也。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Now three years' mourning is the means fully to exhaust feeling and extend ritual; once buried then remove—what cannot be borne.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Three years exist precisely so feeling can match ritual; to strip mourning at burial alone I cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 當敘吾哀懷，言用斷絕，柰何！

translations.literal: About to narrate my sorrowful bosom, words use cutting off—what to do!
translations.idiomatic: If I speak my grief I break down—what can I do?

sentences.zh: 柰何！

translations.literal: What to do!
translations.idiomatic: What can I do?

sentences.zh: 」有司又固請。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices again firmly requested.
translations.idiomatic: " They pressed their plea again.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「不能篤孝，勿以毀傷為憂也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Unable to practice thick filial piety—do not take wrecked injury as worry.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Do not fret that strict mourning will ruin my health.

sentences.zh: 誠知衣服末事耳，然今思存草土，率當以吉物奪之，乃所以重傷至心，非見念也。

translations.literal: Truly know garments are trivial matters—yet now thinking to dwell on straw and earth, generally ought with auspicious things seize them—this is thus doubly to wound the utmost heart; it is not being mindful.
translations.idiomatic: Clothes are trifles, I agree; yet while my heart stays with her grave-mound, forcing bright dress on me would wound me more deeply—it would show no understanding.

sentences.zh: 每代禮典質文皆不同耳，何為限以近制，使達喪闕然乎！

translations.literal: Each generation's ritual canons, substance and pattern, all are not the same—why confine with recent regulations, causing the universally acknowledged mourning to be lacking!
translations.idiomatic: Every age reshapes ritual substance and style—why bind me to the latest shortcut and leave full mourning hollow?

sentences.zh: 」群臣又固請，帝流涕久之乃許。

translations.literal: " The host of ministers again firmly requested; the emperor wept flowing tears long and then granted.
translations.idiomatic: " After ministers insisted again, he wept for a long while before consenting.

sentences.zh: 文明皇后崩及武元楊后崩，天下將吏發哀三日止。

translations.literal: When Empress Wenming died and when Empress Wu Yuan surnamed Yang died, generals and clerks all under Heaven sounded mourning three days then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wenming and Empress Yuanwu Yang died, officers throughout the realm observed only three days of public lament.

sentences.zh: 穆帝崩，哀帝立。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu died; Emperor Ai was established.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mu died, Emperor Ai ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝于穆帝為從父昆弟，穆帝舅褚歆有表，中書答表朝廷無其儀，詔下議。

translations.literal: The emperor relative to Emperor Mu was father's brother's son male cousins; Emperor Mu's maternal uncle Chu Xin had a memorial; the Secretariat replied to the memorial that the court lacked its ceremony; an edict ordered discussion below.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai was Emperor Mu's cousin on their fathers' side. Chu Xin, Emperor Mu's uncle, submitted a memorial; the Secretariat replied that no precedent existed, and the throne ordered deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射江虨等四人並云，閔僖兄弟也，而為父子，則哀帝應為帝嗣。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Jiang Bin and four others together said: Min and Xi were brothers yet acted as father and son—then Emperor Ai ought to be imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin and three colleagues argued that because Duke Min and Duke Xi of Lu were brothers yet succeeded one another as father and son, Emperor Ai should count as Emperor Mu's ritual heir.

sentences.zh: 衛軍王述等二十五人云「成帝不私親愛，越授天倫，康帝受命顯宗。

translations.literal: General of the Guards Wang Shu and twenty-five others said: "Emperor Cheng did not selfishly favor intimate love; he crossed and handed the heavenly ethical bonds; Emperor Kang received the mandate from Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu and twenty-five others countered that Emperor Cheng had bypassed close kin to give the throne to Emperor Kang, who derived his legitimacy from Emperor Yuan (Xianzong).

sentences.zh: 社稷之重，已移所授，纂承之序，宜繼康皇。

translations.literal: The weight of altars of soil and grain already shifted what was conferred; the succession sequence ought to continue Emperor Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The mandate had already passed along that line; the succession should therefore follow Emperor Kang.

sentences.zh: 」尚書謝奉等六人云：「繼體之正，宜本天屬，考之人情，宜繼顯宗也。

translations.literal: " Director Xie Feng and six others said: "The correctness of inheriting the bodily succession ought to root in Heaven-conferred kinship; examining human feeling, ought to continue Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie Feng's faction held that legitimate succession follows blood and popular sentiment alike—Emperor Ai should therefore trace his line to Emperor Yuan (Xianzong).

sentences.zh: 」詔從述等議，上繼顯宗。

translations.literal: " The edict followed Shu and others' discussion, ascending to continue Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: " The court adopted Wang Shu's view and recognized Emperor Ai as succeeding Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 七月，簡文帝崩再周而遇閏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Emperor Jianwen died—two cycles completed and encountered intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year Emperor Jianwen died just as the second mourning cycle closed on an intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 博士謝攸、孔粲議：「魯襄二十八年十二月乙未，楚子卒，實閏月而言十二月者，附正於前月也。

translations.literal: Erudits Xie You and Kong Can discussed: "In Lu Xiang's twenty-eighth year, twelfth month yiwei, the Chu lord died—it was actually an intercalary month but speaks twelfth month—attaching correctness to the prior month.
translations.idiomatic: Doctors Xie You and Kong Can cited the Spring and Autumn entry for Duke Xiang's twenty-eighth year: though the Chu ruler died in an intercalary month recorded as the twelfth month, the entry counted it with the preceding standard month.

sentences.zh: 喪事先遠，則應用博士吳商之言，以閏月祥。

translations.literal: Mourning affairs prioritize what is farther—then ought to apply Erudit Wu Shang's words, taking intercalary month as xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Because mourning follows the remoter reckoning, they urged adopting Wu Shang's opinion and holding the xiang ceremony in the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 」尚書僕射謝安、中領軍王劭、散騎常侍鄭襲、右衛將軍殷康、驍騎將軍袁宏、散騎侍郎殷茂、中書郎車胤、左丞劉遵、吏部郎劉耽意皆同。

translations.literal: " Vice Director of the Secretariat Xie An, Central Army Commander Wang Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Zheng Xi, General of the Right Guard Yin Kang, General of Swift Cavalry Yuan Hong, Cavalier Gentleman Yin Mao, Secretariat Gentleman Che Yin, Left Assistant Liu Zun, Personnel Section Chief Liu Dan—all intentions were the same.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie An, Wang Shao, Zheng Xi, Yin Kang, Yuan Hong, Yin Mao, Che Yin, Liu Zun, and Liu Dan concurred.

sentences.zh: 康曰：「過七月而未及八月，豈可謂之逾期。

translations.literal: Kang said: "Having passed the seventh month but not yet reached the eighth month—how can it be called exceeding the period?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kang objected: "If the date falls after the seventh month but before the eighth, you cannot call that overdue.

sentences.zh: 必所不了，則當從其重者。

translations.literal: If what must be done is not completed, then ought to follow its heavier one.
translations.idiomatic: Where the calendar is ambiguous, follow the stricter reading.

sentences.zh: 」宏曰：「假值閏十二月而不取者，此則歲未終，固不可得矣。

translations.literal: " Hong said: "Suppose encountering intercalary twelfth month and not taking it—then this is the year not yet ended—indeed cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong replied that rejecting an intercalary twelfth month would leave the civil year unfinished—an unacceptable outcome.

sentences.zh: 《漢書》以閏為後九月，明其同體也。

translations.literal: The Book of Han treats the intercalary month as the "later ninth month," clarifying that they are of the same substance.
translations.idiomatic: The Han History counts an intercalary month as a trailing ninth month, showing it belongs to the same reckoning as the months around it.

sentences.zh: 」襲曰：「中宗、肅祖皆以閏月崩，祥除之變皆用閏之後月。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "Emperor Zhongzong and Emperor Suzu both died in intercalary months; the transitions for the great xiang removal all employed the month after the intercalary.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xi noted that Emperors Yuan and Ming had both died during intercalary months and that the shift out of the second mourning year had in each case been observed in the month following that intercalation.

sentences.zh: 先朝尚用閏之後月，今閏附七月，取之何疑，亦合遠日申情之言。

translations.literal: The prior court still used the month after intercalary; now intercalary attaches to the seventh month—what doubt in taking it? It also accords with the saying of choosing a distant day to express feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The previous reign did the same; now that the leap month rides with the seventh month, adopting it raises no difficulty and fits the classical preference for a later date that gives fuller expression to grief.

sentences.zh: 又閏是後七而非八也，豈逾月之嫌乎！

translations.literal: Moreover intercalary comes after seven and is not eight—how could there be suspicion of exceeding the month!
translations.idiomatic: The intercalary month still counts as after the seventh rather than the eighth—there is no "going past the month" here.

sentences.zh: 」尚書令王彪之、侍中王混、中丞譙王恬、右丞戴謐等議異，彪之曰：「吳商中才小官，非名賢碩儒、公輔重臣、為時所準則者。

translations.literal: " Director of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi, Palace Attendant Wang Hun, Palace Assistant Censor Prince of Qiao Wang Tian, Right Assistant Dai Mi, and others debated differently; Biaozhi said: "Wu Shang is a middling-talent petty official, not a famed worthy or great scholar, not a ministerial pillar heavy minister whom the age takes as norm.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi, Wang Hun, Wang Tian, Dai Mi, and others dissented. Wang Biaozhi argued that Wu Shang was only a junior erudit of middling ability—not a celebrated scholar or chief minister whose word should set the standard for the age.

sentences.zh: 又取閏無證據，直攬遠日之義，越祥忌，限外取，不合卜遠之理。

translations.literal: Moreover taking intercalary lacks textual proof; he straightway seizes the meaning of distant days, crosses xiang taboos, takes outside the limit—it does not accord with the principle of divining for a distant day.
translations.idiomatic: Nor does Wu Shang cite real precedent: he simply invokes choosing a remote date, skips past the weight of xiang prohibitions, and picks a day beyond the proper boundary—contrary to what "selecting a distant day" was meant to authorize.

sentences.zh: 又丞相桓公嘗論云，《禮》二十五月大祥。

translations.literal: Moreover Chancellor Duke Huan once discussed saying, the Rites [say] twenty-five months for great xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Chancellor Huan Wen had already argued that the canon fixes the great xiang at twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 何緣越期取閏，乃二十六月乎？

translations.literal: What cause crosses the period taking intercalary—thus twenty-six months?
translations.idiomatic: Why leap past that limit into an intercalary month and stretch mourning to twenty-six months?

sentences.zh: 」於是啟曰：「或以閏附七月，宜用閏月除者。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they presented: "Some hold that because intercalary attaches to the seventh month, one ought to use the intercalary month for removal.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial continued: "One faction holds that because the leap month belongs with the seventh month, mourning should end in that intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 或以閏名雖除七月，而實以三旬別為一月，故應以七月除者。

translations.literal: Some hold that although intercalary's name removes [attachment to] the seventh month, yet in reality three ten-day periods separately count as one month—therefore ought to remove in the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Others reply that although the leap period is reckoned after the seventh month, its thirty days still form a distinct month, so release should still fall in the seventh proper month.

sentences.zh: 臣等與中軍將軍沖參詳，一代大禮，宜準經典。

translations.literal: We and General of the Central Army Chong consulted in detail; for a generation's great rites, ought to align with the classics.
translations.idiomatic: We deliberated with General Xie Chong of the Central Army: such a fundamental observance must be anchored in classical warrant.

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，十三月而練，二十五月而畢，《禮》之明文也。

translations.literal: Three years' mourning: at thirteen months the lien practice; at twenty-five months it finishes—this is explicit text in the Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites state plainly that three years' mourning includes the lien change at thirteen months and concludes at twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 《陽秋》之義，閏在年內，則略而不數。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Yangqiu [Guliang tradition]: if intercalary falls within the year, then omit and do not count.
translations.idiomatic: Per the Guliang reading, an intercalary month inside the civil year is passed over in the reckoning.

sentences.zh: 明閏在年外，則不應取之以越期忌之重，禮制祥除必正期月故也。

translations.literal: Clarifying: if intercalary is outside the year, then ought not take it so as to cross the weight of period taboos—ritual regulation for xiang removal must correct the proper month—therefore.
translations.idiomatic: When the leap month hangs outside the counted year, adopting it would violate the gravity of the mourning limit; canonical release from xiang must observe the exact scheduled month.

sentences.zh: 」己酉晦，帝除縞即吉。

translations.literal: " On jiyou, last day of the month, the emperor removed white silk and entered auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the cycle, jiyou, the emperor laid aside white mourning garb and resumed normal dress.

sentences.zh: 徐廣論曰：「凡辨義詳理，無顯據明文可以折中奪易，則非疑如何。

translations.literal: Xu Guang discussed saying: "Whenever distinguishing meanings and detailing principles, if there is no manifest proof clear text by which to reconcile and alter—then if not doubtful how?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang observed that whenever doctrine lacks explicit textual warrant, one cannot simply overturn settled readings.

sentences.zh: 禮疑從重，喪易甯戚，順情通物，固有成言矣。

translations.literal: When ritual is doubtful follow the heavier; in mourning change—rather mourn fully—follow feeling and penetrate things—indeed there are established sayings.
translations.idiomatic: The canon itself bids us favor the stricter reading when rites are ambiguous, and in mourning to privilege heartfelt grief over convenience—the wise have said so plainly.

sentences.zh: 彪之不能徵援正義，有以相屈，但以名位格人，君子虛受，心無適莫，豈其然哉！

translations.literal: Biaozhi could not cite and summon correct righteousness whereby to bend others—only used fame and rank to block people; the gentleman emptily receives, mind without preference or refusal—how could it be thus!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi never cited orthodox precedent that could refute his opponents; he relied on official stature instead of argument—a gentleman weighs evidence impartially, but Wang hardly behaved like one.

sentences.zh: 執政從而行之，其殆過矣。」

translations.literal: Those holding power followed and enacted it—perhaps this exceeded."
translations.idiomatic: The dominant ministers accepted his line nonetheless—a grave mistake."

sentences.zh: 魏武以正月崩，魏文以其年七月設妓樂百戲，是則魏不以喪廢樂也。

translations.literal: Wei Wu died in the first month; Wei Wen in that year's seventh month set up singing-girls music and hundred entertainments—this then shows Wei did not because of mourning abolish music.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao died in the first month of that year, yet Cao Pi staged musicians and variety performances that seventh month—clear proof that Wei did not suspend music for the whole mourning period.

sentences.zh: 武帝以來，國有大喪，輒廢樂終三年。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wu onward, whenever the state had great mourning, then abolished music to the end of three years.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Jin and thereafter, major imperial bereavements brought a three-year suspension of court music.

sentences.zh: 惠帝太安元年，太子喪未除，及元會亦廢樂。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui first year of Tai'an, the heir-apparent's mourning not yet removed—when it reached New Year's court assembly likewise abolished music.
translations.idiomatic: In Tai'an 1 of Emperor Hui, mourning for the crown prince had not yet ended, so the New Year audience went ahead without music.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和中，為中原山陵未修復，頻年元會廢樂。

translations.literal: During Emperor Mu's Yonghe era, because Central Plain imperial tombs were not yet repaired, successive years' New Year's assemblies abolished music.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Emperor Mu's Yonghe reign the court omitted music from successive New Year ceremonies because the northern imperial tombs remained unrestored.

sentences.zh: 是時太后臨朝，后父褚裒薨，元會又廢樂也。

translations.literal: At this time the Empress Dowager faced court; the Empress's father Chu Pou died—New Year's assembly again abolished music.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while the Empress Dowager ruled from behind the screen, her father Chu Pou died and music was dropped from the New Year levee once more.

sentences.zh: 孝武，為皇后王氏喪，亦廢樂。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, for Empress Wang's mourning, likewise abolished music.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu likewise suspended music during mourning for Empress Wang.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，太傅錄尚書會稽王道子議：「山陵之後，通婚嫁不得作樂，以一期為斷。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Grand Tutor concurrently Recorder of the Secretariat Prince of Kuaiji Wang Daozi discussed: "After the hills-and-mounds tomb, passing marriage alliances may not make music—take one cycle as limit."
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu's death Wang Daozi ruled that until one full year after burial weddings across the realm must remain joyless—no music.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，太皇太后、皇太后崩，長樂太僕、少府大長秋典喪事，三公奉制度，他皆如禮。

translations.literal: Han protocol: when Grand Empress Dowager or Empress Dowager died, Changle Grand Coachman, Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Grand Chief Retainer supervised mourning affairs; Three Dukes presented regulations—other all according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Han precedent charged the Changle coachman and senior eunuch stewards with organizing an empress dowager's funeral while the Three Excellencies set the regulatory framework; everything else followed classical mourning codes.

sentences.zh: 魏晉亦同天子之儀。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin likewise matched Son of Heaven ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin courts mirrored the same imperial funeral ceremonies.

sentences.zh: ，武元楊皇后崩，及將遷于峻陽陵，依舊制，既葬，帝及群臣除喪即吉。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Empress Wu Yuan surnamed Yang died; when about to be transferred to Junyang Mausoleum, according to old regulation, once buried, the emperor and host of ministers removed mourning and entered auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Yuanwu Yang died and her cortège prepared removal to the Junyang tombs, precedent held: once she was buried, emperor and ministers alike shed mourning for auspicious dress.

sentences.zh: 先是，尚書祠部奏從博士張靖議，皇太子亦從制俱釋服。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Ministries Secretariat Cult Bureau memorialized following Erudit Zhang Jing's opinion—the heir-apparent likewise followed regulation together releasing garments.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Bureau of Sacrifices had memorialized to adopt Erudit Zhang Jing's opinion, and the crown prince too was to lay aside mourning alongside everyone else.

sentences.zh: 博士陳逵議，以為「今制所依，蓋漢帝權制，興於有事，非禮之正。

translations.literal: Erudit Chen Kui debated, considering: "What present regulation relies on is Han emperor expedient regulation—arisen when there were emergencies—not ritual correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Erudit Chen Kui argued that the current rule rests on Han expedients devised for emergencies—not on canonical mourning.

sentences.zh: 皇太子無有國事，自宜終服。

translations.literal: The heir-apparent has no state affairs—naturally ought to complete garments.
translations.idiomatic: The heir bears no public duties of his own and ought therefore to observe mourning to the end.

sentences.zh: 」有詔更詳議。

translations.literal: " There was an edict to deliberate again in detail.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne ordered further discussion.

sentences.zh: 尚書杜預以為：「古者天子諸侯三年之喪始同齊斬，既葬除喪服，諒闇以居，心喪終制，不與士庶同禮。

translations.literal: Minister Du Yu considered: "In antiquity Son of Heaven and feudal lords' three years' mourning at first alike qi cut hemp; once buried removed mourning garments, dwelt in sincere darkness, heart mourning completing regulation—not same ritual as gentlemen and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu argued that ancient sovereigns began mourning like everyone else but, once burial ended, doffed sackcloth and continued grief in seclusion—heart mourning through the full term—not the same observance required of common subjects.

sentences.zh: 漢氏承秦，率天下為天子修服三年。

translations.literal: Han inherited Qin; led all under Heaven to practice three years' garments for Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Han, inheriting Qin's institutions, kept the whole realm in three years of outward mourning for an emperor.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝見其下不可久行，而不知古制，更以意制祥禫，除喪即吉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han saw those below could not long practice it, yet did not know ancient regulation—further by intention regulated xiang and tan; removed mourning and entered auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen saw the bureaucracy could not sustain it indefinitely but misunderstood antiquity; he improvised rules for the second- and third-year rites and jumped straight to auspicious dress afterward.

sentences.zh: 魏氏直以訖葬為節，嗣君皆不復諒闇終制。

translations.literal: Wei took burial's completion as limit; succeeding lords all did not again sincere-darkness complete regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei treated burial as the cutoff, and no succeeding ruler afterward kept the full silent vigil through the classical term.

sentences.zh: 學者非之久矣，然竟不推究經傳，考其行事，專謂王者三年之喪，當以衰麻終二十五月。

translations.literal: Scholars have criticized this long—yet finally do not investigate classics and commentaries, examine their practiced affairs, exclusively holding that king's three years' mourning ought with frayed hemp end at twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: Classicists have complained for ages, yet few actually combed the texts and histories; most simply assumed a monarch must wear sackcloth the full twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 嗣君苟若此，則天子群臣皆不得除喪。

translations.literal: If succeeding lord were thus, then Son of Heaven and host of ministers all could not remove mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Were that rule binding on the heir, neither emperor nor bureaucracy could ever shed mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 雖志在居篤，更逼而不行。

translations.literal: Although intent lies in dwelling thickly, further pressed yet cannot proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Even sincere wishes for strict observance collapse under practical pressure.

sentences.zh: 至今世主皆從漢文輕典，由處制者非制也。

translations.literal: Down to now generations of rulers all follow Emperor Wen of Han's light canons—because those who framed regulation did not regulate.
translations.idiomatic: Hence every recent sovereign follows Emperor Wen's lighter code—the fault lies with legislators who legislated badly.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子與尊同體，宜復古典，卒哭除衰麻，以諒闇終制。

translations.literal: Now the heir-apparent with the honored shares one body—ought restore ancient regulation; at end-wailing remove frayed hemp; with sincere darkness complete regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince shares one body with his royal father; he should revive antiquity—strip sackcloth after the end-wailing rites and complete the term in silent heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 于義既不應不除，又無取于漢文，乃所以篤喪禮也。

translations.literal: As to righteousness, neither ought refuse removal; moreover nothing to take from Emperor Wen of Han—this then is the means to thicken mourning ritual.
translations.idiomatic: By principle he cannot refuse to end outward mourning, yet he need not ape Emperor Wen's shortcut—this is how to honor mourning in earnest.

sentences.zh: 」於是尚書僕射盧欽、尚書魏舒問杜預證據所依。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Qin and Minister Wei Shu asked Du Yu what evidence he relied on.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Qin and Wei Shu then pressed Du Yu for his textual proofs.

sentences.zh: 預云：「傳稱三年之喪自天子達，此謂天子絕期，唯有三年喪也。

translations.literal: Yu said: "The commentary states three years' mourning from Son of Heaven extends downward—this speaks of Son of Heaven cutting off qi—only having three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu answered that when the Zuozhuan says three years' mourning runs from the Son of Heaven downward, it means the throne ends the one-year mourning obligation—only the three-year observance applies.

sentences.zh: 非謂居喪衰服三年，與士庶同也。

translations.literal: It does not mean dwelling in mourning frayed garments three years, same as gentlemen and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: It does not mean the monarch wears sackcloth alongside commoners for three full years.

sentences.zh: 故后、世子之喪，而叔向稱有三年之喪二也。

translations.literal: Therefore empress and heir's mourning—yet Shu Xiang called there being two three-year mournings.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Shu Xiang could speak of two simultaneous three-year mournings when both empress and heir-apparent died.

sentences.zh: 周公不言高宗服喪三年，而云諒闇三年，此釋服心喪之文也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou did not say Gaozong wore mourning three years, but said sincere darkness three years—this is text of releasing garments heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou never said King Wu Ding wore mourning dress three years—only that he kept three years of silent vigil; that is the classical wording for doffing attire yet prolonging grief.

sentences.zh: 叔向不譏景王除喪，而譏其燕樂已早，明既葬應除，而違諒闇之節也。

translations.literal: Shu Xiang did not fault King Jing's removing mourning, but faulted his banquet music already early—clarifying once buried ought remove, yet violated sincere-darkness restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xiang faulted King Jing not for ending mourning dress but for holding convivial music too soon—proof that burial ends garments yet breach of the silent vigil still matters.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》，晉侯享諸侯，子產相鄭伯，時簡公未葬，請免喪以聽命，君子謂之得禮。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn: Jin marquis feasted feudal lords; Zichan assisted Zheng earl—at the time Duke Jian was not yet buried; requested release mourning to heed commands—the noble man called this obtaining ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn records how Zichan asked to set mourning aside while Duke Jian of Zheng remained unburied so he could attend Jin's feast—the gentleman judged this ritually proper.

sentences.zh: 宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵，傳曰『弔生不及哀』。

translations.literal: Minister Xuan came to present Duke Hui and Zhongzi's burial gifts—the commentary says "Condoling the living does not reach mourning."
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Xuan delivered funeral gifts for Duke Hui and Lady Zhongzi, the commentary noted that condolences offered while someone still lived do not substitute for mourning.

sentences.zh: 此皆既葬除服諒闇之證，先儒舊說，往往亦見，學者來之思耳。

translations.literal: These all are proofs of once buried removing garments sincere darkness—former scholars' old explanations often also appear—scholars come think on it.
translations.idiomatic: Each passage supports ending dress at burial while continuing seclusion—earlier exegetes often noted the same if later students troubled to look.

sentences.zh: 《喪服》，諸侯為天子亦斬衰，豈可謂終服三年邪！

translations.literal: The Mourning Garments: feudal lords for Son of Heaven likewise cut hemp—how can it be called completing garments three years!
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Dress canon prescribes even feudal lords' utmost sackcloth for the Son of Heaven—would anyone insist they literally wear it three full years?

sentences.zh: 上考七代，未知王者君臣上下衰麻三年者誰；

translations.literal: Ascending examine seven generations—do not know who among kings ruler-minister above-below frayed hemp three years;
translations.idiomatic: Look back through seven dynasties and you will not find emperor and bureaucracy alike in sackcloth for three solid years.

sentences.zh: 下推將來，恐百世之主其理一也。

translations.literal: Descending extrapolate to future—fear hundred generations' rulers their principle is one.
translations.idiomatic: Project forward and every sovereign will face the same imperatives.

sentences.zh: 非必不能，乃事勢不得，故知聖人不虛設不行之制。

translations.literal: Not must be unable—rather affairs' momentum cannot obtain—therefore know sages did not vainly establish unworkable regulations.
translations.idiomatic: It is not inability but circumstance that forbids full dress mourning—so the sages never mandated unusable rules.

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰『禮所損益雖百世可知』，此之謂也。

translations.literal: Zhongni said "What ritual diminishes or augments—even through hundred generations can be known"—this speaks of it.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said ritual's expansions and contractions remain intelligible across ages—this is what he meant.

sentences.zh: 」於是飲、舒從之，遂命預造議，奏曰：

translations.literal: " Thereupon Qin and Shu followed him; then ordered Yu to draft discussion, memorializing saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Qin and Wei Shu accepted his reading and commissioned Du Yu to draft a formal memorial summarizing:

sentences.zh: 於是太子遂以厭降之議，從國制除衰麻，諒闇終制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the heir-apparent then by suppressed-descending discussion followed state regulation removing frayed hemp, sincere darkness completing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince therefore accepted the "suppressed descent" formula: he followed dynastic usage in laying aside sackcloth while completing the term in private mourning.

sentences.zh: 于時外內卒聞預異議，多怪之。

translations.literal: At that time outer and inner suddenly heard Yu's dissenting opinion—many wondered at it.
translations.idiomatic: Court and capital alike were startled by Du Yu's unusual thesis and largely disapproved.

sentences.zh: 或者乃謂其違禮以合時。

translations.literal: Some then called it violating ritual so as to suit the times.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged him with bending ritual to modern convenience.

sentences.zh: 時預亦不自解說，退使博士段暢博采典籍，為之證據，令大義著明，足以垂示將來。

translations.literal: At the time Yu also did not himself explain; withdrew and ordered Erudit Duan Chang broadly gather classics and records, making for it evidence, causing great meaning clear—sufficient to hang and show future.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu did not argue further at once; he assigned Erudit Duan Chang to compile classical citations that would clarify the principle for posterity.

sentences.zh: 暢承預旨，遂撰集書傳舊文，條諸實事成言，以為定證，以弘指趣。

translations.literal: Chang received Yu's intent; thereupon compiled and gathered document commentary old texts, itemizing various accomplished facts into statements, taking them as fixed proofs, so as to enlarge intended direction.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chang carried out Du Yu's brief, assembling classical passages and arranging verified precedents into a dossier that spelled out the larger argument.

sentences.zh: 其傳記有與今議同者，亦具列之，博舉二隅，明其會歸，以證斯事。

translations.literal: Among biographical records those agreeing with present discussion, likewise fully list them; broadly raise two corners—clarify their convergent return—so as to prove this affair.
translations.idiomatic: He listed every anecdote that matched Du Yu's reading, showing both sides of the debate so the synthesis would prove the case.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is much—not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The full compilation is omitted here for length.

sentences.zh: 武帝楊悼皇后既母養懷帝，后遇難時，懷帝尚幼，及即位，中詔述后恩愛。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's Empress Yang Dao having mother-nurtured Emperor Huai—when the empress met calamity, Huai was still young; when he ascended, inner edict narrated the empress's kindness and love.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dao of Emperor Wu had raised Emperor Huai as a mother; when she met violent death he was still a child, and on enthronement he issued an intimate edict recounting her devotion.

sentences.zh: 及后祖載，群官議帝應為追制服，或以庶母慈己，依禮制小功五月，或以謂慈母服如母服齊衰者，眾議不同。

translations.literal: When the empress's spirit carriage departed, host of officials debated whether the emperor ought practice retrospective regulation garments—some by concubine-mother kindly nurturing self, according to ritual regulating si-gong five months; some by calling foster-mother garments like mother's garments qi-cui—crowd opinions differed.
translations.idiomatic: At her funeral convoy officials disputed what retrospective mourning the emperor owed: some cited the five-month si privilege for a nurturing concubine mother, others equated her with a foster mother deserving qi-cui like a birth mother—opinion split.

sentences.zh: 閭丘沖議云：「楊后母養聖上，蓋以曲情。

translations.literal: Lüqiu Chong debated saying: "Empress Yang mother-nurtured the sage ascendant—generally by indirect feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Lüqiu Chong argued that Empress Yang's nurture rested on an exceptional bond rather than standard kinship.

sentences.zh: 今以恩禮追崇，不配世祖廟。

translations.literal: Now by kindness ritual posthumously honors—not paired in Shizu temple.
translations.idiomatic: She is honored posthumously yet not enshrined with Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 王者無慈養之服，謂宜祖載之日，可三朝素服發哀而已。

translations.literal: Kings lack kindly-nurturing garments—we consider on spirit-carriage day, may three courts plain garments sound grief—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: No canonical mourning grade fits a royal foster mother; plain dress and lament for three courts on the day of her cortège should suffice.

sentences.zh: 」於是從之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The court adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 康帝正月晦，成恭杜皇后周忌，有司奏，至尊期年應改服。

translations.literal: Emperor Kang first month last day—Empress Cheng Gong surnamed Du weekly taboo—relevant offices memorialized: the supreme one full year ought change garments.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of Emperor Kang's first lunar month fell the first anniversary of Empress Cheng Gong Du's death; officials reported that the sovereign should change mourning grade after one cycle.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「君親，名教之重也，權制出於近代耳。

translations.literal: Edict said: "Lord and kin—this is the weight of name-teaching; expedient regulation issues from recent generations alone.
translations.idiomatic: An edict answered: "Sovereign and parent anchor moral order; recent dynasties invented expedients.

sentences.zh: 」於是素服如舊，固非漢魏之典也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon plain garments as before—indeed not Han–Wei canons.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore kept plain dress as before—far stricter than Han or Wei precedent.

sentences.zh: ，哀帝章皇太妃薨，帝欲服重。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Empress Zhang imperial concubine died—emperor desired to wear heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When Honored Consort Zhang died, Emperor Ai wished to observe heavier mourning.

sentences.zh: 江虨啟：「先王制禮，應在緦服。

translations.literal: Jiang Bin presented: "Former kings regulated ritual—ought be in si garments.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin replied that former kings assigned only the lightest si-grade hemp.

sentences.zh: 」詔欲降期，虨又啟：「厭屈私情，所以上嚴祖考。

translations.literal: " Edict desired to lower to qi period—Bin again presented: "Suppressing bending private feeling—this is how above to solemnize ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor sought one-year mourning instead, Jiang urged him to restrain private feeling so as to uphold ancestral dignity.

sentences.zh: 」於是制緦麻三月。

translations.literal: " Thereupon regulated si hemp three months.
translations.idiomatic: " They settled on three months in finest mourning hemp.

sentences.zh: 孝武甯康中，崇德太后褚氏崩。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowu's Ningkang era, Empress Dowager Chongde surnamed Chu died.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaowu's Ningkang reign Empress Dowager Chongde of the Chu clan died.

sentences.zh: 后於帝為從嫂，或疑其服。

translations.literal: The empress relative to the emperor was father's brother's son's wife—some doubted her garments.
translations.idiomatic: She was the emperor's cousin-in-law, which puzzled officials about the proper mourning grade.

sentences.zh: 博士徐藻議，以為：「資父事君而敬同。

translations.literal: Erudit Xu Zao debated, considering: "Taking father serves lord yet reverence same.
translations.idiomatic: Erudit Xu Zao argued that serving one's ruler matches serving one's father in solemn duty.

sentences.zh: 又，禮，其夫屬父道者，其妻皆母道也。

translations.literal: Moreover ritual: whose husbands belong to father's way—their wives all are mother's way.
translations.idiomatic: The canon adds that wives join their husbands' ritual generation—those wed to men treated as fathers are mothers in ritual terms.

sentences.zh: 則夫屬君道，妻亦后道矣。

translations.literal: Then husbands belonging to lord's way—wives likewise empress way.
translations.idiomatic: If the husband ranks as sovereign, his consort ranks as empress in ritual logic.

sentences.zh: 服后宜以資母之義。

translations.literal: Serving empress ought by foster-mother meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning her therefore follows the foster-mother precedent.

sentences.zh: 魯譏逆祀，以明尊尊。

translations.literal: Lu criticized inverted sacrifice—so as to clarify honoring honor.
translations.idiomatic: Lu censured misplaced sacrifices to clarify hierarchical precedence.

sentences.zh: 今上躬奉康、穆、哀皇及靖后之祀，致敬同於所天。

translations.literal: Now the ascendant personally attends Kang, Mu, Ai emperors and Empress Jing's sacrifices—extending reverence same as to him who is Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The reigning emperor personally sacrifices to Emperors Kang, Mu, and Ai and to Empress Jing with the same reverence he owes Heaven's surrogate.

sentences.zh: 豈可敬之以君道，而服廢於本親。

translations.literal: How can reverence them by lord way—yet garments abolished toward root kin?
translations.idiomatic: How treat her with sovereign honors in sacrifice yet withhold mourning owed close kin?

sentences.zh: 謂應服齊衰期。

translations.literal: Consider ought wear qi-cui qi period.
translations.idiomatic: He concluded that one year's qi-cui mourning was appropriate.

sentences.zh: 」於是帝制期服。

translations.literal: " Thereupon emperor regulated qi garments.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor therefore adopted one-year mourning.

sentences.zh: ，孝武太皇太后李氏崩，疑所服。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Grand Empress Dowager Li of Emperor Xiaowu died—doubted what garments.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Empress Dowager Li died under Emperor Xiaowu, officials debated the emperor's mourning grade.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射何澄、右僕射王雅、尚書車胤、孔安國、祠部郎徐廣議、太皇太后名位允正，體同皇極，理制備盡，情禮彌申。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director He Cheng, Right Vice Director Wang Ya, Ministers Che Yin, Kong Anguo, Cult Bureau Chief Xu Guang debated: Grand Empress Dowager name position duly correct—substance matches august pole—principle regulation fully complete—feeling ritual further extends.
translations.idiomatic: He Cheng, Wang Ya, Che Yin, Kong Anguo, and Xu Guang held that the Grand Empress Dowager's standing matched the cosmic pivot; ritual obligation toward her was therefore complete and emotionally weighty.

sentences.zh: 《陽秋》之義，母以子貴，既稱夫人，禮服從正。

translations.literal: The Yangqiu meaning: mother by son becomes noble—already titled lady—mourning garments follow correctness.
translations.idiomatic: The Guliang principle that a mother's rank rises with her son means that once styled "lady," mourning follows the orthodox grade.

sentences.zh: 故成風顯夫人之號，文公服三年之喪。

translations.literal: Therefore Chengfeng displayed lady's title—Duke Wen practiced three years' mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Duke Wen of Lu mourned Lady Chengfeng the full three years once she received ducal honors.

sentences.zh: 子于父之所生，體尊義重。

translations.literal: Son toward father's bearing-born—substance noble righteousness heavy.
translations.idiomatic: A son honors his father's birth mother with heightened ritual gravity.

sentences.zh: 且禮，祖不厭孫，固宜遂服無屈，而緣情立制。

translations.literal: Moreover ritual: grandfather does not suppress grandson—solidly ought follow garments without bend—yet along feeling establish regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the canon says an ancestor does not cancel a grandson's mourning—the sovereign should follow full observance without diminution, tailoring only by humane circumstance.

sentences.zh: 若嫌明文不存，則疑斯從重，謂應同于為祖母后齊衰期。

translations.literal: If suspect clear text not preserved—then doubt this follow heavy—consider ought same as for grandmother empress qi-cui qi period.
translations.idiomatic: Where texts seem silent, favor the heavier reading: treat her like a dowager grandmother—one year of qi-cui.

sentences.zh: 永安皇后無服，但一舉哀，百官亦一期。

translations.literal: Empress Yong'an without garments—only one sounding grief—hundred officials likewise one qi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yong'an required no graded mourning—only a single lament—while officials observed one cycle.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " Edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝，淑媛陳氏卒，皇太子所生也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu—Noble Lady Chen died—she was the one by whom heir-apparent was born.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu, Noble Lady Chen—the crown prince's birth mother—passed away.

sentences.zh: 有司參詳母以子貴，贈淑媛為夫人，置家令典喪事。

translations.literal: Relevant offices consulted in detail mother by son noble—posthumously gifted Noble Lady as lady—set up Household Superintendent superintending mourning affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials cited the principle that a mother's rank rises with her son, promoted Lady Chen posthumously to "lady," and assigned a household superintendent to manage the funeral.

sentences.zh: 太子前衛率徐邈議：「《喪服傳》稱與尊者為體，則不服其私親。

translations.literal: Former crown-prince guard commander Xu Miao debated: "The Mourning Garments Commentary states that when one forms one body with the honored person, then one does not wear mourning for one's private kin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao, lately commander of the crown prince's guard, cited the Mourning Garments subcommentary: whoever is ritually one with a superior does not observe mourning for a private parent.

sentences.zh: 又，君父所不服，子亦不敢服。

translations.literal: Moreover, what lord and father does not wear, the son likewise dare not wear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a son may not wear mourning that his sovereign father foregoes.

sentences.zh: 故王公妾子服其所生母練冠麻衣，既葬而除，非五服之常，則謂之無服。

translations.literal: Therefore royal lords' sons by concubines wear for their birth mothers lien cap and hemp cloth—once buried then remove—not among the five garments' constant norms—then it is called having no garment.
translations.idiomatic: Hence princes' sons by concubines wear only a plain lien cap and hemp until burial, then lay them aside—outside the five canonical grades—ritually counted as "no mourning."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court accepted his reading.

sentences.zh: ，孝武帝崩，孝武太后制三年之服。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Emperor Xiaowu died—Empress Dowager Xiaowu regulated three years' garments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Empress Dowager Xiaowu ordered full three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 惠帝三月，皇太孫尚薨。

translations.literal: In the third month of Emperor Hui's reign, the imperial grandson-heir Shang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Emperor Hui's reign, Sima Shang, heir as imperial grandson, died.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，御服齊衰期。

translations.literal: The offices memorialized that the sovereign should wear qi-cui for one full year (qi).
translations.idiomatic: The authorities asked that the emperor observe qi-cui mourning for the standard one-year term.

sentences.zh: 詔下通議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered general court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent down an edict for the whole bureaucracy to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍謝衡以為：「諸侯之太子，誓與未誓，尊卑體殊。

translations.literal: Cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Xie Heng held: "For a feudal lord's heir apparent, sworn presentation versus not yet sworn—the honored base and bodily tie differ.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Heng, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, argued that for a feudal heir's ritual standing, whether or not he had undergone the sworn presentation rite made a real difference in rank and ritual "one body."

sentences.zh: 《喪服》云為嫡子長殤，謂未誓也，已誓則不殤也。

translations.literal: The Mourning Garments [canon] states mourning for the eldest legitimate son's long shang means not yet sworn; once sworn then it is not [counted as] shang.
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garments canon treats mourning for an eldest legitimate son who dies in the "long shang" bracket as applying only before the sworn presentation; after that rite he is no longer classed as a shang death.

sentences.zh: 」中書令卞粹曰：「太子始生，故已尊重，不待命誓。

translations.literal: " Minister of the Secretariat Bian Cui said: "The heir apparent from birth is therefore already honored high—does not await mandate-swearing.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Cui, minister of the Secretariat, answered that a crown prince is already supreme in rank from birth and does not wait upon any separate mandate or sworn presentation.

sentences.zh: 若衡議已誓不殤，則無服之子當斬衰三年；

translations.literal: If by Xie's debate sworn means not shang, then the son for whom there is no [shang-scale] garment ought wear zhan-cui three years;
translations.idiomatic: If Xie's rule—sworn, therefore not shang—were accepted, any son outside the shang grades would require the mourner to wear zhan-cui for three full years;

sentences.zh: 未誓而殤，則雖十九當大功九月。

translations.literal: not sworn and [dies as] shang, then though age nineteen ought wear da gong nine months.
translations.idiomatic: yet if he had not been sworn and still counted as shang, even at nineteen the prescribed grade would be only da gong for nine months.

sentences.zh: 誓與未誓，其為升降也微；

translations.literal: Sworn and not sworn—the rise and fall therein is slight;
translations.idiomatic: The ritual gap between sworn and unsworn is tiny;

sentences.zh: 斬衰與大功，其為輕重也遠。

translations.literal: zhan-cui and da gong—the light and heavy therein is far apart.
translations.idiomatic: but the gulf between zhan-cui and da gong is enormous.

sentences.zh: 而今注云『諸侯不降嫡殤重』。

translations.literal: Yet now the commentary states 'feudal lords do not lower the weight of legitimate-son shang.'
translations.idiomatic: The gloss nonetheless says feudal lords do not mitigate mourning for a legitimate son who dies young.

sentences.zh: 嫌于無服，以大功為重嫡之服，則雖誓，無復有三年之理明矣。

translations.literal: Loath to [say] no garment, taking da gong as the garment weighting the legitimate heir—then though sworn, there is no longer principle for three years—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid calling it "no mourning," commentators assign da gong as the heavy mourning for the heir—so even after the sworn rite, three years of zhan-cui simply cannot apply. That much is plain.

sentences.zh: 男能衛社稷，女能奉婦道，以可成之年而有已成之事，故可無殤，非孩齔之謂也。

translations.literal: When a male can guard altars of soil and grain and a female can uphold the wifely way—in years when completion is possible yet matters already accomplished—therefore may be without shang—it does not mean infant teeth.
translations.idiomatic: A lad old enough to defend the altars, or a girl able to discharge a wife's duties, has crossed out of the shang brackets once capable adulthood is acknowledged—not toddlers still at breast.

sentences.zh: 為殤後者尊之如父，猶無所加而止殤服，況以天子之尊，而為無服之殤行成人之制邪！

translations.literal: One who succeeds a shang [decedent] honors him like a father—still adds nothing and stops at shang garment—how much more with Heaven's Son's honor to enact adult norms for a shang without garment!
translations.idiomatic: An heir who continues a shang line honors the dead like a father yet still caps mourning at the shang grades—how then could the Son of Heaven impose full adult mourning where the canon prescribes none?

sentences.zh: 凡諸宜重之殤，皆士大夫不加服，而令至尊獨居其重，未之前聞也。

translations.literal: All shangs that ought be weighted—great officers add no garment—yet to make the supremacy alone bear the weight—never before heard.
translations.idiomatic: Every other heavy shang case lets ministers stop short of extra mourning; to load that weight solely onto the sovereign would be without precedent.

sentences.zh: 」博士蔡克同粹。

translations.literal: " Erudite Cai Ke agreed with Bian Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Court erudite Cai Ke sided with Bian Cui.

sentences.zh: 秘書監摯虞云：「太子初生，舉以成人之禮，則殤理除矣。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Library Zhi Yu said: "The heir apparent from birth is raised with adult rites—then shang principle is removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu, director of the palace library, said the crown prince is invested from birth with ceremonies meant for adults, so the logic of "shang" mourning drops away entirely.

sentences.zh: 太孫亦體君傳重，由位成而服，全非以年也。

translations.literal: The grand heir likewise forms one body with the lord and transmits weight—garments follow from position achieved, wholly not by age.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson-heir likewise embodies the ruler and bears the ritual "weight"; mourning follows his station, not his calendar age.

sentences.zh: 天子無服殤之義，絕期故也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has no principle of wearing [mourning for] shang—because [such ties] are cut off at one full cycle (qi).
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven never wears shang-grade mourning for kin, precisely because those relationships are ritually severed at the one-year boundary.

sentences.zh: 」於是從之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon [the court] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted this view.

sentences.zh: 魏氏故事，國有大喪，群臣凶服，以帛為綬囊，以布為劍衣。

translations.literal: Wei-house precedent: when the state had great mourning, many ministers wore funeral dress—silk for seal-cord pouches, cloth for sword sheaths.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei dynasty usage, a dynastic funeral saw ministers in mourning garb with silk pouches for seal cords and cloth wrappers for swords.

sentences.zh: 新禮，以《傳》稱「去喪無所不佩」，明在喪則無佩也，更制齊斬之喪不佩劍綬。

translations.literal: The New Rites, because the Commentary states 'upon leaving mourning nothing is not suspended,' clarifies that in mourning there is no suspension—reformed so qi-cui and zhan-cui mourning do not suspend sword and seal cord.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin "New Rites" cited the gloss "after mourning ends, everything may hang from the belt" to infer that during mourning nothing should hang there, and barred sword and seal cord under qi-cui and zhan-cui.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為「《周禮》武賁氏，士大夫之職也，皆以兵守王宮，國有喪故，則衰葛執戈楯守門，葬則從車而哭。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held that "the Zhou Rites' Wu-ben guards—great officers' duty—all with arms guard the royal palace; when the state has mourning cause, then [wear] frayed robe and kudzu, grasp halberd and shield guarding gates; at burial then follow carts and wail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu countered that the Zhou Rites' royal guardsmen were officers under arms who defended the palace; on a national bereavement they wore mourning hemp with shield and polearm at the gates and followed the hearse wailing.

sentences.zh: 又，成王崩，太保命諸大夫以干戈內外警設。

translations.literal: Moreover, when King Cheng died, Grand Protect ordered various great officers with shields and halberds to set inner and outer vigil.
translations.idiomatic: When King Cheng died, the Grand Protect ordered ministers to stand watch inside and out with shields and halberds.

sentences.zh: 明喪故之際，蓋重宿衛之防。

translations.literal: This clarifies that at mourning's crisis one esteems night-watch defense.
