translations.idiomatic: That shows how gravely a reign treats palace security even amid mourning.

sentences.zh: 去喪無所不佩，謂服飾之事，不謂防禦之用。

translations.literal: 'Upon leaving mourning nothing not suspended' speaks of adornment matters—not defense uses.
translations.idiomatic: "Nothing suspended after mourning" governs dress ornaments, not weapons of defense.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮布衣劍如舊，其餘如新制。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites: cloth garment and sword as of old—the rest as new regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites should keep cloth sword covers as before and leave the rest under the new rules.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事，將葬，設吉凶鹵簿，皆以鼓吹。

translations.literal: Han-Wei precedent: nearing burial, set auspicious and inauspicious halberd-escort arrays—all used drum-and-pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei practice paired auspicious and funeral halberd escorts at burial, both complete with military music.

sentences.zh: 新禮以禮無吉駕導從之文，臣子不宜釋其衰麻以服玄黃，除吉駕鹵簿。

translations.literal: The New Rites held the rites lack text for auspicious carriages with outriders—ministers and sons ought not shed their frayed hemp to wear black-and-yellow—removed auspicious-carriage halberd escort.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites argued classical texts never sanctioned festive carriages and outriders for a burial, so ministers should not strip mourning hemp for court blacks—and struck the auspicious half of the halberd escort.

sentences.zh: 又，凶事無樂，遏密八音，除凶服之鼓吹。

translations.literal: Moreover, inauspicious affairs have no music—suppress and silence the eight tones—removed drum-and-pipe from funeral dress [processions].
translations.idiomatic: Funerals should silence every instrument, they added, so drum-and-pipe bands had to go from the mourning procession as well.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「葬有祥車曠左，則今之容車也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: "Burial has auspicious cart with empty left seat—that is today's appearance cart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu replied that the classic "auspicious cart with the left seat left empty" is the ancestor of today's display carriage.

sentences.zh: 既葬，日中反虞，逆神而還。

translations.literal: Once buried, at midday perform returning yu, welcome the spirit back.
translations.idiomatic: After interment, the noon returning-yu rite escorts the spirit home again.

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》，鄭大夫公孫蠆卒，天子追賜大路，使以行。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Commentary: Zheng grand officer Gongsun Chai died—the Son of Heaven posthumously granted great road-chariot, ordering it used for the procession.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition records how, when Zheng minister Gongsun Chai died, the Zhou king sent a state chariot so the cortège could ride in due splendor.

sentences.zh: 《士喪禮》，葬有稿車乘車，以載生之服。

translations.literal: The Gentlemen's Mourning Rites: burial has straw cart and riding cart—to carry garb [used] in life.
translations.idiomatic: The "Gentleman's Mourning" specifies straw carts and riding carts bearing the clothes the dead wore in life.

sentences.zh: 此皆不唯載柩，兼有吉駕之明文也。

translations.literal: These all not only bear the coffin—together they have explicit text for auspicious carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Those provisions plainly sanction festive vehicles alongside the bier, not coffins alone.

sentences.zh: 既設吉駕，則宜有導從，以象平生之容，明不致死之義。

translations.literal: Once auspicious carriages are set, then fittingly there should be outriders—to image deportment in life, clarifying the meaning of not treating [the deceased] as utterly dead.
translations.idiomatic: Where such carriages appear, outriders belong too—the ritual echoes how the noble lived and insists he is not cast away like carrion.

sentences.zh: 臣子衰麻不得為身而釋，以為君父則無不可。

translations.literal: Ministers and sons in frayed hemp may not for themselves shed—for lord and father then nothing impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: A minister may not shrug off mourning for private convenience, yet for his lord or father nothing in the canon forbids fitting splendor to the cortège.

sentences.zh: 《顧命》之篇足以明之。

translations.literal: The 'Charge at Gu' piece suffices to clarify this.
translations.idiomatic: The "Charge at Gu" chapter of the Documents proves the point.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮設吉服導從如舊，其凶服鼓吹宜除。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites to set auspicious-garment outriders as of old—the funeral drum-and-pipe ought be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu urged restoring festive outriders under the New Rites while still banning martial music on the mourning train.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事，大喪及大臣之喪，執紼者輓歌。

translations.literal: Han-Wei precedent: great mourning and great ministers' mourning—those holding tow-ropes sang dirges.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei custom had catafalque bearers chant pulling-dirges at imperial funerals and at those of great ministers.

sentences.zh: 新禮以為輓歌出於漢武帝役人之勞歌，聲哀切，遂以為送終之禮。

translations.literal: The New Rites held dirges arose from Han Emperor Wu's corvée people's labor songs—sound mournful and piercing—thereupon taken as seeing-off-the-end rite.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites traced those laments to corvée labor songs under Emperor Wu—voices sharp with grief—and showed how they had hardened into funeral practice.

sentences.zh: 雖音曲摧愴，非經典所制，違禮設銜枚之義。

translations.literal: Though melody is crushing-grief—not fashioned by classics—contravenes the rites' meaning of mouth-plugs.
translations.idiomatic: However wrenching the tunes, they are nowhere mandated in the classics and violate the spirit of biting wooden gag-bits to keep silence.

sentences.zh: 方在號慕，不宜以歌為名。

translations.literal: Just now in wailing longing—not fitting to take 'song' as name.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-wail for the dead, nothing should parade under the label of "song."

sentences.zh: 除，不輓歌。

translations.literal: Removed—no dirges.
translations.idiomatic: The reform abolished pulling-dirges altogether.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「輓歌因倡和而為摧愴之聲，銜枚所以全哀，此亦以感眾。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: "Dirges through lead-and-chorus become crushing sounds—mouth-plugs thereby preserve mourning—this too thereby moves the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued that antiphonal dirges shape communal grief, much as gag-bits enforce solemn silence—they stir the throng rather than cheapen it.

sentences.zh: 雖非經典所載，是歷代故事。

translations.literal: Though not carried in classics—it is successive dynasties' precedent.
translations.idiomatic: They never appear verbatim in the canon, yet dynasty after dynasty relied on them.

sentences.zh: 《詩》稱『君子作歌，惟以告哀』，以歌為名，亦無所嫌。

translations.literal: The Odes state 'the gentleman makes song—only to declare grief'—to take song as name—also nothing blameworthy.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes themselves praise the gentleman who "raises a song only to voice sorrow," so the word "song" is hardly improper.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮如舊。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites as of old.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the New Rites reinstate the older practice.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his opinion.

sentences.zh: ，安平穆王薨，無嗣，以母弟敦上繼獻王後，移太常問應何服。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Prince Mu of Anping died—no heir—his uterine younger brother Dun was elevated to continue Prince Xian's line—the case was referred to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials asking what mourning ought apply.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Mu of Anping died without issue, his full brother Sima Dun was promoted to continue Prince Xian's line; the matter went to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials to settle the proper mourning grades.

sentences.zh: 博士張靖答，宜依魯僖服閔三年例。

translations.literal: Erudite Zhang Jing replied—it should follow Duke Xi of Lu's mourning Duke Min three-year precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Zhang Jing answered that the parallel was Duke Xi of Lu wearing three years' mourning for Duke Min.

sentences.zh: 尚書符詰靖：「穆王不臣敦，敦不繼穆，與閔僖不同。

translations.literal: The Secretariat issued a writ pressing Jing: "Prince Mu did not treat Dun as subject—Dun does not succeed Mu—this differs from Min and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat shot back: Prince Mu never treated Dun as his subject, and Dun was not succeeding Prince Mu himself—nothing like the Duke Min and Duke Xi case.

sentences.zh: 」孫毓、宋昌議，以穆王不之國，敦不仕諸侯，不應三年。

translations.literal: " Sun Yu and Song Chang debated that because Prince Mu never went to his fief and Dun never served feudal lords, three years should not apply.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu and Song Chang countered that because Prince Mu never took up his fief and Dun had never served as a feudal officer, full three-year mourning was out of the question.

sentences.zh: 以義處之，敦宜服本服，一期而除，主穆王喪祭三年畢，乃吉祭獻王。

translations.literal: Judging by right principle, Dun ought wear his proper garment—remove after one full cycle (qi)—preside over Prince Mu's mourning sacrifices completing three years—then perform auspicious sacrifice to Prince Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On principle, Dun should wear only his own proper grade—doffing it after the one-year term—yet still oversee Prince Mu's mortuary rites through three years before he may offer auspicious sacrifices to Prince Xian.

sentences.zh: 毓云：「《禮》，君之子孫所以臣諸兄者，以臨國故也。

translations.literal: Sun Yu said: "By the Rites, why lord's descendants treat elder brothers as lord—because they face the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu cited the canon: princes' sons honor elder brothers as lords only when they actually rule a state.

sentences.zh: 《禮》又與諸侯為兄弟服斬者，謂鄰國之臣於鄰國之君，有猶君之義故也。

translations.literal: The Rites moreover [say] wearing zhan-cui for feudal-lord brothers means neighboring state's ministers toward neighboring state's lord—because there is quasi-lord meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan-cui for a brother who is another state's ruler applies only where ministers owe their neighbor's prince something like fealty.

sentences.zh: 今穆王既不之國，不臣兄弟，敦不仕諸侯，無鄰臣之義，異于閔僖，如符旨也。

translations.literal: Now Prince Mu neither went to state nor treated brothers as subjects—Dun never served feudal lords—no neighboring-minister meaning—differs from Min and Xi—as the writ's intent [states].
translations.idiomatic: Here Prince Mu never took his throne in the fief, never treated brothers as vassals, and Dun was no feudal minister—so none of the "neighbor's minister" logic applies, exactly as the Secretariat argued.

sentences.zh: 但喪無主，敦既奉詔紹國，受重主喪，典其祭祀。

translations.literal: But mourning lacked a master—Dun having received edict to continue the state—received weight and presided mourning—administers its sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bereavement had no ritual head; Dun, ordered to continue the line, carries the "weight" of heirship, directs the funeral, and manages the offerings.

sentences.zh: 『大功者主人之喪，有三年者則必為之再祭』。

translations.literal: 'For da gong [mourning] the master's mourning—if there is one with three years then must perform for him twice the sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: "When the chief mourner wears da gong but someone else in the household still owes three full years, he must conduct both intermediate auspicious rites for them."

sentences.zh: 鄭氏《注》云，『謂死者之從父昆弟來為喪主也。

translations.literal: Zheng's Commentary states: '[This] means the deceased's father's brothers' sons who come as mourning master.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses this as paternal cousins who arrive to act as funeral master.

sentences.zh: 」有三年者，謂妻若子幼少也』。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior quotation;] 'those who have three years' refers to wife or young children (close of Zheng Xuan gloss).
translations.idiomatic: Zheng finishes the gloss: the survivors who still owe three years are the widow or very young children.

sentences.zh: 『再祭，謂大小祥也』。

translations.literal: 'Twice sacrifice means great and small xiang.'
translations.idiomatic: "The two offerings are the great and small xiang rites."

sentences.zh: 穆妃及國臣於禮皆當三年，此為有三年者，敦當為之主大小兩祥祭也。

translations.literal: Prince Mu's consort and state ministers by rites all ought three years—these are those with three years—Dun ought for them preside both great- and small-xiang sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mu's consort and his household ministers each owe three years of mourning; they are the "three-year" parties for whom Dun must preside over both xiang ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 且哀樂不相雜，吉凶不相干。

translations.literal: Moreover grief and joy do not mix—inauspicious and auspicious do not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover grief must not mingle with celebration, nor mourning with felicity.

sentences.zh: 凶服在宮，哭泣未絕。

translations.literal: Funeral dress in the palace—wailing not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral weeds still fill the palace and wails have not fallen silent.

sentences.zh: 敦遽主穆王之喪，而國制未除，則不得以己本親服除而吉祭獻王也。」

translations.literal: Dun hastily presides Prince Mu's mourning—yet state regulation not removed—then may not with his own kin garment removed perform auspicious sacrifice to Prince Xian."
translations.idiomatic: While Dun is abruptly directing Prince Mu's obsequies and the prescribed mourning is unfinished, he cannot shed mourning for his natural kin and turn to auspicious rites for Prince Xian."

sentences.zh: ，陳留國上，燕公是王之父，王出奉明帝祀，今于王為從父，有司奏應服期，不以親疏尊卑為降。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Chenliu state reported—the Duke of Yan is the king's father—the king went out to serve Emperor Ming's sacrifices—now toward the king [the duke] is congfu kin—the offices memorialized [the duke] ought wear qi (one full cycle) mourning—not lowering by kin distance or honor base.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu memorialized that the Duke of Yan was the king's natural father; once the king had been given to continue Emperor Ming's line, the duke counted only as a congfu relative. Officials proposed qi-grade mourning with no reduction for intimacy or rank.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「王奉魏氏，所承者重，不得服其私親。

translations.literal: Edict stated: "The king carries Wei house—the inheritance is weighty—may not wear for private kin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict refused: "The king upholds Wei ancestry under grave obligation; he cannot observe mourning for a private parent."

sentences.zh: 」穆帝時，東海國言，哀王薨逾年，嗣王乃來繼，不復追服，群臣皆已反吉，國妃亦宜同除。

translations.literal: " Under Emperor Mu, Donghai state reported—King Ai died over a year—then the successor king came to continue—did not retroactively wear mourning—all ministers already returned auspicious—the state's royal consort likewise ought remove together.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Emperor Mu, Donghai argued that King Ai had been dead more than a year before the heir arrived, so no retroactive mourning was worn; ministers had all returned to felicity garb, and the princess-consort should shed weeds as well.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朝廷所以從權制者，以王事奪之，非為變禮也。

translations.literal: Edict stated: "Why the court followed expedient regulation—because royal affairs seized them—not to alter the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered: "We shortened mourning only because state business overrode private duty—not to rewrite the canon."

sentences.zh: 婦人傳重義大，若從權制，義將安托！

translations.literal: Women's transmitting weight—right meaning is great—if following expedient regulation—where will right rest!
translations.idiomatic: Women who bear the ritual "weight" of heirship hold immense obligation—if we subject them to the same expedient, where does principle find footing?

sentences.zh: 」於是國妃終三年之禮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the state's royal consort completed three years' rites.
translations.idiomatic: The princess-consort therefore observed the full three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 孫盛以為：「廢三年之禮，開偷薄之源，漢魏失之大者也。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng held: "Abolishing three years' rites—opens source of stingy thinness—Han-Wei's great failure.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng thought waiving three-year mourning opened the floodgates to meanness—that was Han and Wei's gravest ritual lapse.

sentences.zh: 今若以大夫宜奪以王事。

translations.literal: Now if holding great officers ought be seized by royal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If we allow that grandees may be yanked from mourning by state business,

sentences.zh: 婦人可終本服，是吉凶之儀雜陳于宮寢，彩素之制乖異於內外，無乃情禮俱違，哀樂失所乎！」

translations.literal: women may complete proper garment—is this not auspicious and inauspicious observances mixed in palace chambers—bright and plain regulations contrary inner and outer—surely emotion and rites both violated—grief and joy lose their place!"
translations.idiomatic: yet women finish full mourning for kin, would we not parade mourning and felicity through the same inner chambers, clash bright dress with hemp inside and out, and undo both feeling and ritual until grief and joy lose their proper seats?"

sentences.zh: ，太常車胤上言：「謹案《喪服禮經》，庶子為母緦麻三月。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Chamberlain for Ceremonials Che Yin submitted: "Respectfully reviewing the Mourning Garments ritual classic—a son by concubine for mother [wears] si (fine hemp) three months.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin, chamberlain for ceremonials, cited the Mourning Garments classic: a concubine's son owes his mother only three months in si-grade hemp.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『何以緦麻？

translations.literal: The Commentary states: 'Why si?
translations.idiomatic: The subcommentary asks why si applies.

sentences.zh: 以尊者為體，不敢服其私親也。

translations.literal: Because one forms body with the honored—dare not wear for private kin.
translations.idiomatic: Because the heir is ritually one with his exalted father, he cannot wear heavy mourning for a private parent.

sentences.zh: 』此《經》《傳》之明文，聖賢之格言。

translations.literal: ' This is classic and commentary's clear text—sages' model words.
translations.idiomatic: That pairing of text and gloss is explicit scripture—language the sages meant as normative.

sentences.zh: 而自頃開國公侯，至於卿士，庶子為後，各肆私情，服其庶母，同之於嫡。

translations.literal: Yet from recently enfeoffed dukes and marquises down to ministers—sons by concubine who became heirs—each indulged private feeling—wore mourning for concubine-mothers—equating to legitimate mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately every enfeoffed noble down to senior ministers, once a concubine's son succeeded, indulged private affection and mourned a concubine-mother like a legal parent.

sentences.zh: 此末俗之弊，溺情傷教，縱而不革，則流遁忘返矣。

translations.literal: This is late custom's harm—drowning feeling injures teaching—if indulged and not reformed—then drift astray unable return.
translations.idiomatic: That late-born abuse drowns sentiment and wounds instruction; left unchecked, custom slides past recall.

sentences.zh: 且夫尊尊親親，雖禮之大本，然厭親于尊，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: Moreover honoring honor and kinning kin—though rites' great root—yet subordinating kin to honor—from antiquity esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring superiors and cherishing kin are the roots of ritual, yet subordinating private kin to public rank has been honored since high antiquity.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》曰，『為父後，出母無服也者，不祭故也』。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites states: 'Acting as father's heir—divorced mother no garment—because [one does] not sacrifice [to her] thereby.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says an heir to his father wears nothing for a divorced mother because he no longer sacrifices to her.

sentences.zh: 又，禮，天子父母之喪，未葬，越紼而祭天地社稷。

translations.literal: Moreover, by rites—Son of Heaven's father-mother mourning—not yet buried—step over rope-coffin and sacrifice to Heaven Earth soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Son of Heaven may vault the burial cord before interment and still offer to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 斯皆崇嚴至敬，不敢以私廢尊也。

translations.literal: These all exalt stern utmost reverence—dare not with private discard honor.
translations.idiomatic: Such acts exalt awe before public cult—never letting private grief scrap obligations to the supreme powers.

sentences.zh: 今身承祖宗之重，而以庶母之私，廢烝嘗之事。

translations.literal: Now personally bearing ancestors' weight—yet with concubine-mother's private—abolish zheng-offering and chang-offering affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Today heirs shoulder ancestral temples yet scrap winter and autumn offerings for a concubine mother's sake.

sentences.zh: 五廟闕祀，由一妾之終，求之情禮，失莫大焉。

translations.literal: Five temples lack sacrifice—because one concubine's end—seek in emotion and rites—failure none greater.
translations.idiomatic: Five shrines miss sacrifice because one concubine died—by any measure of feeling or ritual, the harm could hardly be worse.

sentences.zh: 舉世皆然，莫之裁貶。

translations.literal: Whole age thus—none trims or faults it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone does it; nobody reins it in.

sentences.zh: 就心不同，而事不敢異。

translations.literal: In heart disagree—but in deed dare not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Men may dissent inwardly yet dare not break step in public.

sentences.zh: 故正禮遂穨，而習非成俗。

translations.literal: Hence correct rites thus crumble—and habit wrong becomes custom.
translations.idiomatic: Thus orthodox ritual collapses while repeated error hardens into custom.

sentences.zh: 此《國風》所以思古，《小雅》所以悲歎。

translations.literal: This is why Airs of the States longs for antiquity—why Lesser Odes laments.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the Airs of the States sigh for ancient ways and the Lesser Odes pour out their grief.

sentences.zh: 當今九服漸甯，王化惟新，誠宜崇明禮訓，以一風俗。

translations.literal: Now the nine domains gradually pacified—kingly transformation anew—truly fitting exalt bright ritual instruction—to unify customs.
translations.idiomatic: With the nine circuits calming and royal influence renewing, it is time to lift bright ritual teaching and knit the realm into one custom.

sentences.zh: 請臺省考修經典，式明王度。

translations.literal: Request terrace and provincial offices examine and revise classics—to pattern-clarify kingly measure.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the central departments to collate the classics and codify them so the kingly norm shines clear.

sentences.zh: 」不答。

translations.literal: Closing the quoted memorial—no reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The court returned no answer.

sentences.zh: 十八年，胤又上言：「去年上，自頃開國公侯，至於卿士，庶子為後者，服其庶母，同之於嫡，違禮犯制，宜加裁抑。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Yin again submitted words: "Last year I submitted—since recently founding-state dukes and marquises down to ministers and gentlemen—those secondary sons who become heirs—they observe mourning for their secondary mothers—as equal to the principal mother—violating ritual and infringing regulation—fitting to add curbing restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Yin again memorialized: "My petition last year noted that, from the founding ranks onward—dukes and marquises down to senior officials—heirs born of secondary consorts have been mourning their birth mothers on the same footing as a principal mother. That breaches canonical mourning law and ought to be restrained.

sentences.zh: 事上經年，未被告報，未審朝議以何為疑。

translations.literal: The matter has been on file a full year—yet no notification has come—I do not know what doubt the court deliberation harbors.
translations.idiomatic: A year has passed since it went up, yet no ruling has come down; I cannot tell what hesitation keeps the council silent.

sentences.zh: 若以所陳或謬，則經有文；

translations.literal: If because what was stated perhaps errs—then the classics have the wording;
translations.idiomatic: If my argument is mistaken, the canon itself supplies the text;

sentences.zh: 若以古今不同，則晉有成典。

translations.literal: If because ancient and present differ—then Jin has established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: If the objection is that antiquity and today diverge, Jin already has binding precedent.

sentences.zh: 升平四年，故太宰武陵王所生母喪，表求齊衰三年，詔聽依昔樂安王故事，制大功九月。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shengping—the late Grand Tutor Prince of Wuling's birth mother died—he memorialized requesting zīcuī for three years—the edict permitted him to follow the former Prince of Le'an precedent—regulating greater felicitous mourning at nine months.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengping 4, when the birth mother of the late Grand Tutor, the Prince of Wuling, died, he petitioned for three years in trimmed sackcloth; the throne allowed him to follow the old Prince of Le'an precedent and fixed greater mourning at nine months.

sentences.zh: ，故梁王㻱又所生母喪，亦求三年。

translations.literal: —therefore when the Prince of Liang, Jin, lost his birth mother—he too requested three years.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise, when the Prince of Liang, Jin, lost his birth mother, he too sought three full years.

sentences.zh: 《庚子詔書》依太宰故事，同服大功。

translations.literal: The Gēngzǐ Edict Document followed the Grand Tutor precedent—likewise prescribing greater felicitous mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Gēngzǐ edict followed the Grand Tutor precedent and likewise prescribed nine months of greater mourning.

sentences.zh: 若謹案周禮，則緦麻三月；

translations.literal: If one carefully examines the Rites of Zhou—then finest hemp is three months;
translations.idiomatic: Strictly applying the Zhou canon would mean only three months in finest hemp;

sentences.zh: 若奉晉制，則大功九月。

translations.literal: If one upholds Jin's regulation—then greater felicitous mourning is nine months.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin's own statute, it is nine months of greater mourning.

sentences.zh: 古禮今制，並無居廬三年之文，而頃年已來，各申私情，更相擬襲，漸以成俗。

translations.literal: Ancient ritual and present regulation together lack any text authorizing three years in the mourning hut—yet in recent years already come—each voices private feeling—mutually imitating and inheriting—gradually thereby becoming custom.
translations.idiomatic: Neither classical ritual nor current codes authorize three years in the mourning hut; yet lately everyone pleads private feeling, copies one another, and the practice is hardening into habit.

sentences.zh: 縱而不禁，則聖典滅矣。

translations.literal: If indulged and not forbidden—then the sagely canon is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: If we indulge it and never curb it, the sagely canon will be hollowed out.

sentences.zh: 夫尊尊親親，立人之本，王化所由，二端而已。

translations.literal: Now honoring the honored and cherishing the cherished—establishing people's root—kingly transformation whereby—it is these two ends only.
translations.idiomatic: Reverence for rank and affection for kin are the twin foundations of human order and the springs of royal transformation—nothing beyond these two.

sentences.zh: 故先王設教，務弘其極，尊郊社之敬，制越紼之禮，嚴宗廟之祀，厭庶子之服，所以經緯人文，化成天下。

translations.literal: Therefore former kings established teaching—striving to enlarge its utmost—honoring reverence for the suburban and soil altars—regulating the ritual of vaulting the funeral cords—strictening ancestral temple sacrifices—suppressing what secondary heirs may wear for birth parents—thereby warp-and-wefting human patterns—transforming and completing all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the ancient kings framed instruction to carry each principle to its limit: they magnified reverence for suburban and soil altars, set rules for vaulting the funeral cords, tightened ancestral worship, and bridled what secondary heirs might wear for birth parents—thus ordering civilization's warp and weft until the realm was shaped.

sentences.zh: 夫屈家事于王道，厭私恩於祖宗，豈非上行乎下，父行乎子！

translations.literal: Now bending family affairs to the kingly way—suppressing private grace toward ancestors—is this not the high acting upon the low—the father acting upon the son!
translations.idiomatic: To subordinate household sentiment to the kingly norm and set private tenderness beneath ancestral duty—is that not precisely how what is high trains what is low, and fathers train sons?

sentences.zh: 若尊尊之心有時而替，宜厭之情觸事而申，祖宗之敬微，而君臣之禮虧矣。

translations.literal: If the mind that honors hierarchy falters at times—while the feeling fit for suppression swells whenever affairs arise—reverence for ancestors grows subtle—then the ritual between lord and minister is impaired.
translations.idiomatic: Once reverence for hierarchy falters and disciplined restraint swells at every turn of feeling, respect for forebears thins and the ritual bond between ruler and minister erodes.

sentences.zh: 嚴恪微於祖宗，致敬虧於事上，而欲俗安化隆，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Strict reverence toward ancestors grows subtle—extended reverence toward serving superiors is impaired—yet one desires customs pacified and transformation lofty—is this not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: When solemn duty toward the ancestors fades and dutiful deference to superiors frays, can customs settle and transformation flourish? Surely that is hard.

sentences.zh: 區區所惜，實在於斯。

translations.literal: What I regret in my meager way truly lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: What troubles me, slight though my voice may be, is precisely this.

sentences.zh: 職之所司，不敢不言。

translations.literal: What my office oversees—I dare not fail to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The office I hold leaves me no silence.

sentences.zh: 請臺參詳。

translations.literal: I request the terrace offices to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: I ask the supreme departments to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 」尚書奏：「案如辭輒下主者詳尋。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "Investigate as the wording states—then dispatch it to the responsible overseers for thorough inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat reported: "As the wording requests, forward this at once to the responsible offices for thorough inquiry.

sentences.zh: 依禮，庶子與尊者為體，不敢服其私親，此尊祖敬宗之義。

translations.literal: According to ritual, the secondary son shares one body with the exalted predecessor—he dares not observe mourning for his private kin—this is the meaning of honoring ancestors and revering the main line.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual a secondary heir shares one body with his exalted predecessor and therefore does not wear mourning for his own birth parent—that is how one honors forebears and reveres the main line.

sentences.zh: 自頃陵遲，斯禮遂廢。

translations.literal: Since recently standards have declined—this ritual has then been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Of late, as standards slackened, that rule fell away.

sentences.zh: 封國之君廢五廟之重，士庶匹夫闕烝嘗之禮，習成穨俗，宜被革正。

translations.literal: Lords of enfeoffed states abandon the weight of the five temples—gentlemen and commoners lack the steam-and-taste offerings—practice completes a decadent custom—fitting that it receive reform and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords neglect the gravity of the five shrines; commoners omit seasonal offerings at home—habit has rotted into custom and ought to be cleaned up.

sentences.zh: 輒內外參詳，謂宜聽胤所上，可依樂安王大功為正。

translations.literal: We have consulted inside and outside—we deem it fitting to accept what Yin submitted—one may rely on the Prince of Le'an's greater felicitous mourning as standard.
translations.idiomatic: After consulting court and ministries, we hold that Yin's petition should be accepted and the Prince of Le'an precedent—nine months of greater mourning—should be taken as normative.

sentences.zh: 請為告書如左，班下內外，以定永制，普令依承，事可奉行。

translations.literal: We request drafting a proclamation document as at left—distributing it through court and countryside—to fix a perpetual regulation—universally ordering compliance—so the affair may be enacted and followed.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that an edict be drafted along the lines below, circulated through court and countryside to settle the standing rule, enjoin universal compliance, and put the matter into practice.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 《禮》，王為三公六卿錫衰，為大夫士疑衰，首服弁絰。

translations.literal: The Canon of Rites: the king wears smooth sackcloth for the Three Dukes and the six ministers, doubtful sackcloth for great officers and gentlemen, with cap and forehead cord as headgear.
translations.idiomatic: The Canon of Rites prescribes that the king wear smooth sackcloth for the Three Dukes and six ministers, doubtful sackcloth for great officers and gentlemen, with cap and forehead cord.

sentences.zh: 天子諸侯皆為貴臣貴妾服三月。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike observe three months' mourning for honored ministers and honored concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike observe three months' mourning for favored ministers and favored concubines.

sentences.zh: 漢為大臣制服無聞焉。

translations.literal: For Han, regulating mourning garments for great ministers—nothing is heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: Han sources record no fixed mourning wardrobe for great ministers.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝時，東海恭王薨，帝出幸津門亭發哀。

translations.literal: In the time of Han Mingdi, the Respectful Prince of the Eastern Sea died—the emperor went out to the Ferry Gate pavilion to voice grief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Mingdi, when the Respectful Prince of the Eastern Sea died, the emperor travelled to the Ferry Gate pavilion to voice grief.

sentences.zh: 及武帝十一月，詔「諸王公大臣薨，應三朝發哀者，逾月不舉樂，其一朝發哀者，三日不舉樂也」。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor Wu, in the eleventh month, an edict declared: "When various kings, dukes, and great ministers die—those who ought to observe mourning at three successive audiences—for more than a month they shall not raise music—those who observe mourning at one audience—for three days they shall not raise music."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Emperor Wu's reign an edict declared: "When kings, dukes, or senior ministers die, those who observe mourning at three successive audiences shall refrain from music for more than a month; those who mourn at only one audience shall refrain for three days."

sentences.zh: 元帝姨廣昌鄉君喪，未葬，中丞熊遠表云：「案《禮》『君于卿大夫，比葬不食肉，比卒哭不舉樂』，惻隱之心未忍行吉事故也。

translations.literal: When Yuan-di's aunt the Village Mistress of Guangchang died—not yet buried—Palace Assistant Xiong Yuan memorialized, stating: "I investigate the Rites: 'Toward ministers and great officers, until burial the ruler eats no meat; until the end of staged wailing he performs no music'—because the heart of compassion cannot bear to conduct auspicious affairs."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan-di's aunt, the Village Mistress of Guangchang, died and lay unburied, Palace Assistant Xiong Yuan submitted: "The Rites teach that until burial the ruler eats no meat for his ministers and until the end of staged wailing performs no music—because lingering pity forbids auspicious display."

sentences.zh: 被尚書符，冬至後二日小會。

translations.literal: We have received a Ministry tally—calling a minor gathering two days after the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we have received a Ministry directive calling a minor court gathering two days after the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 臣以為廣昌鄉君喪殯日，聖恩垂悼。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that on the encoffining days of the Village Mistress of Guangchang—sagely grace already hangs over her grief.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that while the lady still lies in mourning hall, imperial sympathy already attends her.

sentences.zh: 禮，大夫死，廢一時之祭。

translations.literal: By ritual, when a great officer dies—one seasonal sacrifice is suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual suspends one seasonal sacrifice when a great officer dies.

sentences.zh: 祭猶可廢，而況餘事。

translations.literal: Sacrifices may still be suspended—how much more other affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If even sacrifices may halt, how much more lesser observances.

sentences.zh: 冬至唯可群下奉賀而已，未便小會。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice it is only fitting that hosts below offer congratulations—that is all—not yet fitting to hold a minor gathering.
translations.idiomatic: The solstice should bring nothing beyond congratulations from officials; a banquet is premature.

sentences.zh: 」詔以遠表示賀循，又曰：「武皇帝故事云『王公大臣薨，三朝發哀，逾月不舉樂，其一朝發哀，三日不舉樂』，此舊事明文。

translations.literal: The edict forwarded Xiong Yuan's memorial to He Xun and added: "Emperor Wu's precedent states: 'When kings, dukes, or great ministers die—three audiences of mourning—for more than a month no music is raised—those with one audience of mourning—for three days no music is raised'—this old affair has clear wording.
translations.idiomatic: The throne forwarded Xiong Yuan's memorial to He Xun and added: "Emperor Wu's precedent reads: 'When kings, dukes, or great ministers die, three audiences of mourning mean no music for more than a month; a single audience means three days without music'—that ancient ruling is explicit.

sentences.zh: 」賀循答曰：「案《禮·雜記》，『君于卿大夫之喪，比葬不食肉，比卒哭不舉樂』。

translations.literal: He Xun answered, stating: "I investigate the Miscellaneous Record of the Rites: 'For the bereavement of ministers and great officers—until burial the ruler eats no meat—until the end of staged wailing he performs no music.'"
translations.idiomatic: He Xun replied: "The Miscellaneous Record of the Rites says: 'For the death of ministers and great officers the ruler eats no meat until burial and performs no music until the end of staged wailing.'"

sentences.zh: 古者君臣義重，雖以至尊之義，降而無服，三月之內，猶錫衰以居，不接吉事。

translations.literal: In antiquity the righteousness between lord and minister was weighty—although by the utmost-venerated ritual principle mourning was lowered so there was no garment—within three months—smooth sackcloth was still worn at court—auspicious affairs were not joined.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity weighted the bond between ruler and minister so heavily that even when ritual "lowered" mourning to none, the sovereign still wore smooth sackcloth for three months and kept clear of joyous business.

sentences.zh: 故春秋晉大夫智悼子未葬，平公作樂，為屠蒯所譏。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Spring and Autumn annals, when the Jin great officer Zhi Daozi was not yet buried—Duke Ping ordered music—and was ridiculed by Tu Kuai.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in the Spring and Autumn annals, when Duke Ping of Jin ordered music while Minister Zhi Daozi still lay unburied, Tu Kuai rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 如遠所答，合于古義。

translations.literal: As Xiong Yuan answered—it matches ancient righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan's argument answers to classical meaning.

sentences.zh: 咸寧詔書雖不會經典，然隨時立宜，以為定制，誠非群下所得稱論。

translations.literal: Although the Xiánning edict document does not tally with the classics—yet it established what fitted its time—making it fixed regulation—truly not something hosts below may weigh and debate.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiánning edict may not tally with every canonical line, yet it was framed for its moment and has become binding statute—not something subordinates may debate away.

sentences.zh: 」，帝姑廬陵公主未葬，符問太常，冬至小會應作樂不。

translations.literal: When the emperor's aunt the Princess of Luling was not yet buried—a tally asked the Grand Master of Ceremonies whether at the winter solstice minor gathering music ought to be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while the emperor's aunt, the Princess of Luling, remained unburied, a directive asked the Grand Master of Ceremonies whether music should sound at the winter-solstice gathering.

sentences.zh: 博士胡訥議云：「君于卿大夫，比卒哭不舉樂。

translations.literal: Erudite Hu Ne deliberated, stating: "Toward ministers and great officers—until the end of staged wailing music is not raised.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Hu Ne argued: "Until the end of staged wailing the ruler performs no music for ministers and great officers.

sentences.zh: 公主有骨肉之親，宜闕樂。

translations.literal: The princess has bone-and-flesh kinship—music fittingly should be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: A princess is flesh and blood; music should be withheld.

sentences.zh: 」太常王彪之云：「案武帝詔，三朝舉哀，三旬乃舉樂；

translations.literal: Grand Master Wang Biaozhi stated: "I investigate Emperor Wu's edict—three audiences of mourning—for three ten-day cycles then music is raised;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi of the Grand Master office countered: "Emperor Wu's edict says three audiences of mourning delay music for three decadal cycles;

sentences.zh: 其一朝舉哀者，三日則舉樂。

translations.literal: those with one audience of mourning—after three days then music is raised.
translations.idiomatic: a single audience lifts the ban after three days.

sentences.zh: 春，長樂長公主薨，秋，扶風王駿薨，武帝並舉哀三日而已。

translations.literal: In spring the Elder Princess of Changle died—in autumn Prince Jun of Fufeng died—Emperor Wu together observed mourning three days only.
translations.idiomatic: In spring the Elder Princess of Changle died; in autumn Prince Jun of Fufeng died—Emperor Wu mourned each for three days only.

sentences.zh: 中興已後，更參論不改此制。

translations.literal: After the restoration—consultation and debate again did not alter this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Since the restoration the court has reviewed the matter repeatedly without changing that rule.

sentences.zh: 今小會宜作樂。

translations.literal: Now for the minor gathering it is fitting to perform music.
translations.idiomatic: Music at today's gathering is therefore appropriate.

sentences.zh: 」二議竟不知所取。

translations.literal: In the end the two deliberations did not settle which to take.
translations.idiomatic: The two opinions never settled which to follow.

sentences.zh: 《喪服記》，公為所寓，齊衰三月。

translations.literal: The Record of Mourning Dress: the duke for one who lodged him—trimmed sackcloth three months.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Mourning Dress says a duke wears three months of trimmed sackcloth for one who lodged him.

sentences.zh: 新禮以今無此事，除此一章。

translations.literal: The New Rites, because today this affair does not occur—removed this one chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites dropped the chapter, judging the case obsolete.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「《周禮》作于刑厝之時，而著荒政十二。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu deemed: "The Rites of Zhou were composed when punishments lay dormant—yet they record twelve famine-relief policies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued: "The Rites of Zhou were compiled when punishments lay dormant, yet they still codified twelve relief measures for famine.

sentences.zh: 禮備制待物，不以時衰而除盛典，世隆而闕衰教也。

translations.literal: Ritual completes regulations to await things—not because the age declines thereby removing grand ceremonies—nor because the age is lofty thereby omitting mourning teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual completes institutions to meet every contingency; one does not strike great ceremonies merely because the age declines, nor abandon mourning instruction merely because the age flourishes.

sentences.zh: 曩者王司徒失守播越，自稱寄公。

translations.literal: Formerly Minister Wang lost his defense and was scattered in flight—calling himself a lodged duke.
translations.idiomatic: Once Minister Wang lost his command and fled, styling himself a guest lord.

sentences.zh: 是時天下又多此比，皆禮之所及。

translations.literal: At that time all under heaven again had many of this sort—all are what ritual reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Many in the realm stood in like case—precisely what ritual addresses.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮自如舊經。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites to accord with the old classics.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites ought to be settled to match the old canon.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事無五等諸侯之制，公卿朝士服喪，親疏各如其親。

translations.literal: Han and Wei precedent lacked the institution of five-ranked feudal lords—dukes, ministers, and court gentlemen observed mourning—near or distant each according to actual kin.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei precedent knew no five-tier nobility; dukes, ministers, and courtiers mourned according to actual kinship.

sentences.zh: 新禮王公五等諸侯成國置卿者，及朝廷公孤之爵，皆傍親絕期，而旁親為之服斬衰，卿校位從大夫者皆絕緦。

translations.literal: The New Rites: kings, dukes, five-ranked feudal lords who completed a state and installed ministers—and court ranks of duke and orphan—all collateral kin sever one-year mourning—yet collateral kin for them wear deepest mourning—ministerial officers whose rank follows great officers all sever finest-hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites would cut collateral ties at one year for kings, dukes, and five-tier lords who founded states with ministers, and for dukes and orphans at court—yet demand those collaterals wear deepest mourning for them, and sever even finest-hemp mourning for ministerial officers ranked with great officers.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「古者諸侯君臨其國，臣諸父兄，今之諸侯未同于古。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu deemed: "Ancient feudal lords lorded over their states—treating fathers and elder brothers as ministers—present feudal lords are not the same as antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued: "Ancient feudal lords truly ruled their domains and treated uncles and elder brothers as ministers; today's nobles are not their peers.

sentences.zh: 未同于古，則其尊未全，不宜便從絕期之制，而令傍親服斬衰之重也。

translations.literal: Not the same as antiquity—then their honored standing is not complete—not fitting abruptly to follow the regulation that severs one-year mourning—yet order collateral kin to wear the weight of deepest mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Because they lack that stature, their ritual supremacy is incomplete; they should not abruptly adopt the rule that severs one-year mourning while forcing collaterals into deepest mourning for them.

sentences.zh: 諸侯既然，則公孤之爵亦宜如舊。

translations.literal: Since feudal lords are thus—then ranks of duke and orphan also fittingly should be as before.
translations.idiomatic: The same holds for dukes and orphans; let them follow earlier practice.

sentences.zh: 昔魏武帝建安中已曾表上，漢朝依古為制，事與古異，皆不施行，施行者著在魏科。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Wei in the Jiàn'ān era already once memorialized upward—the Han court according to antiquity made regulation—the affairs differed from antiquity—all were not enacted—what was enacted is recorded in Wei statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Emperor Wu of Wei petitioned in the Jiàn'an era; Han tried to legislate on classical lines, found the cases unlike antiquity, and let the scheme lapse—what survived entered Wei law.

sentences.zh: 大晉采以著令，宜定新禮皆如舊。

translations.literal: Great Jin adopted this to establish ordinance—it is fitting to fix the New Rites entirely as the old.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin incorporated those provisions; the New Rites should be reset to match them.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 《喪服》無弟子為師服之制，新禮弟子為師齊衰三月。

translations.literal: Mourning Dress lacks any regulation for disciples mourning teachers—the New Rites prescribed disciples mourning teachers trimmed sackcloth three months.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning Dress prescribes no mourning for a teacher; the New Rites imposed three months of trimmed sackcloth.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「自古無師服之制，故仲尼之喪，門人疑于所服。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu deemed: "From antiquity there has been no regulation for mourning teachers—therefore at Zhongni's bereavement disciples doubted what to wear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu noted that antiquity fixed no teacher-mourning; hence Confucius's disciples puzzled over what to wear.

sentences.zh: 子貢曰：『昔夫子之喪顏回，若喪子而無服，請喪夫子若喪父而無服。

translations.literal: Zigong stated: 'Formerly when the Master mourned Yan Hui—it was like mourning a son yet without garments—I request mourning the Master like mourning a father yet without garments.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong said, 'When the Master mourned Yan Hui he grieved like a father yet wore no mourning dress; I ask to mourn the Master as I would a father but likewise without prescribed garments.'

sentences.zh: 』遂心喪三年。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon they observed heart-mourning three years.
translations.idiomatic: ' They therefore observed three years of heart-mourning.

sentences.zh: 此則懷三年之哀，而無齊衰之制也。

translations.literal: This then cherishes three years of grief—yet lacks the trimmed-sackcloth regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they bore three years of grief without the formal trimmed-sackcloth regimen.

sentences.zh: 群居，入則絰，出則否，所謂弔服加麻也。

translations.literal: Dwelling in a group—entering then cord—exiting then not—this is what is called condolence garb with hemp added.
translations.idiomatic: Living together, they donned hemp cords indoors and doffed them outdoors—the so-called mourning garb with added hemp.

sentences.zh: 先聖為禮，必易從而可傳。

translations.literal: Former sages made ritual—it must be easy to follow and possible to transmit.
translations.idiomatic: The sages fashioned ritual to be easy to follow and easy to hand down.

sentences.zh: 師徒義誠重，而服制不著，歷代相襲，不以為缺。

translations.literal: Teacher and disciple righteousness is truly heavy—yet garment regulation is not manifest—successive ages mutually inherited—not deeming it a deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Master and pupil mean much, yet no mourning wardrobe was codified; dynasty after dynasty accepted the silence without calling it a flaw.

sentences.zh: 且尋師者以彌高為得，故屢遷而不嫌；

translations.literal: Moreover those who seek teachers take ever higher attainment as gain—therefore they shift repeatedly without dislike;
translations.idiomatic: Seekers of teachers prize ever loftier instruction, so they change masters without shame;

sentences.zh: 修業者以日新為益，故舍舊而不疑。

translations.literal: those who cultivate learning take daily renewal as benefit—therefore they abandon the old without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: students who pursue improvement welcome each day's novelty and leave former teachers without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 仲尼稱『三人行，必有我師焉』。

translations.literal: Zhongni praised 'Three persons walking—there must be my teacher therein.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'In any trio walking by, there is surely my teacher.'

sentences.zh: 子貢云，『夫何常師之有』。

translations.literal: Zigong stated—'Now what fixed teacher is there?'
translations.idiomatic: Zigong added, 'Who keeps one fixed master forever?'

sentences.zh: 淺學之師，暫學之師，不可皆為之服。

translations.literal: Teachers of shallow learning—teachers of brief learning—not possible for all to observe mourning for them.
translations.idiomatic: Casual tutors and brief instructors cannot all merit full mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 義有輕重，服有廢興，則臧否由之而起，是非因之而爭，愛惡相攻，悔吝生焉。

translations.literal: When righteousness has light and heavy—and garments have abandonment and revival—then praise and blame arise thereby—right and wrong contend thereby—love and hate attack each other—regret and shame are born therein.
translations.idiomatic: Where obligation varies and garments rise or fall, praise and blame ignite, right and wrong quarrel, liking and loathing clash, and regret follows.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮無服如舊。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites—no garments—as the old.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites should revert to the old silence—no prescribed mourning.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict agreed.

sentences.zh: 古者天子諸侯葬禮粗備，漢世又多變革，魏晉以下世有改變，大體同漢之制。

translations.literal: In antiquity Son of Heaven and feudal lords' burial rites were roughly complete—the Han age again had many changes—from Wei and Jin downward generations had alterations—the great outline largely matched Han regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity gave Son of Heaven and nobles a rough burial code; Han reworked it often; Wei and Jin kept tweaking, yet the outline still followed Han.

sentences.zh: 而魏武以禮送終之制，襲稱之數，繁而無益，俗又過之，豫自制送終衣服四篋，題識其上，春秋冬夏，日有不諱，隨時以斂。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Wu of Wei deemed ritual regulations for sending off the dead—the inherited titles and tallies—numerous yet without benefit—custom again surpassed them—beforehand he himself made send-off garments four chests—inscribed marks on their tops—spring, autumn, winter, summer—when the day held no taboo—following the season thereby to encoffin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei judged funeral ritual bloated with pointless inherited titles; popular excess made it worse. He prepared four chests of burial clothes in advance, labeled them for the seasons, and ordered that whenever death came, whatever the season, he be dressed from those stores.

sentences.zh: 金珥珠玉銅鐵之物，一不得送。

translations.literal: Things of gold ear-rings pearl jade copper iron—not one may be sent along.
translations.idiomatic: Not a single article of gold, jeweled earpieces, jade, copper, or iron might accompany him.

sentences.zh: 文帝遵奉，無所增加。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen obeyed and upheld—nothing was increased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen adhered without adding.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，刻金璽，追加尊號，不敢開埏，乃為石室，藏璽埏首，以示陵中無金銀諸物也。

translations.literal: When it came to receiving the abdication—a gold seal was carved—posthumous honor was added—he dared not open the tomb slope—thereupon made a stone chamber—hid the seal at the tomb-head—to show that inside the mausoleum there were no gold or silver objects.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the abdication he had a gold seal cut and posthumous honors added, yet feared opening the slope; he built a stone niche at the entrance and sealed the cipher there to show the mound held no gold or silver.

sentences.zh: 漢禮明器甚多，自是皆省之矣。

translations.literal: Han ritual spirit-objects were very many—from this onward all were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Han tombs had brimmed with grave goods; from then on those were pared back.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝，又自作終制曰：「禮，國君即位為椑，存不忘亡也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei—again himself composed end instructions stating: "Ritual—a state lord at accession makes the inner coffin—existing does not forget perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei also drafted final instructions: "Ritual demands that a ruler have his inner coffin readied at accession—the living must remember dying.

sentences.zh: 壽陵因山為體，無封樹，無立寢殿，造園邑，通神道。

translations.literal: The Shou mausoleum relies on the mountain as its body—no mound or trees—no erecting resting halls—building garden settlements—opening spirit roads.
translations.idiomatic: My barrow at Shou will hug the hill without mound-markers or trees, without resting halls, garden towns, or spirit ways cut through.

sentences.zh: 夫葬者藏也，欲人之不得見也。

translations.literal: Now burial is hiding—it desires that people not obtain sight.
translations.idiomatic: Burial means concealment; it must hide the dead from sight.

sentences.zh: 禮不墓祭，欲存亡不黷也。

translations.literal: Ritual does not sacrifice at the tomb—it desires that neither the living nor the dead be profaned.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual forbids tomb-side sacrifice so neither living nor dead suffer violation.

sentences.zh: 皇后及貴人以下不隨王之國者，有終沒，皆葬澗西，前又已表其處矣。

translations.literal: Empresses and honored ladies below who do not follow the prince to his state—when they end and die—all are buried west of the stream—I have already earlier marked their place.
translations.idiomatic: Empresses and concubines who do not travel to princely domains will, when they die, all be buried west of the stream—I have already noted the site.

sentences.zh: 」此詔藏之宗廟，副在尚書、秘書、三府。

translations.literal: This edict store it in the ancestral temple—copies at the Ministry, the Palace Library, and the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered this edict deposited in the ancestral shrine with copies at the Secretariat, the Palace Library, and the three chief ministries.

sentences.zh: 明帝亦遵奉之。

translations.literal: Mingdi also obeyed and upheld it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi likewise obeyed.

sentences.zh: 明帝性雖崇奢，然未遽營陵墓之制也。

translations.literal: Although Mingdi's nature esteemed extravagance—yet he did not hastily undertake expanding mausoleum-hill regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mingdi loved splendor, he still refrained from rashly expanding tomb ritual.

sentences.zh: 宣帝豫自于首陽山為土藏，不填不樹，作《顧命終制》，斂以時服，不設明器。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan beforehand on Mount Shouyang made an earthen store—no filling mound no trees—composed the Testamentary Resting Instructions—encoffined in timely garments—did not install spirit-objects.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan prepared an earthen repository at Mount Shouyang—no raised mound, no marker trees—writing his Testamentary Resting Instructions to be dressed in daily clothes and buried without grave goods.

sentences.zh: 景、文皆謹奉成命，無所加焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing and Emperor Wen both scrupulously upheld the settled testamentary commands, adding nothing further.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao both faithfully carried out the late emperor's completed instructions, neither amplifying nor altering them.

sentences.zh: 景帝崩，喪事制度又依宣帝故事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing died, the regulations for the funeral observances again followed Emperor Xuan's precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Upon the death of Emperor Jing, mourning protocol once more adhered to the model set under Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 武帝，文明王皇后崩，將合葬，開崇陽陵，使太尉司馬望奉祭，進皇帝密璽綬于便房神坐。

translations.literal: When Empress Wang the Cultured and Enlightened of Emperor Wu died, as she was to be buried with him they opened Chongyang Mausoleum, sent Grand Commandant Sima Wang to present the offerings, and advanced the emperor's sealed seal and ribbons to the spirit seat in the side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wang the Cultured and Enlightened—consort of Emperor Wu—died and was to join him in the tomb, workers opened Chongyang Mausoleum; Grand Commandant Sima Wang performed the sacrifice; and the imperial jade seal and cords, still sealed, were set before the spirit throne in the tomb vestibule.

sentences.zh: 魏氏金璽，此又儉矣。

translations.literal: The Wei dynasty's golden seal—this too marked austerity.
translations.idiomatic: Resorting to the Wei gold seal was itself another gesture of frugality.

sentences.zh: 江左初，元、明崇儉，且百度草創，山陵奉終，省約備矣。

translations.literal: Early on the south bank of the Yangzi, Emperors Yuan and Ming honored thrift; moreover, as every institution was still being founded, provisions for imperial tombs and laying the dead to rest were altogether spare and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding decades south of the Yangzi, Emperors Yuan and Ming prized simplicity; with the machinery of state still nascent, imperial burial practice was correspondingly lean and restrained.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸康七年，皇后杜氏崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh Xiankang year of Emperor Cheng, Empress Du died.
translations.idiomatic: In 341 CE—the seventh year of the Xiankang era—Empress Du passed away.

sentences.zh: 詔外官五日一入臨，內官旦一入而已，過葬虞祭禮畢止。

translations.literal: An edict [ordered]: outer officials to enter collective mourning once every five days, inner officials only once each dawn; after burial, when the Yu offerings were finished, it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: A decree directed officials outside the palace to join mourning audiences every five days, and those within only once each morning; the schedule ended once interment and the subsequent Yu rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，大行皇后陵所作凶門柏歷門，號顯陽端門。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: at the late empress's mausoleum they had fashioned the 'ominous gate' of cypress timbers, styling it the formal gate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported that for the late empress's tomb they had erected the ritual cypress "death gate," designated as the main portal of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「門如所處。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'The gate—allow it as sited.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded: "The gate may stand where you have placed it."

sentences.zh: 凶門柏歷，大為煩費，停之。

translations.literal: The ominous gate of cypress timbers was greatly troublesome and costly; stop it.
translations.idiomatic: The elaborate cypress death gate, however, would have meant prohibitive labor and expense; that portion of the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 」案蔡謨說，以二瓦器盛始死之祭，繫於木，裹以葦席，置庭中，近南，名為重，今之凶門是其象也。

translations.literal: " Investigating Cai Mo's explanation: they used two pottery vessels to hold offerings for the newly deceased, tied them to wood, wrapped them in reed matting, set them in the courtyard toward the south, and called this chong; today's ominous gate is its likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo explained that two earthenware vessels, filled with offerings for the newly dead, were lashed to a wooden frame, swathed in reed mats, and set toward the south of the courtyard—this was the chong; the contemporary "death gate" imitates that form.

sentences.zh: 禮，既虞而作主，今未葬，未有主，故以重當之。

translations.literal: By the rites, after the Yu ceremony they fashion the spirit tablet; now she was not yet buried and there was no tablet; therefore they used the chong in its stead.
translations.idiomatic: Canon prescribes carving the spirit tablet only after the Yu sacrifice; with burial still pending and no tablet yet installed, the chong temporarily stood in for it.

sentences.zh: 禮稱為主道，此其義也。

translations.literal: The rites term this 'the way of the spirit tablet'; such is its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The classical texts call this the proper sequence leading to the principal tablet—that is the underlying rationale.

sentences.zh: 范堅又曰：「凶門非禮，禮有懸重，形似凶門。

translations.literal: Fan Jian also said: 'The ominous gate is not in the rites; the rites have the suspended chong, whose shape resembles the ominous gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jian added that the freestanding "death gate" has no classical warrant; what the canon knows is the suspended chong, whose silhouette merely resembles later death gates.

sentences.zh: 後人出之門外以表喪，俗遂行之。

translations.literal: Later people moved it outside the gate to display mourning; custom then practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations transferred the structure beyond the gateway as an outward emblem of bereavement, and the usage hardened into folk practice.

sentences.zh: 薄帳，即古弔幕之類也。

translations.literal: Thin curtains—they are of the kind of the ancient mourning canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The light draperies belong to the same family of funerary screens used in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 」是時，又詔曰：「重壤之下，豈宜崇飾無用，陵中唯潔掃而已。

translations.literal: " At that time there was again an edict: 'Beneath heaped earth—how should useless ornament be glorified? Within the mausoleum, only clean sweeping.'
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared that deep underground there must be no ostentatious clutter—only a swept chamber worthy of the dead.

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏，依舊選公卿以下六品子弟六十人為挽郎，詔又停之。

translations.literal: " The offices again memorialized: according to precedent select sixty sons of nobles and officials from the highest ranks down through the sixth grade as pallbearers; an edict again suspended it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry repeated the old request for sixty noble youths of sixth rank or higher to serve as pallbearers; again the throne withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝九月，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Empress Wang passed away.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「終事唯從儉速。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Bringing the observances to an end—only follow frugality and dispatch.'
translations.idiomatic: He commanded that the funeral conclude with utmost economy and speed.

sentences.zh: 」又詔：「遠近不得遣山陵使。

translations.literal: " Again an edict: 'Near and far may not dispatch mausoleum commissioners.'
translations.idiomatic: A further decree forbade locals and provincials alike from sending special envoys to the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏選挽郎二十四人，詔停之。

translations.literal: " The offices memorialized to select twenty-four pallbearers; an edict suspended it.
translations.idiomatic: When officials proposed naming twenty-four pallbearers, that too was vetoed.

sentences.zh: 古無墓祭之禮。

translations.literal: Antiquity had no rite of sacrificing at graves.
translations.idiomatic: High antiquity knew no sanctioned cult performed at the burial mound itself.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦，皆有園寢。

translations.literal: Han inherited Qin; all had garden enclosures and resting halls.
translations.idiomatic: The Han, adopting Qin institutions, paired each imperial tumulus with an outer park and inner shrine hall.

sentences.zh: 正月上丁，祠南郊禮畢，次北郊、明堂、高廟、世祖廟，謂之五供。

translations.literal: On the upper ding day of the first month, when sacrifice at the southern suburb was finished, next came northern suburb, Bright Hall, Gaozu Temple, and Shizu Temple—called the Five Offerings.
translations.idiomatic: On the premier ding day of the first lunar month, after the southern suburban liturgy came, in order, the northern suburb, the Bright Hall, the temple of Gaozu, and the temple of Guangwu—the sequence known as the "five offerings."

sentences.zh: 魏武葬高陵，有司依漢立陵上祭殿。

translations.literal: When Wei Wu was buried at Gaoling, the offices according to Han precedent erected sacrifice halls atop the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At Cao Cao's interment at Gaoling, officials followed Han practice and built offering halls on the tumulus.

sentences.zh: 至文帝，乃詔曰：「先帝躬履節儉，遺詔省約。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Wen, an edict said: 'The late emperor personally practiced restraint; his testament enjoined reduction.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen issued an edict citing his father's lifelong austerity and testamentary demand for simplicity.

sentences.zh: 子以述父為孝，臣以繫事為忠。

translations.literal: A son takes transmitting the father as filial piety; a minister takes carrying forward affairs as loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: A worthy son embodies filial duty by fulfilling a father's charge; a loyal minister does the same by advancing the ruler's unfinished business.

sentences.zh: 古不墓祭，皆設於廟。

translations.literal: Antiquity did not sacrifice at graves; all was instituted at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients offered cult solely in the temple complex, never at the graveside.

sentences.zh: 高陵上殿皆毀壞，車馬還廄，衣服藏府，以從先帝儉德之志。

translations.literal: The halls atop Gaoling were all torn down; carriages and horses returned to the stables, garments to the storehouses—thereby following the late emperor's aspiration toward austere virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoling terrace chapels were demolished, horses returned to their stalls, robes to the wardrobe—all to honor Cao Cao's ideal of sober restraint.

sentences.zh: 」文帝自作終制，又曰「壽陵無立寢殿，造園邑」，自後園邑寢殿遂絕。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen himself drafted mortuary instructions, also stating 'At Shouling erect no resting hall, establish no mausoleum town'—from then on mausoleum towns and resting halls ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's own burial testament likewise forbade chapel or ceremonial township at Shouling; thereafter such adjuncts largely disappeared from Wei imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 齊王在位九年，始一謁高平陵而曹爽誅，其後遂廢，終於魏世。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi occupied the throne nine years; he had visited Gaoping Mausoleum only once when Cao Shuang was executed; thereafter the practice lapsed and did not revive for the remainder of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fang reigned nine years and managed a single visit to Gaoping Mausoleum before Cao Shuang's purge; court visits to Wei tumuli then fell dormant for the dynasty's remainder.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝，遺詔「子弟群官皆不得謁陵」。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor Xuan, his testament read: 'Sons, nephews, and all officials alike must not visit mausoleums.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan's deathbed injunction barred even imperial kinsmen and the bureaucracy from pilgrimages to the tombs.

sentences.zh: 於是景、文遵旨。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sima Shi and Sima Zhao obeyed it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao enforced that prohibition without exception.

sentences.zh: 至武帝，猶再謁崇陽陵，一謁峻平陵，然遂不敢謁高原陵，至惠帝復止也。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu, he still twice visited Chongyang Mausoleum and once Junping Mausoleum; yet he never ventured to Gaoyuan Mausoleum; by Emperor Hui the practice again stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu twice worshipped at Chongyang and once at Junping but avoided Gaoyuan; under Emperor Hui the custom ceased altogether.

sentences.zh: 逮于江左，元帝崩後，諸公始有謁陵辭告之事。

translations.literal: When matters shifted to the south bank, after Emperor Yuan died the great ministers first began visiting mausoleums with memorial farewells.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the court relocated south did high ministers inaugurate tomb pilgrimages paired with formal announcements.

sentences.zh: 蓋由眷同友執，率情而舉，非洛京之舊也。

translations.literal: Probably because affection felt like sworn friendship—following impulse they acted; it was not the Luoyang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Those journeys sprang from bonds as intimate as sworn brotherhood rather than from metropolitan statute—they were alien to old Luoyang usage.

sentences.zh: 成帝時，中宮亦年年拜陵，議者以為非禮，於是遂止，以為永制。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng's reign the empress too bowed yearly at the tombs; critics judged this contrary to ritual; thereupon it stopped and became standing policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng's empress continued annual tomb worship, ritualists objected; the court abolished the practice and codified the ban.

sentences.zh: 至穆帝時，褚太后臨朝，又拜陵，帝幼故也。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Mu, Empress Dowager Chu held court; again they worshipped at mausoleums—because the emperor was a minor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mu, Empress Dowager Chu resumed tomb visits while the boy emperor remained under regency.

sentences.zh: 至孝武崩，驃騎將軍司馬道子曰：「今雖權制釋服，至於朔望諸節，自應展情陵所，以一周為斷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, General-in-chief Who Pelts the Enemy Sima Daozi said: 'Although provisional regulations have released mourning garments, on new-moon, full-moon, and festival days feeling naturally extends to the mausoleum; let one full cycle mark the limit.'
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaowu's death, Sima Daozi argued that even though provisional rules had ended formal mourning, lunar and seasonal commemorations at the tomb should continue for one complete round.

sentences.zh: 」於是至陵，變服單衣，煩黷無準，非禮意也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon when they reached the mausoleum they changed into thin single garments—vexatious, without standard; not what the rites intend.
translations.idiomatic: The result was chaotic visits in summer-weight dress—burdensome, arbitrary, and far from ritual intent.

sentences.zh: 及安帝，尚書左僕射桓謙奏：「百僚拜陵，起于中興，非晉舊典，積習生常，遂為近法。

translations.literal: " Reaching Emperor An, Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Huan Qian memorialized: 'The hundred officials bowing at mausoleums arose with the Restoration; it is not Jin's ancient statute. Habit hardened into norm and became recent law.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor An, Huan Qian observed that ministers' tomb pilgrimages began only after the Eastern Jin restoration—not with western Jin precedent—and had ossified into questionable custom.

sentences.zh: 尋武皇帝詔，乃不使人主諸王拜陵，豈唯百僚！

translations.literal: Reflect on Emperor Wu's edict—it indeed forbade even the sovereign and kings from tomb worship—how much less mere officials!'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had explicitly barred rulers and princes from such journeys, let alone ordinary officials.

sentences.zh: 謂宜遵奉。

translations.literal: We deem it fitting to obey and uphold.'
translations.idiomatic: Huan urged strict conformity to that older policy.

sentences.zh: 」於是施行。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne adopted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 及義熙初，又復江左之舊。

translations.literal: By the opening years of Yixi, they again restored the Jiangzuo precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yixi era the southern court reverted to its earlier tomb-going habits.

sentences.zh: ，大鴻臚鄭默母喪，既葬，當依舊攝職，固陳不起，於是始制大臣得終喪三年。

translations.literal: , Grand Herald Zheng Mo's mother died; after burial he ought by precedent to resume office; he firmly declined appointment—thereupon it was first enacted that great ministers might observe the full three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Herald Zheng Mo, refusing reinstatement after burying his mother, prompted the first statutory allowance for senior ministers to complete three years of bereavement leave.

sentences.zh: 然元康中，陳準、傅咸之徒，猶以權奪，不得終禮，自茲已往，以為成比也。

translations.literal: Yet in Yuankang, Chen Zhun, Fu Xian, and their like still suffered expedient stripping of mourning and could not finish the rites; from this onward it was treated as settled precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, during Yuankang figures such as Chen Zhun and Fu Xian still saw mourning curtailed by administrative fiat; thereafter such interruptions hardened into precedent.

sentences.zh: ，東平王楙上言，相王昌父毖，本居長沙，有妻息，漢末使入中國，值吳叛，仕魏為黃門郎，與前妻息死生隔絕，更娶昌母。

translations.literal: , Prince of Dongping Mao submitted: Wang Chang's father Bi originally dwelt in Changsha with wife and children; late Han dispatched him into the Central Plains; when Wu rebelled he served Wei as a Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; cut off by war from his first household, he remarried and fathered Chang by the second wife.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mao reported the case of Wang Chang's father Bi: a Changsha native separated from his first family during the Wu revolt, who took a second wife in Wei after serving at court—and whose son now sought ritual clarity.

sentences.zh: 今江表一統，昌聞前母久喪，言疾求平議。

translations.literal: Now the southland is reunified; Chang learned his first mother died long ago; citing illness he seeks even adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: With the Yangzi region pacified, Wang Chang learned of his birth mother's distant death and petitioned—pleading illness—for an authoritative ruling.

sentences.zh: 守博士謝衡議曰：「雖有二妻，蓋有故而然，不為害於道，議宜更相為服。

translations.literal: Acting Erudite Xie Heng debated: 'Although there are two wives, there was compelling cause; it does not injure the Way; deliberation should favor mutual mourning obligations.'
translations.idiomatic: Xie Heng argued that dual wives born of wartime separation did not violate moral principle and that each party deserved reciprocal mourning recognition.

sentences.zh: 」守博士許猛以為「地絕，又無前母之制，正以在前非沒則絕故也。

translations.literal: Acting Erudite Xu Meng held: 'Territorial severance; moreover there is no statute for a "former mother"—precisely because unless earlier deceased there is severance.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Meng countered that geographic rupture removed classical guidance for a "prior wife" and severed ritual ties unless death had been confirmed.

sentences.zh: 前母雖在，猶不應服。

translations.literal: Though the former mother still lived, still one should not wear mourning for her.'
translations.idiomatic: Even had she survived, Chang owed her no mourning under statute.

sentences.zh: 」段暢、秦秀、騶沖從猛。

translations.literal: " Duan Chang, Qin Xiu, and Zou Chong sided with Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chang, Qin Xiu, and Zou Chong endorsed Xu Meng.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍劉智安議：「禮為常事制，不為非常設也。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Liu Zhian debated: 'The rites legislate ordinary cases, not anomalies.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhian insisted that canonical ritual addresses normal circumstances, not irregular wartime families.

sentences.zh: 亡父母不知其死生者，不著於禮。

translations.literal: For deceased parents whose fate is unknown—it is not codified in the rites.'
translations.idiomatic: No clause covers parents whose survival cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 平生不相見，去其加隆，以期為斷。

translations.literal: Never meeting in life—remove heightened mourning; let the one-year boundary decide.'
translations.idiomatic: Where lifelong separation obtained, augmented mourning should yield to the lighter "expectant" limit.

sentences.zh: 」都令史虞溥議曰：「臣以為禮不二嫡，所以重正，非徒如前議者防妒忌而已。

translations.literal: " Capital Clerk Yu Pu debated: 'Your servant holds: the rites forbid two principal wives—thereby to shore up legitimacy; not merely, as prior debaters said, to prevent jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu defended the principle that monogamous legitimacy—not jealousy management—forbade recognizing two coequal wives.

sentences.zh: 故曰『一與之齊，終身不改』，未有遭變而二嫡。

translations.literal: Hence it says "Once united with her in marriage, one does not alter it for life"—never has catastrophe legitimized dual principals.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry's pledge of lifelong union admits no doubled "primary" spouse.

sentences.zh: 苟不二，則昌父更娶之辰，是前妻義絕之日也。

translations.literal: If there cannot be two, then the moment Chang's father remarried was the day ritual obligation to the first wife ended.
translations.idiomatic: If only one principal wife was possible, Bi's second marriage dissolved whatever residual duty remained to his Changsha spouse.

sentences.zh: 使昌父尚存，二妻俱在，必不使二嫡專堂，兩婦執祭，同為之齊也。

translations.literal: Had Chang's father lived with both women present, surely they would not have allowed two principals to share the hall, two wives to offer sacrifice, both honored as coequal spouses.'
translations.idiomatic: Had both women shared one household, custom would never have tolerated rival mistresses of the altar.

sentences.zh: 」秦秀議：「二妾之子，父命令相慈養，而便有三年之恩，便同所生。

translations.literal: " Qin Xiu debated: 'Sons of two concubines—the father orders mutual nurturing—then there arises three-year grace; then same as born-of.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu pointed to parallel cases: half brothers commanded to care for one another observe full mourning as if sharing a mother.

sentences.zh: 昌父何義不命二嫡依此禮乎！

translations.literal: What righteousness allowed Chang's father not to subject both principals to that rite!'
translations.idiomatic: Why should Wang Chang's father be exempt from symmetric obligations toward both households?

sentences.zh: 父之執友有如子之禮，況事兄之母乎！

translations.literal: A father's sworn friends receive quasi-filial rites—how much more an elder brother's mother!'
translations.idiomatic: If ritual honors even a father's bondsman as quasi-kin, surely it encompasses a father's earlier consort.

sentences.zh: 」許猛又議：「夫少婦稚，則不可許以改娶更適矣。

translations.literal: " Xu Meng again debated: 'When the young wife is immature, one cannot permit remarriage and another match.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Meng replied that youth of the second wife cannot excuse unauthorized remarriage.

sentences.zh: 今妻在許以更聘，夫存而妻得改醮者，非絕而何。

translations.literal: Now with wife present permitting further betrothal—husband alive yet wife able to remarry—if not severance, what is it!'
translations.idiomatic: Allowing a living husband's new union while the earlier spouse remained wed elsewhere constitutes outright ritual divorce.

sentences.zh: 」侍中領博士張惲議：「昔舜不告而娶，婚禮蓋闕，故《堯典》以釐降二女為文，不殊嫡媵。

translations.literal: " Palace Attendant supervising Erudites Zhang Yun debated: 'Anciently Shun married without informing—wedding rites were lacking; hence the Canon of Yao narrates the descent of two daughters without distinguishing principal from secondary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun cited Shun's unsanctioned double marriage, recorded in the Canon of Yao without ranking consorts.

sentences.zh: 傳記以妃夫人稱之，明不立正后也。

translations.literal: Traditions call them consorts and ladies—making clear none was established as orthodox empress.'
translations.idiomatic: Later texts label them merely "consorts," implying no sole queen.

sentences.zh: 夫以聖人之弘，帝者嫡子，猶權事而變，以定典禮。

translations.literal: Given even the sage's latitude, the emperor's eldest legitimate son still weighed circumstance and adapted practice to fix canonical rites.'
