translations.idiomatic: Even sagely rulers adjusted ritual boundaries when founding a dynasty.

sentences.zh: 黃昌之告新妻使避正室，時論許之。

translations.literal: Huang Chang instructing his new wife to yield the principal chamber—contemporary opinion approved it.'
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chang's order that his second wife defer to the returned first won contemporaries' praise.

sentences.zh: 推姬氏之讓，執黃卿之決，宜使各自服其母。

translations.literal: Extend the Ji clan's deference, uphold Huang Qing's verdict—fitting to make each son mourn only his own mother.'
translations.idiomatic: Following Ji clan humility and Huang Chang's precedent, each son should mourn the woman who raised him.

sentences.zh: 」黃門侍郎崔諒、荀悝、中書監荀勖、領中書令和嶠、侍郎夏侯湛皆如溥議。

translations.literal: " Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Cui Liang and Xun Kui, Palace Secretariat Director Xun Xu, Palace Secretariat Supervisor He Qiao, and Attendant Xiahou Zhan all followed Pu's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang, Xun Kui, Xun Xu, He Qiao, and Xiahou Zhan sided with Yu Pu.

sentences.zh: 侍郎山雄、兼侍郎著作陳壽以為：「溥駁一與之齊，非大夫也，禮無二嫡，不可以並耳。

translations.literal: Attendant Shan Xiong and concurrent Attendant Compiler Chen Shou held: 'Pu refuted "once united with her"—not concerning grandees; the rites forbid two principals—they cannot coexist.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiong and Chen Shou argued Yu Pu misapplied the "one spouse" dictum, yet agreed two coequal wives remained impermissible.

sentences.zh: 若昌父及二母於今各存者，則前母不廢，已有明徵也。

translations.literal: If Chang's father and both mothers each existed today, the former wife would not be dismissed—there is already clear proof.'
translations.idiomatic: Had all parties survived reunification, the first marriage would still stand—historical exempla prove it.

sentences.zh: 設令昌父將前母之子來入中國尚在者，當從出母之服。

translations.literal: Suppose Chang's father brought the former mother's son into the Central Plains still living—he should follow mourning for an "outgoing mother."'
translations.idiomatic: A stepson arriving with Bi might owe reduced mourning to a repudiated birth mother.

sentences.zh: 苟昌父無棄前妻之命，昌兄有服母之理，則昌無疑於不服。

translations.literal: If Chang's father issued no mandate abandoning the former wife, Chang's elder brother has rationale to mourn that mother—then Chang has no doubt about not wearing mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: Where Bi never formally divorced his first wife, elder sons might owe her rites—yet Chang need not.

sentences.zh: 」賊曹屬卞粹議：「昌父當莫審之時而娶後妻，則前妻同之于死而義不絕。

translations.literal: " Bandit Bureau Clerk Bian Cui debated: 'When Chang's father took a second wife while truth remained uncertain, the first wife was as good as dead yet obligation did not sever.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Cui argued that Bi's second marriage during ambiguity treated wife one as presumed dead without ending kinship.

sentences.zh: 若生相及而後妻不去，則妾列於前志矣。

translations.literal: If in life they reunited yet the later wife was not dismissed, concubinage would be recorded in earlier chronicles.'
translations.idiomatic: Had both women later shared one roof without demoting the newcomer, chronicles would register concubinary rank.

sentences.zh: 死而會乎，則同祔於葬，無並嫡之實。

translations.literal: If death reunited them, joint burial annexed them—no reality of coequal principals.'
translations.idiomatic: Burial beside Bi would subsume both wives without elevating either as rival queen.

sentences.zh: 必欲使子孫於沒世之後，追計二母隔絕之時，以為並嫡，則背違死父，追出亡母。

translations.literal: Should descendants after death retrospectively reckon the years of separation as coequal principals—they betray the dead father and cast out the lost mother.'
translations.idiomatic: Retroactive elevation of both wives insults Bi's memory and disinherits the exile consort.

sentences.zh: 議者以為禮無前母之服者，可謂以文害意。

translations.literal: Those who argue the rites lack mourning for a former mother—may be called harming meaning by the letter.'
translations.idiomatic: Literalists who deny mourning for an abandoned first wife mistake exegetical pedantry for humane reading.

sentences.zh: 愚以為母之不親而服三年，非一無異於前母也。

translations.literal: I hold: for a mother not intimate yet wearing three years—it is not wholly without difference from a former mother.'
translations.idiomatic: Demanding full mourning for a stranger-mother differs materially from honoring a known birth parent.

sentences.zh: 倉曹屬衛恆議：「或云，嫡不可二，前妻宜絕。

translations.literal: " Granary Bureau Clerk Wei Heng debated: 'Some say principals cannot be two—the former wife should be severed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng summarized two camps: one insists on annulling the first match.

sentences.zh: 此為奪舊與新，違母從子，禮律所不許，人情所未安也。

translations.literal: This strips the old for the new, violates the mother to follow the son—what ritual and law forbid, what human feeling cannot abide.
translations.idiomatic: That path confiscates prior ties and subordinates maternal claims to filial convenience—law and sympathy alike reject it.

sentences.zh: 或云，絕與死同，無嫌二嫡，據其相及，欲令有服。

translations.literal: Some say severance equals death—no shame in two principals; according to mutual survival they wish mourning worn.
translations.idiomatic: Others equate estrangement with death and therefore authorize dual mourning.

sentences.zh: 此為論嫡則死，議服則生，還自相伐，理又不通。

translations.literal: This debates principals as dead yet discusses mourning as alive—it contradicts itself; in principle again untenable.
translations.idiomatic: That stance kills one wife juridically yet resurrects her ritually—a self-defeating muddle.

sentences.zh: 愚以為地絕死絕，誠無異也，宜一如前母，不復追服。

translations.literal: I hold territorial severance and deathly severance—truly no difference; should uniformly follow the former mother, not again pursue mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng concluded that exile and mortality alike ended obligation—no retrospective mourning.

sentences.zh: 」主簿劉卞議：「毖在南為邦族，於北為羈旅，以此名分言之，前妻為元妃，後婦為繼室。

translations.literal: " Registrar Liu Bian debated: 'Bi in the south was native kin; in the north a sojourner—by this status the former wife was primary consort, the later wife successor chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bian framed Bi as native in the south, guest in the north—making the Changsha wife principal and the Wei wife secondary.

sentences.zh: 何至王路既通，更當逐其今妻，廢其嫡子！

translations.literal: How could reopening imperial highways mean expelling his present wife and disinheriting his heir!'
translations.idiomatic: Reunification hardly requires divorcing the second wife or demoting her son.

sentences.zh: 不書姜氏，絕不為親，以其犯至惡也。

translations.literal: Not recording the Jiang clan—severance not treating as kin—because she committed utmost evil.'
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn omits Jiang because her crime voided kinship entirely.

sentences.zh: 趙姬雖貴，必推叔隗；

translations.literal: Though Lady Zhao was honored—she must defer to Shu Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ji, though ennobled, yielded precedence to her Di sister-in-law Shu Wei;

sentences.zh: 原同雖寵，必嫡宣孟。

translations.literal: Though Yuan Tong was favored—he must treat Xuan Meng as principal.'
translations.idiomatic: and favored Zhao Tong still acknowledged Zhao Dun as rightful heir.

sentences.zh: 若違禮苟讓，何則《春秋》所當善也！

translations.literal: If contrary to rites one yields anyhow—why then does the Spring and Autumn praise deference!'
translations.idiomatic: Canonical history celebrates deferential gestures precisely when they align with ritual hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 論者謂地絕，其情終已不得往來。

translations.literal: Arguers say territorial severance—feeling in the end could not travel back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Separation theorists assumed hearts could never bridge divided realms.

sentences.zh: 今地既通，何為故當追而絕之邪！

translations.literal: Now land already connects—why deliberately pursue severing them!'
translations.idiomatic: With roads open again, manufactured estrangement is perverse.

sentences.zh: 黃昌見美，斯又近世之明比。」

translations.literal: Huang Chang deemed admirable—this again is a clear parallel of recent times.'
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chang's judgment remains the nearest persuasive analogy.

sentences.zh: 司空齊王攸議：「《禮記》『生不及祖父母、諸父昆弟，而父稅喪，己則否』，諸儒皆以為父以他故子生異域，不及此親存時歸見之，父雖追服，子不從稅，不責非時之恩也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Qi Sima You debated: "The Record of Rites states, 'Born too late to see grandparents, uncles, or cousins—while the father pays mitigated mourning, oneself does not'—scholars agree the father sired the child far away and never introduced these kin alive; though the father later observes mourning, the child owes no levy—not requiring grace outside due season.
translations.idiomatic: Sima You cited Tan Gong: children born abroad need not inherit reduced mourning for kin they never met—an apt analogy for Wang Chang and a mother outside his lived experience.

sentences.zh: 但不相見，尚不服其先終，而況前母非親所生，義不逾祖，莫往莫來，恩絕殊隔，而令追服，殆非稱情立文之謂也。

translations.literal: Yet never meeting—still not mourning their prior death—how much less a former mother not born of oneself; obligation does not surpass grandparents; neither going nor coming—grace severed utterly apart—yet ordering retrospective mourning—hardly matches feeling when framing statute.
translations.idiomatic: If even unseen grandparents need no grief from later-born descendants, a culturally absent stepmother merits none—especially across decades without contact.

sentences.zh: 以為昌不宜追服。

translations.literal: We deem Chang unsuitable to pursue mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: Sima You concluded Wang Chang should not retroactively mourn.

sentences.zh: 」司徒李胤議：「毖為黃門侍郎，江南已叛。

translations.literal: " Minister of Education Li Yin debated: 'When Bi served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Jiangnan had already rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin opened by dating Bi's separation to Wu's revolt during his tenure at court.

sentences.zh: 石厚與焉，大義滅親，況於毖之義，可得以為妻乎！

translations.literal: Shi Hou participated therein; great righteousness annihilates kin; as for in Wang Bi's moral logic, how can one thereby treat her as wife!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hou took part in the conspiracy—great righteousness may override even kinship; all the more under the moral reasoning of Wang Bi's case: how could she still count as a wife?

sentences.zh: 」大司馬騫不議，太尉充、撫軍大將軍汝南王亮皆從主者。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Sima Qian offered no argument; Grand Commandant Jia Chong and General-in-Chief Who Pacifies the Army Prince Sima Liang of Runan all followed the presiding officer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Sima Qian did not speak; Grand Commandant Jia Chong and General-in-Chief Who Pacifies the Army Prince Sima Liang of Runan all deferred to the responsible official's ruling.

sentences.zh: 溥又駁粹曰：「喪從甯戚，謂喪事尚哀耳，不使服非其親也。

translations.literal: Pu again refuted Cui, saying: 'Mourning follows Ning-style grief—meaning funeral matters simply esteem sorrow; it does not mean wearing mourning for someone who is not one's kin.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Pu again countered Liu Cui: the classical line that mourning ought to prefer heartfelt grief means funerals should above all express sorrow; it does not license mourning for those outside one's proper kinship.

sentences.zh: 夫死者終也，終事已故無絕道。

translations.literal: For the dead are a completion; with the affair completed, therefore there is no endless continuity.
translations.idiomatic: Death is closure; once the obsequies are finished, the ritual thread does not extend without limit.

sentences.zh: 分居兩存，則離否由人。

translations.literal: If they dwell apart while both survive, then separation or reunion lies with human agency.
translations.idiomatic: When the couple live in different lands yet both still live, whether the bond is treated as broken is decided by people, not by fate alone.

sentences.zh: 夫婦以判合為義，今土隔人殊，則配合理絕。

translations.literal: Husband and wife take matched union as right principle; now territory divides them and persons are sundered, then the logic of pairing is severed.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage rests on conjugal union; when land and circumstance separate the spouses, the moral basis of the match is already ruptured.

sentences.zh: 彼已更娶代己，安得自同於死婦哉！

translations.literal: He has already remarried, replacing her—how can she equate herself with a deceased wife!
translations.idiomatic: He has taken another wife in her place—how can the abandoned wife still be classed as if she were a widow still married to him?

sentences.zh: 伯夷讓孤竹，不可以為後王法也。

translations.literal: Boyi yielding Guzhu cannot be taken as statutory precedent for later kings.
translations.idiomatic: The abdication of Boyi and Shu Qi cannot serve as binding precedent for later imperial ritual law.

sentences.zh: 且既已為嫡後服，復云為妾，生則或貶或離，死則同祔于葬，妻專一以事夫，夫懷貳以接己，開偽薄之風，傷貞信之教，於以純化篤俗，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, having already worn mourning as heir for the principal wife, yet again calling her concubine—in life sometimes demoted or cast off, in death jointly buried in annexation—the wife serves the husband with single devotion while the husband harbors doubleness toward her: this opens deceitful shallow conduct and injures teaching of constancy and trust; by this to purify transformation and deepen custom—is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to acknowledge her once as the principal mother for whom you wore full mourning as heir, then label her a concubine—to demote or divorce her in life yet bury her beside him in death—is for the wife to serve one husband faithfully while the husband keeps two standards toward her; such inconsistency encourages cynical laxity and corrodes the ethic of fidelity; with that example, how can the court hope to refine customs?

sentences.zh: 今昌二母雖土地殊隔，據同時並存，何得為前母后母乎！

translations.literal: Now Chang's two mothers, though lands divide them, according to circumstance coexist—how can they be called former mother and later mother!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang's two mothers may live far apart, but both are alive at once—they cannot be neatly pigeonholed as merely 'first mother' and 'second mother.'

sentences.zh: 設使昌母先亡，以嫡合葬，而前母不絕，遠聞喪問，當復相為制何服邪！

translations.literal: Suppose Chang's mother died first and was buried as principal wife, yet the former mother were not cut off and from afar heard mourning news—ought they again mutually regulate—what mourning would one wear!
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Wang Chang's Jin mother died first and received burial as principal consort while the Wu mother was never formally severed and, from afar, learned of the funeral—what garments of mourning could possibly coordinate such crossed obligations?

sentences.zh: 夫制不應禮，動而愈失。

translations.literal: Regulating contrary to ritual, every move increases loss.
translations.idiomatic: Every gesture that departs from canonical mourning only compounds error.

sentences.zh: 夫孝子不納親於不義，貞婦不昧進而苟容。

translations.literal: The filial son does not involve kin in unrighteousness; the chaste wife does not obscure advancement and tolerate wrongfully.
translations.idiomatic: A dutiful son does not implicate parents in wrongdoing; a virtuous wife does not gloss over compromise that betrays integrity.

sentences.zh: 今同前嫡於死婦，使後妻居正而或廢，於二子之心，曾無恧乎！

translations.literal: Now equating the former principal wife with a dead woman, causing the later wife to hold orthodox standing yet perhaps be set aside—in the hearts of the two sons, is there no shame!
translations.idiomatic: To rank the first wife with a corpse while elevating the successor yet leaving her vulnerable to dismissal—could the two sons feel no shame at such distortion?

sentences.zh: 而云誣父棄母，恐此文致之言，難以定臧否也。

translations.literal: Yet to say it slanders the father and abandons the mother—I fear this is twisted wording; it is hard thereby to determine right or wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Charges that the argument slanders the father and casts off the mother sound like rhetorical overreach; they do not settle the ethical merits.

sentences.zh: 禮，違諸侯適天子，不服舊君，然則昌父絕前君矣，更納後室，廢舊妻矣，又何取於宜誅宜撫乎！

translations.literal: By ritual, when one leaves a feudal lord to attend the Son of Heaven, one does not wear mourning for the former lord—thus Chang's father has cut off the former lord; he has taken a later chamber and abandoned the former wife—what again is there to take from deserving execution or deserving comforting!
translations.idiomatic: Ritual exempts one who leaves a regional lord to serve the emperor from mourning that former lord—so Wang Chang's father has renounced his Wu allegiance, taken a new wife, and set aside the old; why drag in talk of who deserves execution versus who deserves pity?

sentences.zh: 且婦人之有惡疾，乃慈夫之所愍也，而在七出，誠以在人理應絕故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a woman has vile illness, it is what a compassionate husband pities; yet it stands among the seven grounds for divorce—truly because human principle demands severance.
translations.idiomatic: Even grave illness, though the humane husband pities it, counts among the seven lawful divorces precisely because humane order sometimes requires the bond to end.

sentences.zh: 今夫婦殊域，與無妻同，方之惡疾，理無以異。

translations.literal: Now husband and wife are in separate realms—the same as having no wife; compared to vile illness, in principle there is no difference.
translations.idiomatic: Separation by hostile borders leaves the marriage void in practice, much as incurable sickness does; morally the cases parallel.

sentences.zh: 據己更娶，有絕前之證。

translations.literal: According to the fact that he has remarried, there is proof of severance from the former.
translations.idiomatic: His new marriage itself proves the prior tie was broken.

sentences.zh: 而云應服，于義何居！

translations.literal: Yet to say one ought to wear mourning—where does that rest in right principle!
translations.idiomatic: To insist mourning is still owed—on what coherent moral ground?

sentences.zh: 」尚書八座以為「設令有人于此，父為敦煌太守，而子後任于洛，若父娶妻，非徒不見，乃可不知，及其死亡，不得不服。

translations.literal: The Eight Seats of the Secretariat judged: 'Suppose someone whose father was governor of Dunhuang while the son later served at Luoyang: if the father married a woman he never saw—indeed might not know of—and she died, he could not but wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat's Eight Seats argued: imagine a father serving as Dunhuang governor while his son holds office in Luoyang; the father marries a woman he never meets—perhaps never knows exists—and she dies: ritual still obliges him to mourn.

sentences.zh: 但鞠養已者情哀，而不相見名制，雖戚念之心殊，而為之服一也。

translations.literal: Yet toward her who reared oneself affection is sorrowful; toward her unseen the name and regulation—though compassionate thoughts differ, the mourning worn for her is one.
translations.idiomatic: Affection toward her who reared oneself runs deep as grief; toward her unseen only names and regulation apply—though compassionate thoughts differ, the mourning garment is one.

sentences.zh: 又，兩后匹嫡，自謂違禮，不謂非常之事而以常禮處之也。

translations.literal: Again, two queens matched as principals—they themselves call it contrary to ritual; they do not mean an extraordinary event should be handled with ordinary ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Those who acknowledge two coequal principal wives admit the breach of norm; they do not ask that an anomaly be squeezed into everyday precedent.

sentences.zh: 昔子思哭出母於廟，其門人曰：『庶氏之女死，何為哭于孔氏之廟！

translations.literal: Formerly Zisi wept for his divorced mother at the temple; his disciples said, "The daughter of the Shu clan has died—why weep in the Kong clan's temple!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zisi mourned his divorced mother inside the Kong temple, disciples protested: the Shu woman's death should not be lamented in Confucius's ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 』子思懼，改哭於他室。

translations.literal: Zisi feared and changed to weeping in another chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Zisi moved his mourning to another room.

sentences.zh: 若昌不制服，不得不告其父祖，掘其前母之尸，徙之他地。

translations.literal: If Chang does not wear mourning, he cannot but inform his father and grandfather, exhume his former mother's corpse, and move it elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Chang refuses mourning, he must ask father and grandfather to exhume the earlier wife and relocate her remains.

sentences.zh: 若其不徙，昌為罪人。

translations.literal: If he does not move her, Chang becomes a criminal.
translations.idiomatic: Failure to move her makes Wang Chang ritually culpable.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: What then is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 異族之女不得祔于先姑，藏其墓次故也。

translations.literal: Because a woman of another clan may not be buried beside the former mother-in-law—due to storing her in the tomb sequence.
translations.idiomatic: An outsider cannot receive burial beside the senior mother-in-law within the graded tomb complex.

sentences.zh: 且夫婦人牽夫，猶有所尊，趙姬之舉，禮得權通，故先史詳之，不譏其事耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, in woman attaching to husband there is still something honored; Zhao Ji's elevation—ritual allowed expedient adaptation—therefore earlier historians detailed it without censuring the deed.
translations.idiomatic: Even wives defer to husbands, yet precedent honors Zhao Ji's arrangement because ritual permitted flexibility; chroniclers recorded it without moral censure.

sentences.zh: 今昌之二母，各已終亡，尚無並主輕重之事也。

translations.literal: Now Chang's two mothers have each already ended—there is not yet the matter of two mistresses contending priority.
translations.idiomatic: Both of Wang Chang's mothers are deceased; we face no quarrel between rival mistresses still living.

sentences.zh: 昌之前母，宜依叔隗為比。

translations.literal: Chang's former mother ought to take Shu Wei as analogy.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier wife should be analogized to Shu Wei.

sentences.zh: 若亡在昌未生之前者，則昌不應復服。

translations.literal: If she died before Chang was born, then Chang ought not again to wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: If she died before Wang Chang's birth, he owes her no renewed mourning.

sentences.zh: 生及母存，自應如禮以名服三年。

translations.literal: If he was born while his mother survived, naturally according to ritual he should by name wear three years.
translations.idiomatic: If he was born while she lived, canonical mourning demands the full three-year observance.

sentences.zh: 輒正定為文，章下太常報楙奉行。」

translations.literal: Thereupon they fixed the text as regulation, issued it down to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials to report and Mao to carry out.'
translations.idiomatic: They drafted a definitive ruling for transmission to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials and execution by Mao.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「凡事有非常，當依準舊典，為之立斷。

translations.literal: The edict stated: 'Whenever affairs are extraordinary, one ought to rely on old canons and decide them.'
translations.idiomatic: The imperial rescript declared that extraordinary cases must be adjudicated against established classical precedent.

sentences.zh: 今議此事，稱引趙姬、叔隗者粗是也。

translations.literal: Now in debating this matter, those who cite Zhao Ji and Shu Wei are roughly correct.
translations.idiomatic: Debators who invoke Zhao Ji and Shu Wei grasp the essentials.

sentences.zh: 然後狄與晉和，故姬氏得迎叔隗而下之。

translations.literal: Yet afterward the Di made peace with Jin; therefore Lady Ji was able to welcome Shu Wei and rank her below herself.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the Di tribes reconciled with Jin could Lady Ji receive Shu Wei and seat her in subordinate rank.

sentences.zh: 吳寇隔塞，毖與前妻，終始永絕。

translations.literal: The Wu bandits block communications; Bi and his former wife are severed forever from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Wu armies seal the frontier; Wang Bi and his first wife are irreparably estranged.

sentences.zh: 必義無兩嫡，則趙衰可以專制隗氏。

translations.literal: If right principle admits no two principals, then Zhao Cui could autonomously regulate the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: If ethics forbid two coequal wives, Zhao Cui could unilaterally settle Shu Wei's status.

sentences.zh: 昌為人子，豈得擅替其母。

translations.literal: Chang as a man's son—how may he arbitrarily replace his mother!
translations.idiomatic: A son may not unilaterally demote his own mother.

sentences.zh: 且毖二妻並以絕亡，其子猶後母之子耳，昌故不應制服也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Bi's two wives have both perished by separation; his sons are still sons of a stepmother—thus Chang originally ought not to wear mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wang Bi's wives died estranged by politics; the sons answer to a stepmother's household—so Wang Chang never owed formal mourning for the Wu wife.

sentences.zh: 太興初，著作郎干寶論之曰：「禮有經有變有權，王毖之事，有為為之也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, Editorial Director Gan Bao discussed it, saying: 'Ritual has constant rule, variation, and expedient; Wang Bi's affair was undertaken with deliberate purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taixing era, Editorial Director Gan Bao reflected that ritual admits fixed norms, adaptive exceptions, and discretionary expedients—and Wang Bi's predicament was precisely such a deliberate departure.

sentences.zh: 有不可責以始終之義，不可求以循常之文，何群議之紛錯！

translations.literal: There are cases one cannot demand be judged by consistency from beginning to end, cannot seek with ordinary pattern—why so much confused debate among the assembly!
translations.idiomatic: Some circumstances cannot be judged by seamless continuity or boilerplate precedent—so why the endless quarrel?

sentences.zh: 同產者無嫡側之別，而先生為兄；

translations.literal: Those of the same birth have no distinction of principal and secondary; yet he who was born first is elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Full siblings share rank without principal-secondary labels; birth order alone makes elder and younger.

sentences.zh: 諸侯同爵無等級之差，而先封為長。

translations.literal: Feudal lords of same rank have no difference of grade; yet he who was enfeoffed first is senior.
translations.idiomatic: Peers sharing identical noble rank gain seniority solely from who received the fief first.

sentences.zh: 今二妻之入，無貴賤之禮，則宜以先後為秩，順序義也。

translations.literal: Now with two wives entering, if there is no ritual of noble and base, then one ought to take precedence as order—submitting to sequence is right.
translations.idiomatic: When two wives lack hierarchical distinction, chronological precedence supplies the moral order.

sentences.zh: 今生而同室者寡，死而同廟者眾，及其神位，固有上下也。

translations.literal: Now those who share the chamber while alive are few; those who share the temple when dead are many—as to their spirit tablets, there inherently is above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Few couples worship jointly in life; many lineages enshrine multiple mothers after death—tablet placement still observes senior and junior.

sentences.zh: 故《春秋》賢趙姬遭禮之變而得禮情也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals honors Zhao Ji for encountering ritual variation yet grasping ritual sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Annals praise Zhao Ji for navigating ritual change without losing humane proportion.

sentences.zh: 且夫吉凶哀樂，動乎情者也，五禮之制，所以敘情而即事也。

translations.literal: Moreover, fortune and misfortune, grief and joy—these stir feeling; the system of the five rituals exists to order feeling and align with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Weal and woe, lamentation and delight move the human heart; the Five Rites discipline emotion so conduct answers circumstance.

sentences.zh: 今二母者，本他人也，以名來親，而恩否于時，敬不及生，愛不及喪，夫何追服之道哉！

translations.literal: Now as for the two mothers—originally they were others; they came close by title, yet kindness did not obtain at the time; reverence did not reach the living, love did not reach death—what way is there for retrospective mourning!
translations.idiomatic: Both women began as outsiders linked only by title; timely affection never matured, reverence never attached to their lifetimes, affection never accompanied their deaths—what rationale demands retroactive mourning?

sentences.zh: 張惲、劉卞，得其先後之節，齊王、衛恆，通於服絕之制，可以斷矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Yun and Liu Bian grasped the precedence of order; Prince of Qi and Wei Heng understood the regulation when mourning is severed—by this one may decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun and Liu Bian preserved precedence among mothers; the Prince of Qi and Wei Heng grasped when ritual cuts mourning short—that framework suffices for judgment.

sentences.zh: 朝廷於此，宜導之以趙姬，齊之以詔命，使先妻恢含容之德，後妻崇卑讓之道，室人達長少之序，百姓見變禮之中。

translations.literal: The court here ought to guide them with Zhao Ji, align them with edict and command, causing the first wife to restore the virtue of inclusive bearing and the later wife to honor the way of humble yielding, household members to comprehend the order of elder and junior, and the hundred clans to witness the mean in variant ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The throne should steer litigants toward the Zhao Ji precedent, codify it by edict, encourage the first wife's magnanimity and the successor's deference, clarify domestic seniority, and show the realm how flexible ritual still observes the golden mean.

sentences.zh: 若此，可以居生，又況於死乎！

translations.literal: If thus, one may abide while alive—how much more in death!
translations.idiomatic: Such harmony suits the living; it suits the dead still better.

sentences.zh: 古之王者，有以師友之禮待其臣，而臣不敢自尊。

translations.literal: Ancient kings sometimes treated ministers with the rites due teacher and friend, yet ministers did not dare esteem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Former sovereigns occasionally honored ministers as teachers or friends, yet those ministers never presumed upon the privilege.

sentences.zh: 今令先妻以一體接後，而後妻不敢抗，及其子孫交相為服，禮之善物也。

translations.literal: Now if the first wife receives the later with unity of body and the later wife dares not resist, and their descendants reciprocally wear mourning for each other—it is the finest outcome of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the senior wife welcomes the junior as coequal kindred and the junior yields, while descendants exchange proper mourning, ritual achieves its most humane form.

sentences.zh: 然則王昌兄弟相得之日，蓋宜祫祭二母，等其禮饋，序其先後，配以左右，兄弟肅雍，交酬奏獻，上以恕先父之志，中以高二母之德，下以齊兄弟之好，使義風弘于王教，慈讓洽乎急難，不亦得禮之本乎！」

translations.literal: Then on the day Wang Chang's brothers attain harmony, they ought generally to perform joint sacrifice to both mothers, equalize ritual offerings, sequence their precedence, arrange them left and right—brothers reverent and harmonious, exchanging toasts and presenting offerings—above to fulfill their late father's intent, middle to elevate both mothers' virtue, below to harmonize the brothers' goodwill—causing righteous teaching to flourish in royal instruction and kindly yielding to pervade urgent straits—is this not obtaining ritual's root!
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chang's brothers reconcile, they should convene a joint offering for both mothers, balance victims and vessels, sequence seats east and west, and chant hymns together—honoring the father's wish, magnifying both mothers' merit, and sealing fraternal concord—thus extending humane governance into crisis and recovering ritual's deepest purpose.

sentences.zh: 是時，沛國劉仲武先娶毌丘氏，生子正舒、正則二人。

translations.literal: At that time, Liu Zhongwu of Pei first married Lady Muqiu and bore sons Zhengshu and Zhengze.
translations.idiomatic: In Pei commandery Liu Zhongwu had first wed a lady of the Guanqiu clan and fathered Zhengshu and Zhengze.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉反敗，仲武出其妻，娶王氏，生陶，仲武為毌丘氏別舍而不告絕。

translations.literal: When Guanqiu Jian rebelled and was defeated, Zhongwu expelled his wife and married Lady Wang, bore Tao; Zhongwu housed Lady Muqiu separately but did not declare severance.
translations.idiomatic: After Guanqiu Jian's revolt collapsed, Zhongwu cast out that wife, married Lady Wang, and sired Tao, yet lodged the Guanqiu woman apart without formally divorcing her.

sentences.zh: 及毌丘氏卒，正舒求祔葬焉，而陶不許。

translations.literal: When Lady Muqiu died, Zhengshu sought joint burial, but Tao refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guanqiu lady died, Zhengshu asked to bury her with the lineage; Tao blocked the request.

sentences.zh: 舒不釋服，訟於上下，泣血露骨，縗裳綴絡，數十年弗得從，以至死亡。

translations.literal: Shu did not shed mourning; he sued high and low, wept blood and exposed bone, wore hemp with stitched cords—for decades he could not obtain compliance until death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshu refused to end mourning, appealed endlessly, wept blood, laid bare his grievance, and patched his hemp robes for decades, dying without satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 時吳國朱某娶妻陳氏，生子東伯。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu of Wu married Lady Chen and bore son Dongbo.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile a Wu gentleman Zhu had married Lady Chen and fathered Dongbo.

sentences.zh: 入晉，晉賜妻某氏，生子綏伯。

translations.literal: Entering Jin, Jin granted him a wife of the Mou clan and bore son Suibo.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting to Jin, the court assigned him another wife of the Mou clan who bore Suibo.

sentences.zh: 太康之中，某已亡，綏伯將母以歸邦族，兄弟交愛敬之道，二母篤先後之序，雍雍人無間焉。

translations.literal: In the Taikang period, Mou having died, Suibo was about to lead his mother back to their clan homeland—brothers exchanged the way of love and reverence; the two mothers observed earnest precedence as former and later—harmonious, without estrangement among people.
translations.idiomatic: During Taikang, after Mou died Suibo prepared to escort his mother home; the half-brothers practiced mutual devotion, both mothers honored senior-junior order, and the household remained without rancor.

sentences.zh: 及其終也，二子交相為服，君子以為賢。

translations.literal: When they ended, the two sons reciprocally wore mourning for each other—gentlemen deemed them worthy.
translations.idiomatic: At their deaths each son observed mourning for the other's mother—observers praised their virtue.

sentences.zh: 安豐太守程諒先已有妻，後又娶，遂立二嫡。

translations.literal: Prefect of Anfeng Cheng Liang had already had a wife, then married again, thereby establishing two principals.
translations.idiomatic: Anfeng prefect Cheng Liang took a second wife while the first lived, creating two principal consorts.

sentences.zh: 前妻亡，後妻子勳疑所服。

translations.literal: The former wife died; the later wife's son Xun doubted what mourning to wear.
translations.idiomatic: After the first wife died, the second wife's son Xun questioned his mourning obligations.

sentences.zh: 中書令張華造甲乙之問曰：「甲娶乙為妻，後又娶丙，匿不說有乙，居家如二嫡，無有貴賤之差。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Director Zhang Hua posed the jia-yi question: 'Jia married Yi as wife, then married Bing, concealing that Yi existed—dwelling at home like two principals without distinction of noble or base.
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhang Hua framed a hypothetical: Jia weds Yi, then secretly weds Bing so that both wives rank as principals without clear precedence.

sentences.zh: 乙亡，丙之子當何服？

translations.literal: Yi died—what mourning ought Bing's son wear?
translations.idiomatic: When Yi dies, what mourning does Bing's son owe?

sentences.zh: 本實並列，嫡庶不殊，雖二嫡非正，此失在先人，人子何得專制析其親也。

translations.literal: In truth they stood parallel; principal and secondary were not differentiated—though two principals are not orthodox, the fault lies with the prior generation—how may the son on his own authority divide his kin!
translations.idiomatic: They were genuinely coequal; fault rests with the father's deception—not with the child who cannot carve kin ties at will.

sentences.zh: 若為庶母服，又不成為庶。

translations.literal: If he wears mourning for a concubine mother, again he does not count as concubine offspring.
translations.idiomatic: Treating her as a concubine-mother mislabels a principal parent; treating him as a concubine son mislabels his birth.

sentences.zh: 進退不知所從。

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating, he knows not what to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Every option violates some ritual norm.

sentences.zh: 」太傅鄭沖議曰：「甲失禮於家，二嫡並在，誠非人子所得正。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Zheng Chong deliberated: 'Jia failed ritual at home; two principals standing together—truly not something a son may rectify.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Zheng Chong argued that a household with two principal wives lies beyond a son's power to correct.

sentences.zh: 則乙丙之子並當三年，禮疑從重。

translations.literal: Then Yi's son and Bing's son both ought three years; when ritual doubts, follow the heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Both sons should therefore wear the highest grade—three years—because doubtful cases favor the weightier obligation.

sentences.zh: 」車騎賈充、侍中少傅任愷議略與鄭同。

translations.literal: Cavalry-in-ordinary Jia Chong and Palace Attendant Junior Tutor Ren Kai deliberated, broadly agreeing with Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry general Jia Chong and junior tutor Ren Kai largely concurred with Zheng Chong.

sentences.zh: 太尉荀顗議曰：「《春秋》並后匹嫡，古之明典也。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Xun Yi deliberated: 'The Spring and Autumn Annals treats paired queens as coequal principals—an ancient explicit norm.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Xun Yi cited the Annals' pairing of queens as coequal principals—a classical paradigm.

sentences.zh: 今不可以犯禮並立二妻，不別尊卑而遂其失也。

translations.literal: Now one cannot violate ritual by establishing two wives side by side without distinguishing noble and base and thereby perpetuate the fault.
translations.idiomatic: The court must not compound the father's error by letting both wives stand undifferentiated.

sentences.zh: 故當斷之以禮，先至為嫡，後至為庶。

translations.literal: Therefore one ought to decide by ritual: she who arrived first is principal; she who arrived later is secondary.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual arbitration therefore elevates the earlier arrival as principal and demotes the later as secondary.

sentences.zh: 丙子宜以嫡母服乙，乙子宜以庶母事丙。

translations.literal: Bing's son ought by principal mother wear mourning for Yi; Yi's son ought by secondary mother serve Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's son mourns Yi as principal mother; Yi's son honors Bing with the rites owed a secondary mother.

sentences.zh: 昔屈建去芰，古人以為違禮而得禮。

translations.literal: Formerly Qu Jian rejected water chestnuts—ancients thought him contrary to ritual yet obtaining ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jian's refusal of water caltrops seemed to breach etiquette yet embodied its spirit—so commentators judged.

sentences.zh: 丙子非為抑其親，斯自奉禮先後貴賤順敘之義也。

translations.literal: Bing's son is not thereby suppressing his kin—this itself upholds ritual's meaning of precedence, noble and base, and orderly sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's son thus does not dishonor blood ties; he observes precedence, rank, and orderly affection as ritual demands.

sentences.zh: 」中書監荀勖議曰：「昔鄉里鄭子群娶陳司空從妹，後隔呂布之亂，不復相知存亡，更娶鄉里蔡氏女。

translations.literal: Chief of the Secretariat Xun Xu deliberated: 'Formerly in the village Zheng Ziqun married the younger cousin of Minister Chen of Chen; afterward cut off by Lu Bu's rebellion, they no longer knew each other's life or death; he married again Lady Cai of the village.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat supervisor Xun Xu recalled Zheng Ziqun, who married a Chen minister's cousin, lost contact during Lu Bu's turmoil, assumed her dead, and remarried Lady Cai.

sentences.zh: 徐州平定，陳氏得還，遂二妃並存。

translations.literal: When Xuzhou was pacified, the Chen clan returned—thus both consorts coexisted.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuzhou quieted, Lady Chen reappeared, leaving Zheng with two wives.

sentences.zh: 蔡氏之子字元釁，為陳氏服嫡母之服，事陳公以從舅之禮。

translations.literal: Lady Cai's son, courtesy name Yuanxin, wore for Lady Chen the mourning of a principal mother and served Lord Chen with the rites due a mother's brother.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cai's son Yuanxin donned principal-mother mourning for Lady Chen and treated Minister Chen with the courtesy owed a maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 族兄宗伯曾責元釁，謂抑其親，鄉里先達以元釁為合宜。

translations.literal: His lineage elder Zongbo once reproached Yuanxin, saying he suppressed his kin; village elders deemed Yuanxin appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Clan elder Zongbo accused Yuanxin of slighting his birth mother, yet local worthies approved his conduct.

sentences.zh: 不審此事粗相似否。」

translations.literal: I do not know whether this affair is roughly similar.'
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu wondered whether that precedent mapped onto Zhang Hua's puzzle.

sentences.zh: ，以溫嶠為散騎侍郎，嶠以母亡值寇，不臨殯葬，欲營改葬，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: [Earlier clause omitted by source], appointing Wen Qiao as Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary; Qiao, because his mother had died during bandit turmoil and he had not attended burial rites, wished to arrange reburial, firmly declined and would not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: …the court named Wen Qiao Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary; citing his mother's death amid raids, missed funeral, and pending reburial, he steadfastly refused the commission.

sentences.zh: 元帝詔曰：「溫嶠不拜，以未得改卜葬送，朝議又頗有異同。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan's edict stated: 'Wen Qiao's refusal to accept—because he has not yet been able to relocate divination and burial send-off—court deliberation again differs somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan noted Wen Qiao's demurral—linked to unfinished grave relocation—and acknowledged divided counsel.

sentences.zh: 為審由此邪？

translations.literal: Is it indeed for this reason?
translations.idiomatic: Was that truly his motive?

sentences.zh: 天下有闕塞，行禮制物者當使理可經通。

translations.literal: When the realm has blockage and rupture, those who enact ritual and regulate affairs ought to make principle sustainable and pervious.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos sunders the empire, regulators must stretch ritual principle until it remains practicable.

sentences.zh: 古人之制三年，非情之所盡，蓋存亡有斷，不以死傷生耳。

translations.literal: The ancients' system of three years—not that emotion exhausts itself—cover existence and demise having a break; one does not injure the living by the dead.
translations.idiomatic: The three-year mourning rule does not demand limitless grief; it marks a finite rupture between death and life so the living are not crippled by the dead.

sentences.zh: 要絰而服金革之役者，豈營官邪？

translations.literal: Those who tie hemp headbands yet take metal-and-leather campaigns—was it for official salary?
translations.idiomatic: Warriors who gird hemp while bearing arms did not do so for stipends alone.

sentences.zh: 隨王事之緩急也。

translations.literal: They followed the urgency or slackness of royal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They calibrated obligation against the throne's military needs.

sentences.zh: 今桀逆未梟，平陽道斷，奉迎諸軍猶未得徑進，嶠特一身，于何濟其私艱，而以理閡自疑，不服王命邪！

translations.literal: Now the fierce rebels are not yet beheaded; the Pingyang road is cut; the armies sent to escort still cannot advance straight—Qiao is but one man; how would he remedy his private bereavement—yet on grounds of principle obstruct himself and doubt accepting royal command!
translations.idiomatic: Rebels still live, roads to Pingyang remain blocked, relief columns cannot march—Wen Qiao alone cannot hurry a parent's burial; shall ritual niceties excuse defiance of imperial orders?

sentences.zh: 其令三司八座、門下三省、外內群臣，詳共通議如嶠比，吾將親裁其中。

translations.literal: Order the Three Offices, Eight Seats, gates down Three Departments, inner and outer ministers—deliberate thoroughly together on cases like Qiao's; I will personally adjudicate among them.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the Three Departments, Eight Seats, inner and outer ministries to debate precedents comparable to Wen Qiao's and pledged to render the final judgment.

sentences.zh: 」於是太宰、西陽王羕，司徒臨潁公組，驃騎將軍、即丘子導，侍中紀瞻，尚書周顗，散騎常侍荀邃等議，以「昔伍員挾弓去楚，為吳行人以謀楚，誠志在報仇，不苟滅身也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Tutor Prince Xi Yang Sima Xi, Minister Chenggong Zu of Linying, General-in-Chief Who Gallops Fast Prince Qiu Sima Dao, Palace Attendant Ji Zhan, Secretary Zhou Yi, Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Xun Sui and others deliberated: 'Formerly Wu Yuan carried bow and left Chu, became Wu's envoy to plot against Chu—truly his intent lay in avenging wrong, not carelessly destroying himself.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Yang of Xiyang Sima Xi, Duke Zu of Linying, General-in-Chief Prince Dao of Langya, Ji Zhan, Zhou Yi, Xun Sui, and others compared Wen Qiao to Wu Zixu, who fled Chu armed and served Wu as envoy—intent on revenge, not suicide.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠遭難，昔在河朔，日尋干戈，志刷讎惡，萬里投身，歸赴朝廷，將欲因時竭力，憑賴王威，以展其情，此乃嶠之志也。

translations.literal: Wen Qiao encountered calamity—formerly north of the River, daily amid shields and spears—intent to wipe away hatred and evil; he threw himself ten thousand li and hastened to court, intending to seize the moment and exhaust his strength, relying on royal majesty to unfold his feeling—this was Qiao's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao survived catastrophe on the northern frontier amid constant battle, burning to erase shame; he raced thousands of miles to court seeking leverage under imperial authority—that was his purpose.

sentences.zh: 無緣道路未通，師旅未進，而更中辭王事，留志家巷也。

translations.literal: It was not that roads were not yet open or armies not yet advanced, and he again declined royal affairs mid-course and kept his mind on home lanes.
translations.idiomatic: He did not shelve public duty halfway simply because routes stayed dangerous or troops stalled.

sentences.zh: 以為誠宜如明詔。

translations.literal: They deemed it truly fitting to follow the enlightened edict.
translations.idiomatic: They concluded the sovereign's directive should prevail.

sentences.zh: 」於是有司奏曰：「案如眾議，去九月下辛未令書，依禮文，父喪未葬，唯喪主不除。

translations.literal: Thereupon the responsible officials memorialized: 'According to the assembly's deliberation, reviewing the ninth month's lower xinwei order letter—by ritual text, when father's mourning is not yet buried, only the chief mourner does not shed mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: The bureaucracy then reported: per collective opinion, parsing the late ninth-month xinwei edict against canon—while a father's corpse awaits burial, only the chief mourner remains in mourning without shedding it.

sentences.zh: 以他故未葬，人子之情，不可居殯而除，故期於畢葬，無遠近之斷也。

translations.literal: Because some other matter delayed burial, the heart of a son cannot remain beside the bier and yet lay mourning aside; therefore the limit is set at completion of burial, with no distinction drawn between cases near or far.
translations.idiomatic: When interment is postponed for contingent reasons, filial grief cannot end merely from keeping vigil by the coffin; mourning runs until the burial is finished, without carving out exceptions for distance or delay.

sentences.zh: 若亡遇賊難，喪靈無處，求索理絕，固應三年而除，不得故從未葬之例也。

translations.literal: If the deceased meets death amid banditry and the spirit has nowhere to rest and every avenue of search is exhausted, one certainly ought to remove mourning after three years; one must not deliberately invoke the precedent for bodies still unburied.
translations.idiomatic: If someone perishes in rebellion, no remains can be recovered, and inquiry has reached a dead end, mourning properly ends after the three-year term; the rule for an unburied corpse does not apply.

sentences.zh: 若骨肉殲於寇害，死亡漫于中原，而繼以遺賊未滅，亡者無收殯之實，存者又闕於奔赴之禮，而人子之情，哀痛無斷，輒依未葬之義，久而不除，若遂其情，則人居無限之喪，非有禮無時不得之義也。

translations.literal: If flesh and kin are slaughtered by raiders and the dead lie scattered across the Central Plains, and remnant bandits remain undefeated so that the departed lack any reality of gathering and burial while the living lack the rites of rushing to attend, yet the heart of sons knows no break in grief and they cling to the principle of “not yet buried,” refusing to lay mourning aside for a long time—if their feelings were indulged without limit, people would dwell in boundless mourning, which is not the meaning of “there is ritual; without due season one does not obtain release.”
translations.idiomatic: When kin are massacred and corpses lie beyond recovery while war continues—when there is nothing to inter and survivors cannot perform the funeral rush—filial sorrow has no clear term and mourners invoke “still unburied” to prolong grief indefinitely. To indulge that impulse forever would trap the realm in endless mourning, violating the principle that ritual release must observe proper timing.

sentences.zh: 諸如此，皆依東關故事，限行三年之禮畢而除也。

translations.literal: For all cases such as these, rely on the Dongguan precedent and restrict practice so that mourning ends once the three-year observance is completed.
translations.idiomatic: Such situations follow the Dongguan precedent: mourning is capped at three years and concludes when those rites are finished.

sentences.zh: 唯二親生離，吉凶未分，服喪則凶事未據，從吉則疑於不存，心憂居素，出自人情，有如此者，非官制之所裁。

translations.literal: Only when both parents are torn away alive and auspicious or inauspicious outcome is still undecided—if one puts on mourning the ominous fact is not yet established; if one follows auspicious life one suspects oneself of acting as if they no longer exist—then anxious restraint in plain dress arises from human feeling. Situations like this are not what bureaucratic regulation can neatly adjudicate.
translations.idiomatic: When parents are separated from their children with fate unknown—full mourning assumes a death not proved, yet returning to normal dress implies writing them off—people naturally remain in subdued garb. Such cases lie beyond what statutes can prescribe.

sentences.zh: 今嶠以未得改卜奔赴，累設疾辭。

translations.literal: Now Qiao, because he could not obtain permission to choose a new burial site and hurry to attend the funeral, repeatedly pleaded illness to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao, unable to secure leave to rebury his kin and rush to the funeral, repeatedly cited illness to refuse appointment.

sentences.zh: 案辛未之制，已有成斷，皆不得復遂其私情，不服王命，以虧法憲。

translations.literal: Examining the xinwei regulation, there is already a settled ruling; none may again indulge private sentiment, refuse royal command, and thereby harm the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Under the xinwei precedent the matter is closed: officials must not privilege private feeling over imperial orders and thereby undermine the law.

sentences.zh: 參議可如前詔嶠受拜，重告以中丞司徒，諸如嶠比者，依東關故事辛未令書之制。

translations.literal: The deliberators may, as in the prior edict, order Qiao to accept appointment; announce this again to the Palace Assistant Clerk and the Minister of Education; for others comparable to Qiao, follow the Dongguan precedent and the written instruction of the xinwei order.
translations.idiomatic: Let the conference decree as before that Qiao take office, repeating the notice to the Palace Assistant Clerk and Minister of Education; anyone in Qiao’s situation shall follow Dongguan precedent and the xinwei directive.

sentences.zh: 」嶠不得已，乃拜。

translations.literal: ” Qiao had no alternative and therefore accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Left no choice, Wen Qiao accepted.

sentences.zh: 是時中原喪亂，室家離析，朝廷議二親陷沒寇難，應制服不。

translations.literal: At this time the Central Plains were torn by mourning and chaos and households were scattered; the court debated whether, when both parents had fallen into enemy hands, one ought to wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Amid devastation on the Central Plains and broken families, the court asked whether mourners should observe full rites when both parents were lost to invaders.

sentences.zh: 太常賀循曰：二親生離，吉凶未分，服喪則凶事未據，從吉則疑於不存，心憂居素，允當人情。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies He Xun said: “When both parents are separated alive and fortune or calamity is still undecided, putting on mourning means the ominous fact is not yet established; following auspicious life raises doubt about acting as if they were gone; anxious restraint in plain dress truly accords with human feeling.”
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonies He Xun said: “While parents are torn away with survival uncertain, adopting mourning assumes an unconfirmed death, yet casting off weeds suggests indifference to the living; subdued dress driven by anxiety matches human decency.”

sentences.zh: 」元帝令以循議為然。

translations.literal: ” Emperor Yuan ordered that He Xun’s opinion be deemed correct.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan endorsed He Xun’s view.

sentences.zh: ，司徒荀組云：「二親陷沒寇難，萬無一冀者，宜使依王法，隨例行喪。

translations.literal: , Minister of Education Xun Zu said: “When both parents have sunk into enemy hands and there is not one chance in ten thousand, they should be made to follow royal law and observe mourning according to ordinary precedent.”
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xun Zu argued: “When capture leaves virtually no hope of return, mourners should follow statute and keep mourning by routine procedure.”

sentences.zh: 」庾蔚之云：「二親為戎狄所破，存亡未可知者，宜盡尋求之理。

translations.literal: ” Yu Weizhi said: “When both parents have been broken by northern tribes and survival or death cannot yet be known, one ought to exhaust every principle of searching.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Weizhi said: “If barbarian raids engulf one’s parents and their fate is unknown, every effort must be made to seek them.”

sentences.zh: 尋求之理絕，三年之外，便宜婚宦，胤嗣不可絕，王政不可廢故也。

translations.literal: Once the principle of searching is exhausted, beyond three years it is then fitting to marry and take office, because heirs cannot be cut off and royal governance cannot be abandoned.”
translations.idiomatic: When every search fails, after three years marriage and office may resume—succession and administration cannot halt indefinitely.”

sentences.zh: 猶宜以哀素自居，不豫吉慶之事，待中壽而服之也。

translations.literal: Still one ought to conduct oneself in grieving plainness, not participate in auspicious celebrations, and wear mourning until middle age expectancy.”
translations.idiomatic: Even then one should remain in subdued mourning, avoid festivities, and keep mourning garments until roughly midlife expectancy.”

sentences.zh: 若境內賊亂清平，肆眚之後，尋覺無蹤跡者，便宜制服。」

translations.literal: If banditry within the borders is pacified and, after a general amnesty, searches discover no trace, it is then fitting to put on mourning garments.”
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm is calm after amnesty and inquiries find no trace of the missing, formal mourning may begin.”

sentences.zh: ，零陵李繁姊先適南平郡陳詵為妻，產四子而遭賊。

translations.literal: , Li Fan of Lingling—his elder sister had first married Chen Shen of Nanping commandery as wife and borne four sons when bandits struck.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan of Lingling: his sister had married Chen Shen of Nanping and borne four sons before raiders attacked.

sentences.zh: 姊投身于賊，請活姑命，賊略將姊去。

translations.literal: The elder sister threw herself upon the bandits, begging them to spare her mother-in-law’s life; the bandits dragged the elder sister away.
translations.idiomatic: She offered herself to the raiders to ransom her mother-in-law; they carried her off.

sentences.zh: 詵更娶嚴氏，生三子。

translations.literal: Shen married again, taking the Yan clan, and begot three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shen remarried Lady Yan and fathered three sons.

sentences.zh: 繁後得姊消息，往迎還詵，詵籍注領二妻。

translations.literal: Fan later obtained news of his elder sister, went to welcome her back to Shen; Shen’s registry recorded him as maintaining two wives.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan learned she lived and restored her to Chen Shen, the household register listed Shen with two wives.

sentences.zh: 及李亡，詵疑制服，以事言征西大將軍庾亮府平議，時議亦往往異同。

translations.literal: When Li died, Shen hesitated over mourning garments; he laid the matter before the headquarters of Grand General Who Campaigns West Yu Liang for adjudication, and opinions of the time often diverged.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Li died, Chen Shen was unsure how to mourn and referred the case to Yu Liang’s staff; contemporaries disagreed sharply.

sentences.zh: 司馬王愆期議曰：「案禮不二嫡，故惠西元妃孟子，孟子卒，繼室以聲子。

translations.literal: Major Wang Qianqi argued: “Examining the rites, there cannot be two chief wives; therefore Duke Hui of Lu’s primary consort was Mistress Meng—when Mistress Meng died, the successor chamber took Lady Shengzi.”
translations.idiomatic: Major Wang Qianqi cited canon: only one principal wife is allowed—Duke Hui’s chief consort was Mistress Meng; at her death Lady Shengzi entered as successor consort.”

sentences.zh: 諸侯猶爾，況庶人乎！

translations.literal: Feudal lords were still thus—how much more commoners!
translations.idiomatic: If feudal lords observed this, ordinary householders must all the more.

sentences.zh: 《士喪禮》曰，繼母本實繼室，故稱繼母，事之如嫡，故曰如母也。

translations.literal: The Rites for the Mourning of Gentlemen states that a stepmother was originally a successor consort, hence she is called stepmother; she is served like a chief wife, hence it says ‘like a mother.’”
translations.idiomatic: The Officer’s Mourning Canon explains that a stepmother is literally a successor consort—hence the title—and must be honored like a principal wife, which is why she ranks ‘as a mother.’”

sentences.zh: 詵不能遠慮避難，以亡其妻，非犯七出見絕於詵。

translations.literal: Shen could not plan far ahead to escape calamity and thereby lost his wife; she did not violate the seven grounds for divorce and was not cast off by Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shen failed to foresee disaster and lost his wife through no fault meeting the “seven outs.”

sentences.zh: 始不見絕，終又見迎，養姑于堂，子為首嫡，列名黃籍，則詵之妻也。

translations.literal: From the beginning she was not cast aside, and in the end she was welcomed back; she nourished her mother-in-law in the hall; her sons stood as chief heirs; her name was listed on the yellow register—she was Shen’s wife.
translations.idiomatic: Never divorced, welcomed home, caring for her mother-in-law, her sons legitimate heirs, her name on the rolls—she remained Chen Shen’s lawful wife.

sentences.zh: 為詵也妻，則為暉也母，暉之制服無所疑矣。

translations.literal: Being Shen’s wife, she was therefore Hui’s mother; there is no doubt about Hui wearing mourning for her.
translations.idiomatic: As Chen Shen’s wife she was unquestionably Hui’s mother; Hui owes her full mourning.

sentences.zh: 禮為繼母服而不為前母服者，如李比類，曠世所希。

translations.literal: That ritual provides mourning for a stepmother but not for a former mother applies to comparable cases like Li’s—rarities unseen for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Canon directs mourning for stepmothers but not birth mothers only in vanishingly rare cases such as Lady Li’s.

sentences.zh: 前母既終，乃有繼母，後子不及前母，故無制服之文。

translations.literal: When the former mother has already died and only then is there a stepmother, the later-born son never reaches the former mother; hence there is no text prescribing mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Usually the first wife dies before a successor arrives, so younger children never knew her—hence no mourning rule.

sentences.zh: 然礿祠蒸嘗，未有不以前母為母者，亡猶母之，況其存乎！

translations.literal: Yet in spring, autumn, winter, and summer sacrifices none fail to treat the former mother as mother; dead she is still honored as mother—how much more while alive!
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal offerings nonetheless treat the first wife as mother; we honor her dead—still more in life.

sentences.zh: 詵有老母，不可以莫之養，妻無歸期，納妾可也。

translations.literal: Shen had an aged mother and could not leave her unnourished; with the wife having no date of return, taking a concubine was permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shen had an elderly mother to support; with no news of his wife, a concubine was allowed.

sentences.zh: 李雖沒賊，尚有生冀，詵尋求之理不盡，而便娶妻，誠詵之短也。

translations.literal: Although Li was lost among bandits, there was still hope she lived; Shen had not exhausted every principle of searching when he married another wife—truly Shen’s shortcoming.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li might still live; Shen remarried without exhausting every search—that was his lapse.

sentences.zh: 然隴畝之夫，不達禮義，考之傳記不勝。

translations.literal: Yet the husband of ridge and furrow does not comprehend ritual propriety; examining transmitted records, instances are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Rustic men rarely grasp canonical etiquette; chronicles teem with such failures.

sentences.zh: 有施孝叔之妻失身于郤犨而不棄者，以非其罪也。

translations.literal: There is the case of Shi Xiaoshu’s wife, who lost her person to Xi Chou yet was not abandoned, because it was not her crime.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiaoshu’s wife was violated by Xi Chou yet retained because she was blameless.

sentences.zh: 詵有兩妻，非故犯法。

translations.literal: Shen had two wives—not intentionally violating the law.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shen’s dual marriage was not deliberate crime.

sentences.zh: 李鄙野人，而能臨危請活姑命，險不忘順，可謂孝婦矣。

translations.literal: Li was a rustic among rustics, yet facing peril she begged to spare her mother-in-law’s life—danger did not make her forget obedience; she may be called a filial wife.
translations.idiomatic: A humble woman, she faced mortal peril to save her mother-in-law—loyalty undimmed—a model of wifely devotion.

sentences.zh: 議者欲令在沒略之中，必全苦操，有隕無二，是望凡人皆為宋伯姬也。

translations.literal: Those debating wish to demand that in capture and plunder one must preserve bitter integrity unto death with no second spouse—they hope every mortal becomes Song Boji.
translations.idiomatic: Critics demand captives die chaste—effectively expecting every woman to be Song Boji.

sentences.zh: 詵雖不應娶妻，要以嚴為妻，妻則繼室，本非嫡也。

translations.literal: Although Shen ought not to have married a wife, once Yan was taken as wife she was successor consort and fundamentally not chief wife.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shen should not have remarried, yet Lady Yan entered as successor, not principal consort.

sentences.zh: 雖云非嫡，義在始終，寧可以詵不應二妻而己涉二庭乎！

translations.literal: Although it is said she was not chief wife, righteousness runs from beginning to end—how can Shen’s improper taking of two wives mean she herself straddles two households!
translations.idiomatic: Though not ranked principal, her bond endured—Chen Shen’s irregularity must not strand her between two domestic spheres.

sentences.zh: 若能下之，則趙姬之義。

translations.literal: If she can yield beneath another, that is the righteousness of Zhao Ji.
translations.idiomatic: If she can defer like Zhao Ji, she fulfills classical virtue.

sentences.zh: 若云不能，官當有制。

translations.literal: If one says she cannot, the authorities ought to impose regulation.
translations.idiomatic: If not, the state must legislate.

sentences.zh: 先嫡後繼，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Chief wife first and successor afterward—this has come down from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Principal wife precedes successor—that order is ancient.

sentences.zh: 眾議貶譏太峻，故略序異懷。

translations.literal: The crowd’s judgments demeaned and ridiculed too harshly; therefore I briefly set forth differing sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: Public censure was too harsh; hence this rehearsal of dissent.

sentences.zh: 」亮從愆期議定。

translations.literal: ” Liang followed Qianqi’s deliberation and settled the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang adopted Wang Qianqi’s ruling.

sentences.zh: 《五經通義》以為有德則諡善，無德則諡惡，故雖君臣可同。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics holds that those with virtue receive an auspicious posthumous title and those without virtue receive an inauspicious one; therefore even lord and minister may share the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Classics digest teaches that virtue earns a benign epithet and vice a harsh one—so ruler and subject may bear identical posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 魏朝初諡''『宣帝為文侯，景王為武侯』''，文王表不宜與二祖同，於是改諡宣文、忠武。

translations.literal: At first the Wei court posthumously titled ''『 Emperor Xuan as Marquis Wen and King Jing as Marquis Wu』''; King Wen memorialized that he ought not share identical titles with the two ancestors, whereupon the titles were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei dubbed Emperor Xuan “Marquis Wen” and King Jing “Marquis Wu”; King Wen petitioned against duplicate epithets with those forebears, prompting revisions to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 至文王受晉王之號，魏帝又追命宣文為宣王，忠武為景王。

translations.literal: When King Wen received the title Prince of Jin, the Wei emperor further posthumously promoted Xuanwen to King Xuan and Zhongwu to King Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Upon King Wen’s elevation as Prince of Jin, the Wei throne retroactively named Xuanwen King Xuan and Zhongwu King Jing.

sentences.zh: 十月，太常上諡故太常平陵男郭奕為景侯。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Grand Master of Ceremonies submitted a posthumous title for the former Grand Master of Ceremonies, Baron Guo Yi of Pingling, as Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: That tenth month the Director of Ceremonies proposed canonizing late Director Guo Yi, Baron of Pingling, as Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 有司奏云：「晉受命以來，祖宗號諡群下未有同者，故郭奕為景，與景皇同，不可聽，宜諡曰穆。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized: “Since Jin received the Mandate, among ancestors’ temple names and posthumous titles none below has duplicated them; therefore for Guo Yi to take Jing, identical with Emperor Jing, cannot be approved—one ought to posthumously title him Mu.”
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued that since Jin’s rise no minister has shared an imperial ancestor’s epithet—“Jing” duplicates Emperor Jing and must be refused; “Mu” fits better.”

sentences.zh: 」王濟、羊璞等並云：「夫無窮之祚，名諡不一，若皆相避，于制難全。

translations.literal: ” Wang Ji, Yang Pu, and others jointly said: “Now blessings without end produce names and posthumous titles beyond counting; if all mutually avoid one another, the regulation is hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji and Yang Pu replied: an eternal dynasty multiplies epithets; blanket avoidance would collapse the system.

sentences.zh: 如悉不避，復非推崇事尊之禮。

translations.literal: If one altogether fails to avoid, that again is not the ritual of elevating and serving the revered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ignoring taboo entirely would dishonor superiors.”

sentences.zh: 宜依諱名之義，但及七廟祖宗而已，不及遷毀之廟。

translations.literal: One ought to follow the meaning of tabooing personal names—only reaching the ancestors of the seven temples—and not reaching temples moved aside or dismantled.”
translations.idiomatic: Apply name taboo only to the Seven Shrines’ forebears, not to collateral halls already retired.”

sentences.zh: 」成粲、武茂、劉訥並云：「同諡非嫌。

translations.literal: ” Cheng Can, Wu Mao, and Liu Ne jointly said: “Sharing a posthumous title is no offense.”
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Can, Wu Mao, and Liu Ne insisted duplicate epithets are permissible.”

sentences.zh: 號諡者，國之大典，所以厲時作教，經天人之遠旨也。

translations.literal: Temple names and posthumous titles are the great canon of the state; they are the means to sharpen the age and establish teaching—they weave together the far aims of Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous naming is foundational policy for moral instruction and aligning human conduct with cosmic order.”

sentences.zh: 固雖君父，義有所不隆，及在臣子，或以行顯。

translations.literal: Therefore although they are lord and father, righteousness has what must not be excessively elevated; extending to ministers and sons, some shine forth through conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Even sovereigns and fathers merit bounded praise; subjects may earn distinction by deeds.”

sentences.zh: 故能使上下邁德，罔有怠荒。

translations.literal: Hence they can make high and low stride in virtue so that none grow slack or wasteful.
translations.idiomatic: Thus elite and common strive after virtue without slack.”

sentences.zh: 臣願聖世同符堯舜，行周同諡之禮，舍漢魏近制相避之議。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes the sagely age to tally with Yao and Shun, enacting Zhou’s ritual of identical posthumous titles and discarding Han-Wei-style debates about mutual avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: We pray this reign emulate Yao and Shun by reviving Zhou’s shared epithets rather than Han-Wei avoidance.”

sentences.zh: 」又引周公父子同諡曰文。

translations.literal: ” They further cited Duke Zhou and his son sharing the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: They noted the Duke of Zhou and his heir both titled “Wen.”

sentences.zh: 武帝詔曰：「非言君臣不可同，正以奕諡景不相當耳，宜諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu edicted: “It is not said that lord and minister cannot share—precisely because Yi’s posthumous title Jing is unsuitable; one ought to posthumously title him Jian.”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu clarified: shared ruler-subject epithets are not barred—“Jing” simply ill suits Guo Yi; grant “Jian.”

sentences.zh: 」及，侍中王欣之表君臣之嫌同諡，尚書奏以欣之言為然。

translations.literal: ” Later, Palace Attendant Wang Xin memorialized suspicion between lord and minister when sharing posthumous titles; the Secretariat memorialized that Xin’s words were correct.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Wang Xin later argued duplicate titles blurred hierarchy; the Secretariat agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne concurred.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍溫嶠前妻李氏，在嶠微時便卒。

translations.literal: General Who Inspires Might Wen Qiao’s former wife, Lady Li, died while Qiao was still humble.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li, Wen Qiao’s first wife, died before he rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 又娶王氏、何氏，並在嶠前死。

translations.literal: He married again the Wang and He clans, both dying before Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He later wed Ladies Wang and He, both predeceasing him.

sentences.zh: 及嶠薨，朝廷以問陳舒：「三人並得為夫人不？

translations.literal: When Qiao died, the court consulted Chen Shu: “Can all three together be ladies?”
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Qiao died the court asked Chen Shu whether all three wives could rank as primary ladies.”

sentences.zh: 」舒云：「《禮記》『其妻為夫人而卒，而後其夫不為大夫，而祔于其妻，則不易牲。

translations.literal: ” Shu said: “The Book of Rites states: ‘When his wife died as a lady and afterward her husband did not become a grand officer yet appended sacrifice to her, then he does not change the victim.’”
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shu quoted the Book of Rites on sacrifices when rank shifts after a wife’s death.”

sentences.zh: 妻卒。

translations.literal: The wife dies.
translations.idiomatic: If the wife dies first,

sentences.zh: 而後夫為大夫，而祔于其妻，則以大夫牲』。

translations.literal: and afterward the husband becomes a grand officer and appends sacrifice to her, then he uses the grand officer victim.’”
translations.idiomatic: but the husband later attains grand officer rank and continues her cult, he employs the grand officer victim.”

sentences.zh: 然則夫榮于朝，妻貴于室，雖先夫沒，榮辱常隨於夫也。

translations.literal: Thus when the husband is glorious at court the wife is noble in the chamber; although she perished before him, glory and shame always follow the husband.
translations.idiomatic: Court honors lift the wife at home; even dying first, her standing tracks his fortunes.”

sentences.zh: 《禮記》曰『妻祔于祖姑，祖姑有三人，則祔其親者』。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: ‘The wife is appended to grandmother-aunts; when there are three grandmother-aunts, append her to the nearest generation.’”
translations.idiomatic: The canon directs appending a wife to the closest ancestress when multiple generations receive cult.”

sentences.zh: 如禮，則三人皆為夫人也。

translations.literal: According to ritual, then all three were ladies.
translations.idiomatic: By that reading all three count as ladies.”

sentences.zh: 自秦漢已來，廢一娶九女之制，近世無復繼室之禮，先妻卒則更娶。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han onward the regulation of one marriage with nine wives was abolished; recent generations no longer observe successor-consort ritual—when the former wife dies one marries again.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin-Han ended polygamous quotas and later ages dropped formal succession nuptials, men simply remarry after a first wife’s death.”

sentences.zh: 苟生加禮，則亡不應貶。

translations.literal: If while alive ritual honors were added, then in death they ought not be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Distinctions granted in life must not be stripped posthumously.”

sentences.zh: 」庾蔚之云：「賤時之妻不得並為夫人，若有追贈之命則不論耳。

translations.literal: ” Yu Weizhi said: “Wives taken in low station cannot jointly be ladies unless posthumous enfeoffment orders say otherwise.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Weizhi countered that wives from humble beginnings cannot share lady rank without later patents.”

sentences.zh: 」《嶠傳》，贈王、何二人夫人印綬，不及李氏。

translations.literal: ” In Wen Qiao’s biography, Wang and He were granted ladies’ seals and cords; Lady Li was not reached.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao’s biography records posthumous seals for Ladies Wang and He but not Lady Li.”

sentences.zh: ，彭城國為李太妃求諡。

translations.literal: , the Pengcheng princely estate sought a posthumous title for Grand Consort Li.
translations.idiomatic: The Pengcheng domain petitioned an epithet for Grand Consort Li.

sentences.zh: 博士曹耽之議：「夫婦行不必同，不得以夫諡諡婦。

translations.literal: Erudite Cao Dan argued: “Husband and wife need not share identical conduct; one cannot apply the husband’s posthumous title to the wife.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Cao Dan held spouses’ virtues need not match and the husband’s epithet cannot be stamped on the wife.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》婦人有諡甚多，經無譏文，知禮得諡也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals give many ladies posthumous titles; the classic carries no text of reproof—thus ritual allows posthumous titles.”
translations.idiomatic: The Annals honor many women without censure—so epithets are licit.”

sentences.zh: 」胡訥云：「禮，婦人生以夫爵，死以夫諡。

translations.literal: ” Hu Ne said: “By ritual a woman’s living rank follows her husband’s title; her death title follows his posthumous name.”
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ne cited canon tying a woman’s rank and epithet to her husband.”

sentences.zh: 《春秋》夫人有諡，不復依禮耳。

translations.literal: That Spring and Autumn ladies have posthumous titles simply means they no longer followed ritual.”
translations.idiomatic: Women’s epithets in the Annals already departed classical norms.”

sentences.zh: 安平獻王李妃、琅邪武王諸葛妃，太傅東海王裴妃並無諡，今宜率舊典。

translations.literal: Consort Li of Prince Xian of Anping, Consort Zhuge of Prince Wu of Langye, and Consort Pei of the Grand Tutor Prince of the Eastern Sea all lacked posthumous titles; now one ought to follow the old canon.”
translations.idiomatic: Major consorts of several princes lacked epithets; precedent favors restraint.”

sentences.zh: 」王彪之云：「婦人有諡，禮壞故耳。

translations.literal: ” Wang Biaozhi said: “When ladies receive posthumous titles, ritual is broken—that is all.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi argued women’s epithets signal collapsed ritual.”

sentences.zh: 聲子為諡，服虔諸儒以為非。

translations.literal: That Lady Shengzi received a posthumous title—Fu Qian and various scholars deemed it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian and others condemned Lady Shengzi’s epithet.”

sentences.zh: 杜預亦云『禮，婦人無諡』。

translations.literal: Du Yu also said: ‘By ritual women have no posthumous title.’”
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu echoed: canonical women receive no posthumous names.”

sentences.zh: 《春秋》無譏之文，所謂不待貶絕自明者也。

translations.literal: That Spring and Autumn carries no text of reproof is what is meant by needing no explicit demotion—the matter clarifies itself.
translations.idiomatic: Annalistic silence means no added censure is required—the breach is obvious.”

sentences.zh: 近世惟后乃有諡耳。」

translations.literal: In recent generations only empresses receive posthumous titles.”
translations.idiomatic: Only empresses lately merit epithets.”

sentences.zh: 太尉荀顗上諡法云：「若賜諡而道遠不及葬者，皆封策下屬，遣所承長吏奉策即塚祭賜諡。」

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yu Yi submitted rules on posthumous titles: “If a posthumous title is granted but the road is too distant to reach burial in time, all should seal the patent and dispatch it downward; send the inherited chief clerk to carry the patent to the mound, sacrifice, and bestow the posthumous title.”
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yu Yi proposed: when honors cannot reach a distant burial, sealed edicts should go to local magistrates for tombside sacrifice and investiture.

sentences.zh: ，召孔安國為侍中。

translations.literal: , Kong Anguo was summoned as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo was called to serve as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 安國表以黃門郎王愉名犯私諱，不得連署，求解。

translations.literal: Anguo memorialized that Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Yu’s name violated private taboo, preventing joint signatures; he sought relief.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo cited taboo clash with Wang Yu’s name blocking cosignature and asked to step down.

sentences.zh: 有司議云：「名終諱之，有心所同，聞名心瞿，亦明前誥。

translations.literal: The offices deliberated: “One taboos a name to the end—this shares every heart; hearing the name startles the heart—the earlier instruction also made this clear.
translations.idiomatic: Officials noted universal reverence for parental names and earlier edicts affirming the shock of hearing them.

sentences.zh: 而《禮》復云『君所無私諱，大夫之所有公諱』，無私諱。

translations.literal: Yet the Rites further says: ‘At the ruler’s court there is no private taboo; what grand officers have is public taboo’—no private taboo.”
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Rites bar private taboos before the sovereign—public ritual prevails.”

sentences.zh: 又云『詩書不諱，臨文不諱』。

translations.literal: It also says: ‘The Poetry and Documents are not tabooed; facing documents one does not taboo.’”
translations.idiomatic: Canonical texts and formal paperwork likewise waive taboo.”

sentences.zh: 豈非公義奪私情，王制屈家禮哉！

translations.literal: How is this not public righteousness wresting private feeling—kingly regulation bending household ritual!
translations.idiomatic: Thus state duty tempers private grief—dynastic law supersedes domestic etiquette.”

sentences.zh: 尚書安眾男臣先表中兵曹郎王祐名犯父諱，求解職，明詔爰發，聽許換曹，蓋是恩出制外耳。

translations.literal: Minister Anyzhong Baron earlier memorialized that Central Troops Bureau Gentleman Wang You’s name violated his father’s taboo and sought to resign office; a clear edict issued allowing transfer of bureau—that favor emerged outside ordinary regulation.”
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Anyzhong won Wang You a bureau transfer for taboo, that grace exceeded normal statute.”

sentences.zh: 而頃者互相瞻式，源流既啟，莫知其極。

translations.literal: Yet recently they mutually gaze upon precedent; once source and flow were opened, none knows its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Officials now mimic one another until the practice balloons without bound.

sentences.zh: 夫皇朝禮大，百僚備職，編官列署，動相經涉。

translations.literal: Now the imperial court’s ritual is vast—hundred officials fill posts; offices and bureaus are arrayed; movement constantly intersects and passes through.
translations.idiomatic: Our court staffs myriad offices whose jurisdictions constantly intersect.

sentences.zh: 若以私諱，人遂其心，則移官易職，遷流莫已，既違典法，有虧政體。

translations.literal: If by private taboo each person follows his heart, then shifting office and changing posts would revolve without end—already violating canon and harming the body politic.
translations.idiomatic: Letting every taboo whim reshuffle posts would violate law and cripple government.

sentences.zh: 請一斷之。

translations.literal: We request one decisive cut.
translations.idiomatic: We urge a single definitive ruling.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.
